Microsoft Teams Help Guide

Microsoft’s official help for Teams on Windows, the web and iPhone, gathered into one screen-reader-friendly document

2026-07-31

Microsoft Teams Help Guide

This guide gathers the official help Microsoft publishes for Microsoft Teams, taken from support.microsoft.com on 30 July 2026. The words are Microsoft’s; nothing has been summarised or rewritten.

Teams runs as a Windows program, in a web browser, and as an app for iPhone and iPad. All three are covered, usually within the same article, since Microsoft writes one article and marks the steps that differ. There is no Alexa skill.

The sections are Microsoft’s own: the parts of its own address for each article — chat, meetings, calls and devices, teams and channels, and the rest — in alphabetical order, with Miscellaneous last for the few pages Microsoft files outside any of them.

Administrator material and the developer documentation on learn.microsoft.com were left out, as this collection leaves out both everywhere. What remains is written for the person using Teams rather than the person running it for an organisation.

This is the second edition, and it is now the whole estate. The first gathering run stopped when it reached its own page limit with 112 addresses still waiting, so the first edition said plainly that it was short. A second run with the limit raised finished on its own, eleven passes with nothing left in the queue. The two runs have been put together and the result is 434 articles — only three more than the first edition had, which says the addresses left waiting were nearly all repeats of pages already gathered.

That second run also set aside 30 addresses that served a page already saved under another name rather than their own content. Where the first run had caught those pages properly, its copies are the ones used here. Microsoft’s articles carry a good deal of furniture: a rating strip, a subscription pitch, and a “Need more help” block. All of it has been removed. Illustrations do not survive as pictures; where one carried a description it is kept as a short italic note.

Headings run six deep at most. Level one is this title, level two is a section, level three is an article, and anything below that came from inside the article itself.

Apps and services

Add a OneNote notebook in Microsoft Teams

To add a new or existing OneNote notebook to a channel in Microsoft Teams, select Add a tabScreenshot: Add button at the top of the channel and select OneNote.

From there, choose an option:

  • To start from scratch, select Create a new notebook, add a name to the Notebook name field, and click Save.
  • To add an existing notebook, select Browse notebooks, choose the notebook and section, and select Save.
  • To add a link to an existing notebook, select Paste a OneNote link, add the address, and select Save.

Once you add the OneNote tab, everyone in the channel can view and make edits (provided they have access to the notebook). Anyone blocked from viewing the notebook can request access right from the tab.

To access OneNote notes outside of Teams:

  1. Select OneNoteScreenshot: OneNote icon in Teams. If you don’t see OneNote, select AppsScreenshot: Add an app or tab button and search for it.

  2. In OneNote, hover over a notebook and select More optionsScreenshot: Generic Ellipsis button .

    1. Select OpenScreenshot: View town hall insights icon to open it in OneNote for the web.
    2. Hover over the side arrow Screenshot: Expand icon next to OpenScreenshot: View town hall insights icon to expand more options and select Open in desktopScreenshot: OneNote icon to open it in the OneNote desktop app.

Add a workflow from a shared file in Microsoft Teams

Note

Adding a workflow from a shared file is part of the public preview program and might undergo further changes before being released publicly. To get access to this and other upcoming features, switch to Teams public preview.

You can add and run workflows directly from shared files in a chat or channel.

Screenshot: Screenshot showing the workflow menu open from a shared file

  1. Go to More attachment optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon in the bottom right corner of the shared file.
  2. Select Workflows.
  3. Choose from the list of instant workflows that can be done on the file, or select See all workflows.
  4. Choose between instant workflows that are already set up for files or browse templates.

Add or run a workflow from a message

Add an app to Microsoft Teams

You can add apps to Microsoft Teams in either the web, desktop, or mobile versions. You can also add apps from anywhere you’re working in Teams, whether you’re in a chat, channel, or meeting.

Add from Apps

  1. Select AppsScreenshot: teams-add-an-app-or-tab-button-icon in Teams. Search for your favorite app or browse categories to discover new ones. Screenshot: Screenshot of the app store with browsable apps.
  2. Select the app you want, and a description screen opens. The app overview, reviews, and details explain what the app does and where it appears in Teams. Screenshot: Screenshot showing the window that opens when you select an app.
  3. To add the app, select Add.

Add an app to a chat or channel tab

You can add apps to a tab to share content and work collaboratively.

  1. Select a team channel or chat in Teams.
  2. Select Add a tabScreenshot: Add an app or tab button .
  3. Select the app you want.
  4. Select Add.
  5. Return to the app and select whether to Post about this tab in the chat or channel.
  6. Select Save.

Note

Team owners can restrict who can add apps. Some apps can only be installed by a team owner because they require additional permissions.

Add an app to a meeting

Meeting organizers and presenters can add apps before or during meetings.

  • To add an app before a meeting, first send the meeting invite then open the meeting. Select Add a tabScreenshot: Add an app or tab button and choose an app.

  • To add an app during a meeting, after the meeting starts select AppsScreenshot: Add an app or tab button in the meeting controls.

Tip

For more details, see Use apps in Teams meetings.

Add an app from the messaging area

Some apps let you insert the app directly into Teams messages.

  • To add an app to a message, select Actions and appsScreenshot: Plus sign icon and choose the app you want to use.

Add a personal app

Some apps have a personal app capability, letting you use them outside of a channel or chat but still within Teams.

For example, OneNote gives you a private workspace within Teams, while Planner and Wrike offer a bird’s eye view of all your tasks, across boards that you or your team have added as channel tabs.

  1. Select AppsScreenshot: Add an app or tab button in Teams.
  2. Search or browse apps with Personal app listed as a capability.
  3. Select the app.
  4. Select Add.

Find Teams apps

Add or run a workflow in chats, chat messages, channels, and channel posts in Microsoft Teams

You can add or run workflows from the messaging area in Microsoft Teams. Many workflows let you create and insert rich content into a new message or post. Others let you do things like schedule a message or post to be sent later. What all workflows have in common is they let you customize the messaging experience to be more useful to you and your team.

Add a new workflow

  1. Do one of the following:

    • Next to the chat or channel you want to add to the workflow, select More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > Workflows.
    • In a chat message or channel post, select Actions and appsScreenshot: Actions and apps button > Workflows.

  2. In the Workflows dialog box, select the workflow you want.

    • Search for a pre-installed workflow or a pre-built workflow.
    • Choose a workflow from the suggested workflows.

  3. Select a descriptive name for the workflow or use the suggested name.

  4. Ensure that you are signed in to any required apps. Select Next.

  5. Fill in the details for the workflow. Detail items might include things like email addresses or Planner groups.

  6. Select Submit.

Or

  • Select Workflow builder to use AI to describe and create a custom workflow. Learn how at Create a workflow automatically.

Note

If Workflows isn’t in the menu, find it under Chats > More options > Manage apps or in a chat message under Actions and appsScreenshot: Actions and apps button > Search for apps.

Run an existing workflow from a chat, channel, or chat message

  1. On the right side of the message compost box, select Actions and appsScreenshot: Actions and apps button > Workflows.

  2. Select the workflow you’d like to run.

  3. Follow any prompts you’re given.

Note

Connectors for a channel can now be found in the Manage channel section of Settings.

Chat with an app in Microsoft Teams

Whether answering questions or taking care of mundane tasks, Teams apps save you and others time to focus on what’s most important.

Tip

Not sure what to say to an app? Keep in mind each app has a set of commands it understands and responds to. You can see these commands when you start typing a message to an app.

Add an app

To add an app in Teams:

  • Select AppsScreenshot: teams-add-an-app-or-tab-button-icon on the left side of Teams. Search for your favorite app or browse the app categories to find new ones.
  • In a channel or group chat, select Actions and appsScreenshot: plus-icon-teams in the compose box to search and find apps.

Note

If you’re a team owner, you can add apps that receive and send messages in conversations without being @mentioned. Before you add this type of app, make sure you understand the permissions it’s requesting.

Chat with an app in a chat

Apps can contribute to chat conversations, providing important updates or helping teams organize their work.

Typically, you or someone else @mentions an app to interact with it, but some apps can play a more proactive role in conversations. These apps receive messages and respond without an @mention. (Whoever adds this kind of app—whether it’s you or another member—must consent to the required app permissions on for the conversation.)

To chat with an app in a chat:

  1. Type **@** and the app’s name in the text box.
  2. Chat with the app and use it to assign tasks, reminders, or whatever task the app assists with.

Copy a team member’s workflow in Microsoft Teams

If you do the same task over and over again in Teams, chances are other people do too. If you use a template to create a workflow, it’s easy for other people to copy that workflow for their own use.

Note

If you’ve edited the template, people can’t copy it.

Create a poll in Microsoft Teams

  • Desktop
  • Mobile

Polls let you get helpful feedback on questions by making a real-time poll right in a chat or channel in Teams.

Create a poll

  1. To create a poll, select Actions and appsScreenshot: Actions and apps button on the right side of Compose box where you type your message. If Polls isn’t in the menu, select Find more apps or select Apps on the left side of Teams.
  2. Enter your question followed by at least two choices for answers. Polls suggests some responses, which you can choose, or type your own in the Option boxes. Select Screenshot: Actions and apps buttonOptions to add more answers.
  3. Turn on Multiple selections to allow users to choose more than one answer.
  4. Optionally, select Record names of respondents. Only you see the responses.
  5. If you want, select Share aggregated results with respondents.
  6. When you’re done, select Preview to review your poll. Select Edit to make updates or select Send to publish your poll to the message or post.

Responding to a poll

  • To respond to a poll, people choose an option on the poll card and select Submit Vote. As they vote, you’ll see updates to the response summary on the poll card.

View and organize poll results

To view results and other poll details:

  • If you created the poll, you can view the results by selecting More in the poll card. The Responses Overview page in Microsoft Forms shows the following details:

    • Whether the poll is active or inactive.
    • The number of poll responses.
    • The average time people spent in the poll.
    • The duration or length of time the poll is available to respondents.
    • The number of responses for each answer.
    • If you selected to record participant names, select More details to see the name and answer of each participant.

To organize poll results:

  • To view results in a spreadsheet, select Open results in Excel.
  • To see results for each participant, select Check individual results.
  • To delete results, print a results summary, or share a link to poll results, select More options for responsesScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon . Learn more about viewing and sharing poll results Check and share your form results.

Manage a poll

  1. Select More on the poll card to open the result view.
  2. In the upper-left corner, select Back to questions.
  3. Select SettingsScreenshot: Settings button . Specify who can fill out the form, the types of responses, and whether you’re notified of each response.

Microsoft Teams Third Party Notice and Terms of Use for Poll/Survey/Checklist

Get constructive feedback on questions by creating a real-time poll right from a chat or channel with the Poll app for Teams.

Create a poll

  1. To create a poll, tap Menu (…) below the box where you type your messages in Teams and select the Poll app. If the app isn’t in the list, then install it through your desktop or browser.
  2. Enter your poll question in the Poll app followed by at least two choices for answers. You can add as many as 10 choices to a poll.
  3. Set a due date for the poll and restrict who can see poll results in Settings.
  4. Tap Next to preview and Send to publish your poll.

To respond to a poll, choose an option and tap Submit Vote. As people in your group or channel vote, you will see updates to the response summary.

View your poll result

To see the results of your poll, tap View Result.

Participation Summary shows the response list along with the participants’ choices. The list of people who didn’t vote on the poll is in the adjacent tab. Tap Back to return to the result summary view.

Manage a poll

Note

This is available only to the person who created the poll.

  1. Tap View Result on the poll card to open the result view.
  2. Tap Menu (…) at the top right corner of the result view.
  3. Tap Confirm in the pop up to continue with your selection.

Create a workflow automatically in Microsoft Teams

Create a workflow automatically by describing what you want to do. The Workflow builder uses Open AI Codex to suggest a flow that matches what you are trying to do.

Create a workflow automatically

  1. Hover over the chat or channel you want to add a workflow to and select More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > Workflows.

    Or

    From a sent message, select More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > More actions > Create new action.

    Or

    In the compose box, select Actions and appsScreenshot: Actions and apps button > Workflows > Create new action.

  2. Select Workflow builder.

  3. Write a description of the tasks you want to automate. For example, “I want to send an email to the managers when the team finishes a sprint.”

  4. Workflow builder suggests a flow, including the apps, triggers, and actions you need. If you like the suggested workflow, select Next.

  5. Sign in to any apps and enter any information the flow requires. Select Create flow.

  6. To add a new step to the flow, select New step. Add the apps, triggers, or actions for the step. The Flow checker validates the step and highlights any errors.

  7. To delete a step, select MenuScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > Delete next to the step.

  8. Select Done.

Workflow Builder provides several options for creating a flow automatically:

  • Select one of the three examples Workflow builder shows when you open the tool. To see additional flows, choose View more examples. Selecting this link presents three new examples that appear each time you select the link. Select Next.
  • To see a different version of the flow you’ve described, select Show a different suggestion. Select Next.
  • If the suggestions don’t correspond to your description or you prefer to build your own workflow, select This isn’t what I’m looking for. You can choose a blank flow or custom templates. Selecting this option helps Microsoft improve the AI behind automatic workflow builder.

Create a workflow from an emoji reaction in Microsoft Teams

Emoji reactions can be used as workflow triggers in Teams chats and channels. This helps your team move faster, cut down on manual steps, and stay on top of important tasks. When you or your colleagues reply to a chat or channel message with a specific emoji, a workflow process will be triggered automatically.

For example:

  • React with❗️to create a helpdesk ticket and escalate an issue.
  • Use 👀 to send a message to the right channel for visibility.

There are a few ways to set up workflows from emoji reactions:

Use a template

  1. On the left side of Teams, select AppsScreenshot: teams-add-an-app-or-tab-button-icon > WorkflowsScreenshot: workflow-logo .

  2. From the Create tab, use the search bar to find workflow templates. Try searching “emoji” to find all templates that use emoji as triggers.

  3. Select a template.

  4. Follow the steps for the template to customize it. These can include:

    • Naming your flow.
    • Choosing which emoji you want to use.
    • Choosing your reaction frequency (do you want the workflow to be triggered on every reaction or just the first one?).
    • Choosing who can trigger the workflow (everyone, including guests and people outside your org, or just yourself?)

  5. Select the group chat(s) or channel(s) where you want the workflow to apply.

  6. Select Create flow.

Tip

For an emoji reaction to trigger a workflow in both a group chat and a channel, set up separate workflows for each.

Create a workflow from scratch

  1. On the left side of Teams, select AppsScreenshot: teams-add-an-app-or-tab-button-icon > WorkflowsScreenshot: workflow-logo .
  2. Select +New flow > + Create from blank.
  3. Search for When someone reacted to a message in chat.
  4. Fill out the fields to customize your workflow. You can specify chat or channel under Message type.
  5. Select + New step to add the action you want the emoji reaction to trigger and fill out the required fields.
  6. Select Save.

To learn more about advanced settings and limitations of the trigger, see When someone reacted to a message in chat.

Get started with Teams Walkie Talkie

Welcome to Walkie Talkie, the Teams app that makes your work phone a simple and safe way to talk to people on the go. It uses push-to-talk (PTT) technology.

Screenshot: Your browser does not support video. Install Microsoft Silverlight, Adobe Flash Player, or Internet Explorer 9.

In this article

Overview

Open Walkie Talkie

Pin the Walkie Talkie app for quick access

Connect to a channel

See who is connected to a channel

Walkie Talkie devices

Settings

Overview

You may already use a walkie talkie-like device at work to coordinate with coworkers, ask for immediate assistance, contact security, and so on. Like traditional walkie talkies, you press and hold a button to speak on Teams Walkie Talkie and release the button to listen.

Unlike regular walkie talkies, Teams Walkie Talkie is on your phone and works with your Teams environment.

Screenshot: Walkie Talkie screen, showing pinned channels and Talk button when user is speaking.

Note

You need to press Stop listening to stop receiving transmissions.

Open Walkie Talkie

If you’re using Walkie Talkie for the first time in Teams, you’ll see a red dot notification on the Walkie Talkie icon in the Teams app bar.

Screenshot: The Walkie Talkie icon showing the red dot notification

To open Walkie Talkie, tap Walkie Talkie in the Teams app bar.

Screenshot: The Walkie Talkie icon in the Teams app bar

If you don’t see the Walkie Talkie app when you open Teams, swipe up from the bottom of your screen or tap MoreScreenshot: More options button to access it.

Pin Walkie Talkie for quick access

If Walkie Talkie isn’t already pinned to the app bar in Teams, here’s how to do it.

  1. In Teams, swipe up on from the app bar and tap Edit.
  2. In Edit navigation, drag Walkie Talkie from More Apps to the top section.

Note

The number of apps you can have in the app bar is limited. You may need to remove other apps before you can pin Walkie Talkie.

Connect to a channel

You can connect to and talk on only one channel at a time in Walkie Talkie.

Note

  • Walkie Talkie doesn’t support shared channels.
  • To connect to a channel and use Walkie Talkie on iOS devices, Walkie Talkie must be the only PTT app that’s running on your phone. Before you use Walkie Talkie, close any other PTT apps. If the other PTT app is running in the background, tap the Leave button to quit it.
  • On iOS devices, Walkie Talkie can be set up for use from the lock screen when it’s the only PTT app running in the background.

You can choose one channel to connect to or select up to five favorite channels. Your favorite channels are pinned at the top of the Walkie Talkie screen in alphabetical order. This makes it easy to change channels.

  1. Tap Select channels. Screenshot: Walkie Talkie screen, showing suggested channels and Select channels button.

  2. Select up to five channels. If you select more than one channel, and you want to hear activity on all your selected channels, turn on the Listen to multiple channels toggle.

    Screenshot: The Select channels screen in Walkie Talkie.

  3. If you selected one channel, you’re automatically connected to that channel. The channel name appears next to > and the team name is under that.

    Screenshot: Walkie Talkie screen, showing one selected channel.If you selected more than one channel, you’re automatically connected to the first channel in your list of pinned channels.

    The channel name next to > shows your active channel. It’s also highlighted in your pinned channel list. You’ll see the team name under that. The active channel is the channel you speak on.

    Screenshot: Walkie Talkie, showing pinned channels and the active channel To speak on a different channel, tap a pinned channel to switch to it. The channel name next to > changes to show it’s your active channel. You’ll see it in your list of pinned channels.

    Note

    Walkie Talkie remembers the last channel you connected to. It automatically chooses and connects you to that channel the next time you open Walkie Talkie.

    Learn more about how to communicate with your team on Walkie Talkie.

See who’s connected to a channel

The number next to Screenshot: Participants icon indicates how many people are currently connected to the channel, including yourself. Tap Screenshot: Participants icon to see who’s connected.

Screenshot: The people icon in Walkie Talkie, indicating the number people connected to the channel

Walkie Talkie devices and headsets

You can use Walkie Talkie with special devices and headsets that have a PTT button. You can also use wired headsets that have a play/pause or answer/end call button.

Press the PTT button or tap the play/pause or answer/end call button to instantly talk to your team members on your connected channel.

With these devices and headsets, you can communicate on a channel even when your phone is locked. For a list of these devices and headsets, see Walkie Talkie devices and accessories.

If you’re using a wired headset with Walkie Talkie, see Set up and use a wired headset with Walkie Talkie.

Settings

To change Walkie Talkie settings, select your profile picture, go to Settings > Walkie Talkie.

Screenshot: Walkie Talkie settings

The settings you choose will apply across all the devices on which you use Walkie Talkie.

Audio
  • To mute the alert sounds when you send and receive transmissions, turn on the Noise suppression toggle.
  • Turn on or turn off Acoustic Echo Cancellation.
Alert style
  • Turn on or turn off the Beeps toggle, depending on whether you want to hear beep alerts.
  • Turn on or turn off the Vibrate toggle, depending on whether you want your phone to vibrate when you send transmissions.
Transmission mode

If you’re using a wired headset, tap Wired Headset to view or change your transmission mode settings. You can set your transmission length when in Toggle-to-Talk mode, or test your headset to determine transmission mode. To learn more, see Set up and use a wired headset with Walkie Talkie.

Screenshot: Walkie Talkie Toggle To Talk mode settings

Connection

Turn off the Auto connect toggle if you don’t want to automatically connect to channels. By default, this setting is on.

Network

Select Test Network Quality to check your network connection.

Screenshot: The Test Network Quality screen in Walkie Talkie

Overview of workflows in Microsoft Teams

Workflows let you automate repetitive tasks or processes that connect one or more apps to Teams. In short, they can save you time and effort. Here, we’ll walk you through how to add, run, and manage your workflows.

How can workflows help you?

Take a moment to ask yourself the following questions. Every time you answer “yes,” there’s an opportunity to increase your productivity with a workflow.

  • Is there something you do over and over again in Teams?
  • Do you switch between Teams and other apps to check for updates or complete tasks?
  • Do you ever copy and paste info from Teams into other apps?
  • Are you getting app notifications in email that you’d rather get in Teams?
  • Do you ask people the same questions on a regular basis, whether in a channel, chat, or meeting? (For example, can you post your weekly status update?)

Find and add workflows

The easiest way to get started is to browse the collection of pre-built workflows.

  1. Select AppsScreenshot: teams-add-an-app-or-tab-button-icon in Teams.
  2. Select WorkflowsScreenshot: Workflow logo from the navigation on the left.
  3. Select a workflow that interests you.
  4. Follow the prompts given.

When done, you’ll get a confirmation saying, “Workflow added successfully!” The confirmation also includes instructions for running your workflow.

Note

The Workflows app, which runs workflows in Teams, is installed by default. If you can’t find the app, it might be uninstalled. Find the Workflows app in the app store and select Add. The setup screen for the workflow you selected then appears.

How workflows run in Teams

After you’ve added a workflow, you’ll get instructions on how to run it. Workflows run in a few different ways:

Automatic. An automatic workflow doesn’t need you to do anything after you add it. Each workflow has a trigger, and when the trigger occurs, an action or series of actions happen automatically. Here are two examples:

  • Notify a channel when a Planner task changes status
    • Trigger: A Planner task on a board (specified when you set up the workflow) changes status.
    • Actions: A card is automatically posted to a channel (specified when you set up the workflow), notifying your team of the status change.
  • Start an approval when a SharePoint list is modified
    • Trigger: A SharePoint list (specified when you set up the workflow) is modified.
    • Actions: An approval is automatically sent in Teams chat to the right people.

Conditional. Some workflows are designed to act on the content of a single Teams message. After you set up this type of workflow, it appears under More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon . You can run it from any message. Read step-by-step instructions.

Editable. These types of workflows let you change how a message is sent or insert content into a new message. Read step-by-step instructions.

Manage workflows

View when your workflows have run and change connections or delete them in the workflow management tool.

  1. Select AppsScreenshot: teams-add-an-app-or-tab-button-icon in Teams.

  2. Go to WorkflowsScreenshot: Workflow logo .

  3. Select Manage WorkflowsScreenshot: skype-teams-mobile-icon-settings .

Screenshot: manage-workflows

Tip

Another way to open Workflows is from View moreScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon apps on the left side of Teams.

Unpin an app from the left side of Teams

Right-click an app icon and select UnpinScreenshot: teams-chat-unpin-icon .

Pin an app in a channel or chat

  1. Open a chat.
  2. At the top of the channel or chat, select Add a tabScreenshot: teams-add-an-app-or-tab-button-icon .
  3. Select an app to add it.

Remove an app from a channel or chat

  1. Select the app tab you want to remove.
  2. Select the dropdown arrow next to its name.
  3. On the dropdown menu, select RemoveScreenshot: forms-delete-button-trashcan-icon .

Purchase and manage Teams app subscriptions in Microsoft Teams

Add functionality to your Teams experience by subscribing to apps made just for Teams. When you add an app to Teams, check if additional features are available through subscription. You can purchase subscriptions for yourself, your team, or your organization directly from Apps.

Buy a subscription

Note

Depending on your org’s settings, you may need admin approval or may not be able to purchase subscriptions directly in Teams. To learn more, contact your IT admin.

If an app has subscriptions available for purchase, you’ll see that on the app detail page.

  1. Select AppsScreenshot: teams-add-an-app-or-tab-button-icon in Teams.

  2. Find and select the app you’re interested in buying a subscription for.

  3. On the app details page, choose a subscription or upgrade option. Screenshot: Add an app subscription with selection highlighted in red.

  4. Select your country to see which subscription plans are available where you’re located.

    Note

    You can’t change this later. The country you include in your payment details also must be the same.

  5. If you see a subscription plan you want to buy, select it and choose Checkout.

    Note

    You may see a special offer that’s only for your org indicated with this icon Screenshot: Icon used to indicate an app subscription private plan. next to it.

    Screenshot: Select the subscription plan for an app

  6. During checkout, select how many subscription licenses you want, enter a sold-to address, and provide a method of payment.

    • For Sold-to address, enter the address of the legal entity responsible for payment and identified on the invoice. Depending on your situation, this could be your business or residence. The sold-to address determines the estimated tax rate for your purchase.

  7. Select Place order.

  8. Once your order is complete, select Set up now to start your subscription.

You’ll be taken to a website outside Teams to activate your subscription.

Note

If you or your team members haven’t used this app before, you still need to add it to Teams.

Manage subscriptions

If you bought a Teams app subscription or manage one for your team, you can view the list of subscriptions purchased and their details. You can also:

  • Change a plan
  • Buy or remove licenses
  • Update a payment method
  • Cancel a subscription
  • View your invoices

To take additional actions related to your subscription, like editing your billing profile or recurring billing settings, select Manage more in Microsoft 365 admin center.

Screenshot: Screenshot of Teams app subscription details (user).

From Manage your apps

Send a Loop component in Microsoft Teams chats

When you send a Loop component, everyone in your chat will be able to edit it inline—and see changes instantly. You can choose a paragraph, table, checklist, or other component to help focus your team on tasks like co-authoring content, compiling data, or tracking next steps. You’ll be able to collaborate right inside your message, minimizing the need for long chat threads.

Wondering how other people use Loop components? Find inspiration here.

  • Desktop
  • Mobile

Send a Loop component

  1. Select ChatScreenshot: teams-chat-tab-icon in Teams.
  2. Open the chat you want to send a Loop component in.
  3. In the compose box, select Loop componentsScreenshot: Loop icon .
  4. Select the type of component you want to insert into your message.
  5. Enter content into the component.
  6. When ready, select SendScreenshot: Send a message icon. .

Everyone in the chat will be able to edit the content inline.

Note

People without a valid OneDrive license will not see the Collaborate with Loop option. If you’ve recently been assigned a One Drive license, restart Teams to see the option to add a Loop component in a chat.

Edit a Loop component

To edit a Loop component, simply click where you want to add or edit content and start typing.

When editing, you can type / to insert things like an @mention, date, or even a component. If you want to comment on existing text instead of edit it, type //. This will attribute the comment to you.

Tip

Pin the message containing your live component, which puts it at the top of your chat for easy access. To do so, select More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon> Pin.

View activity and access

If others are editing while you’re viewing the component, you’ll see different colored cursors within the text indicating where people are in the document. You might also see text being edited in real time.

Profile cards appear in the upper-right corner to let you know who is viewing, editing, or has recently edited the component. Hover your cursor over any profile card for details.

Tip

@Mention people inside the component to show where you’d like them to contribute. They’ll get an activity feed notification that brings them right to the component.

Select See who has accessScreenshot: See who has access button to understand who can view or edit the component. Avatars of people who have viewed the component at least once appear here, too.

Screenshot: Loop table

Share a Loop component in another chat or channel

  1. Go to the upper-right corner of the component and select Copy linkScreenshot: Copy link button.
  2. Switch to a different chat or channel.
  3. Paste your Loop component in the compose box.

The people in your original chat and in this additional chat or channel will be able to edit the content. No matter where people are editing, the component will always show the latest updates.

View and edit the file on Office.com

Loop components are automatically saved to OneDrive once sent in chat. Here’s how to navigate to the file from chat:

  1. Select the linked file name at the top of your Loop component.

    Screenshot: Loop component filename

  2. The file will open on Office.com, where you can view and co-edit the content.

Send a Loop component

  1. Tap ChatScreenshot: teams-chat-tab-icon in Teams.

  2. Open the chat you want to send a Loop component in.

  3. Tap More messaging optionsScreenshot: More messaging options button > Loop.

    Screenshot: Loop mobile app

  4. Tap the type of component you want to insert into your message.

    Screenshot: Loop component mobile menu

  5. Enter content into the component.

  6. Tap Send.

Edit a Loop component

  1. Tap a Loop component to open it for editing.
  2. Add to or edit the content.
  3. Tap Back <. The component will show your latest updates.

Screenshot: Edit a live component on mobile

View and edit the file on Office.com

Loop components are automatically saved to OneDrive once sent in chat. Here’s how to navigate from chat to the file on Office.com.

  1. Tap a Loop component to open it for editing.
  2. Tap More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon>Open in Browser.

The file will open on Office.com, where the content can be edited with the Office app on your device. You’ll be prompted to download Office if you don’t have it yet.

Share an app with a person, group, or channel

If you find an app you think would be useful for others, there are a few quick ways to share that app with them.

    • If you don’t see the app icon, select AppsScreenshot: teams-add-an-app-or-tab-button-icon and select the app. Then, select ShareScreenshot: Share icon in Teams for iOS .

Update an app in Microsoft Teams

Most app updates happen automatically in Teams, but when an app update requires new permissions, you must manually accept the update. When you do, the update is applied everywhere you have the right to change things. That might include chats, channels, meetings, or other places.

To update an app manually:

  1. Select AppsScreenshot: teams-add-an-app-or-tab-button-icon on the left side of Teams.

  2. Near the bottom left of your screen, you’ll see a small red bubble next to Manage your appsScreenshot: manage-apps-icon . This bubble shows the number of pending app updates. Select that bubble.

  3. On the Manage your appsScreenshot: manage-apps-icon page, apps that need updates are at the top. Select Update for each app you want to update.

    Screenshot: Update available

  4. Select Update now to accept the permissions and update the app.

Update apps in a group chat

  1. Select Chat in Teams.
  2. Select a group chat.
  3. Select Open agents and botsScreenshot: apps-icon-1> Manage appsScreenshot: manage-apps-icon .
  4. Select Update for the app that you want to update.
  5. Select Update now to agree to the new permissions and update the app.

Update apps in a team

  1. Select TeamsScreenshot: skype-teams-team-icon in Teams.
  2. Select Open agents and botsScreenshot: apps-icon-1> Manage appsScreenshot: manage-apps-icon .
  3. Select Update for the app that you want to update.
  4. Select Update now to agree to the new permissions and update the app.

From a personal app

  1. Select an app on the left side of Teams.

  2. If the personal app needs new permissions, you’ll see a banner with an Update button.

    Screenshot: Update from a personal app.

  3. Select Update.

  4. Select Update now to agree to the new permissions and update the app.

Use apps in Microsoft Teams meetings

Apps in Microsoft Teams meetings help you do things like:

  • Get feedback with a survey or send reminders during the meeting
  • Collaborate in real-time on documents, boards, and other interactive content
  • Provide meeting prep material

Tip

Each app is different. Check the app’s support resources to learn what it can do in Teams meetings.

Who can use apps in meetings?

Meeting organizers and presenters can add, use, and manage apps. This includes removing apps and changing settings.

Attendees can use apps, although they might not be able to use every feature.

For more information, see Roles in a Teams meeting.

Note

Adding apps may fail in shared mailbox meeting items.

Before meetings

Set up the app ahead of time to prepare for your meeting.

Add an app before a meeting
  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: teams-calendar-tab-icon in Teams.
  2. Double-click the meeting you want to add an app to.
  3. Select AppsScreenshot: teams-apps-button-icon .
  4. Select an app to add it.
  5. Save any changes to the app.

Tip

You might see apps your org thinks will enhance your meetings.

People can access the app you added before, during, and after the meeting.

Use an app before a meeting
  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: teams-calendar-tab-icon in Teams.
  2. Double-click the meeting you want to use an app in.
  3. Select the app you want to open.
During meetings

You might realize during a meeting that a specific app may add clarity to the discussion or better illustrate your point.

Add an app during a meeting
  1. Select AppsScreenshot: teams-add-an-app-or-tab-button-icon in the meeting controls.
  2. Search for and select an app.

The app will appear in the meeting controls for everyone in the meeting to use during and after the meeting.

Note

Keep in mind, when an app is open on the right side of your screen, others in the meeting typically can’t see what you’re doing in the app until you do something to intentionally involve them, like launch a poll in a meeting.

Share in meeting

Some apps let you share app content with everyone in the meeting. When you have the app open, select Share to let everyone see your interactions with the app content. Depending on the app, some app controls may be available to the other participants.

When you’re done using the app together, select Stop sharingScreenshot: stop-sharing-icon at the top of your screen.

Change app settings

Available settings depend on the app associated with the meeting.

  1. Select the app in the meeting controls.
  2. In the app pane, select More optionsScreenshot: More options button .
  3. View and adjust available settings.
Remove an app from a meeting
  1. Select the app in the meeting controls.
  2. In the app pane, select More optionsScreenshot: More options button > RemoveScreenshot: Delete button .
After meetings

After a meeting ends, you can still go back and use its associated apps.

Use an app after a meeting
  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: teams-calendar-tab-icon in Teams.
  2. Double-click the meeting you want to use an app in.
  3. Select the app you want to open.

Note

Sixty days after a meeting was last joined, you can no longer access its apps or add new ones.

Use LinkedIn in Microsoft Teams

It’s easy to view a person’s LinkedIn profile directly in Teams. When you view a person’s profile card or go to any one-on-one chat, you can quickly see their experience, education, skills, and more. You can also expand your LinkedIn network and connect with people on LinkedIn without leaving Teams.

Note

Your organization must let you use LinkedIn in Teams. When your organization allows the LinkedIn integration, you can access LinkedIn in Outlook too.

From chat

  1. In Teams, go to any one-on-one chat and select the LinkedIn tab.

From a profile card

  2. Select Find LinkedIn profile. Or under LinkedIn, select Show profile matches.

Connect your LinkedIn and Microsoft accounts

You can access LinkedIn profiles in Teams without connecting your LinkedIn and Microsoft accounts. But if you choose to connect these accounts, you can discover more about people. A LinkedIn connection helps you find out what you have in common with them, see your degrees of connection, and connect on LinkedIn without leaving Teams.

  1. In Teams, go to any one-on-one chat and click the LinkedIn tab.
  2. Select Sign in now to connect your LinkedIn account.
  3. Select Accept to connect your LinkedIn account to Microsoft apps.
  4. Select Accept to connect your Microsoft account to LinkedIn.

Note

You only need to sign in the first time you connect with someone on LinkedIn. After that, you’ll remain signed in, so it’s easy to expand your LinkedIn network.

Cast content from a mobile device to a Microsoft Teams Room

Cast your mobile device screen

Caution

Everything on your device screen, including notifications, will be projected. You may want to set your device to Do Not Disturb before sharing your screen.

Note

You won’t be able to answer a call, join a meeting, or switch to a different Teams account while casting.

Stop projecting

Get real-time and historical analytics in the Queues app for Microsoft Teams

Use the Queues app analytics dashboard to see how your queues are doing now (real time) and how they did in the past (historical). Use these metrics to spot trends and plan staffing and queue settings.

For more metrics for auto attendants and call queues in Power BI, see Auto attendant and Call queue historical reports.

Overview

The Queues app provides analytics that help supervisors and queue owners understand how calls move through auto attendants, call queues, and queue members (agents). These analytics are designed to monitor call handling and spot trends over time.

Screenshot: Screenshot showing the Queues app analytics dashboard with the Historical tab open.

If authorized by your IT admin, you can see real-time and historical metrics. What you see depends on your admin settings and your permissions. Analytics are available in two views:

  • Real-time analytics, which reflect current call activity.
  • Historical analytics, which summarize activity over a selected time range.

The metrics you see depend on your permissions and the queues or auto attendants you have access to. Some metrics are available only at specific levels, such as per queue or per agent.

Note

Real-time analytics are reported in your device’s local time, and historical analytics are reported in UTC time zone (Coordinated Universal Time).

Access analytics

You can open analytics in two ways:

Option 1: Select a queue. You will see a quick overview at the top of Quick access on the left side of Teams.

Option 2: Open the full analytics dashboard:

  1. In the Queues app, select Analytics.
  2. Select Real-time or Historical.
  3. If you selected Historical, choose a date range, and then select Apply.
  4. Use the dropdown lists to pick the queue, auto attendant, or agent you want to review.

Call queue metrics

Call queue metrics focus on how calls are handled once they enter a queue. These metrics help you understand caller experience, queue behavior, and how effectively calls are answered.

Real-time call queue metrics

Real-time call queue metrics show what is happening in a queue right now. For example, you can see how many calls are waiting and how long people have been waiting. Real-time metrics show only today, starting at 12:00 AM local time.

  • Number of waiting calls
    • Definition: The number of calls currently waiting in the queue.
  • Average call answering time
    • Definition: The average time it takes for calls to be answered after entering the queue.
  • Longest call waiting time
    • Definition: The longest amount of time any current caller has been waiting in the queue.
  • Abandoned percentage
    • Definition: The percentage of offered calls that were abandoned.
  • Total offered calls
    • Definition: The total number of calls offered to the queue. Includes the number of calls answered and the number of calls that timed out before being answered.
  • Unanswered calls
    • Definition: The total number of calls that were not answered due to caller abandonment, no agent available, call overflowed to another destination, or call timed out before being answered.
Historical call queue metrics

Historical call queue metrics summarize how a queue performed over time. These metrics help identify trends, recurring issues, and changes in call behavior. Historical analytics are shown in UTC time zone.

  • Total call volume
    • Definition: The total number of calls received by the queue during the selected period.
  • Average wait time before answered
    • Definition: The average time callers waited before their call was answered.
  • Average wait time before abandoned
    • Definition: The average time callers waited before abandoning the call.
  • Call results
    • Definition: A breakdown of call outcomes, such as answered, abandoned, timed out, overflow, or no agents available.
  • Exception handling
    • Definition: Information about calls that followed exception paths or behaviors.
  • Abandoned calls over days
    • Definition: Trends showing how abandoned calls change over time.
  • Call volume and opt-in agents
    • Definition: Call volume correlated with the number of agents opted in to the queue.

Call queue member (agent) metrics

Agent metrics focus on how individual agents handle calls in a queue. These metrics help you understand agent participation, availability, and call handling.

Real-time call queue member metrics

Real-time queue member metrics show what each agent is doing right now. For example, you can see whether an agent is available and how calls are being offered. Real-time metrics show only today, starting at 12:00 AM local time.

  • Total calls answered
    • Definition: The total number of calls answered by the agent.
  • Total calls presented
    • Definition: The total number of calls presented to a specific agent.
  • Average call resolution
    • Definition: The percentage of calls presented to the agent that the agent answered.
Historical call queue member metrics

Historical queue member metrics summarize how agents handled calls over time. These metrics help evaluate workload, call duration, and participation. Historical analytics are shown in UTC time zone.

  • Calls answered by agents/call queue
    • Definition: The number of calls answered by agents within the queue.
  • Agent details
    • Definition: Information about individual agents included in the analytics.
  • Calls answered
    • Definition: The total number of calls answered by the agent.
  • Total call duration
    • Definition: The total amount of time the agent spent on answered calls.
  • Average answered call duration
    • Definition: The average duration of calls answered by the agent.

Auto attendant metrics

Auto attendant metrics focus on how callers interact with auto attendants before reaching a queue or other destination. These metrics help you understand caller behavior and call routing patterns.

Real-time auto attendant metrics

Real-time auto attendant metrics show what callers are doing right now. For example, you can see transfers, key selections, and time spent in the auto attendant. Real-time metrics show only today, starting at 12:00 AM local time.

  • Total call volume
    • Definition: The total number of calls presented to the auto attendant, split by internal versus external calls.
  • Total Abandoned calls
    • Definition: The total number of calls abandoned while in the auto attendant.
  • Average time in auto attendant
    • Definition: The average amount of time callers spent in the auto attendant.
  • Average caller action count
    • Definition: The average number of actions taken by callers while in the auto attendant.
  • Total system-initiated disconnects
    • Definition: The total number of calls disconnected by the system, such as when a call occurs after hours.
  • Total callers
    • Definition: The total number of callers, split by internal versus external callers.
  • Key options selected
    • Definition: The number of times each key option (0-9, *, #) was selected.
  • Transfer endpoint initiated by callers
    • Definition: Transfers initiated by callers to voice apps, operators, users, PSTN numbers, or voicemail.
  • Transfer endpoint initiated by system
    • Definition: Transfers initiated by the system to voice apps, operators, users, PSTN numbers, or voicemail.
Historical auto attendant metrics

Historical auto attendant metrics summarize how the auto attendant handled calls over time. These metrics help evaluate call volume, call actions, and call results. Historical analytics are shown in UTC time zone.

  • Total call volume
    • Definition: The total number of calls handled by the auto attendant, split by internal versus external calls.
  • Average caller action count
    • Definition: The average number of actions taken by callers.
  • Average time in auto attendant
    • Definition: The average amount of time callers spent in the auto attendant.
  • Directory search method
    • Definition: The method callers used to search the directory.
  • Caller action count
    • Definition: The total number of caller actions taken.
  • Call results
    • Definition: A breakdown of call outcomes after passing through the auto attendant. Note: Others section in call results includes system-initiated disconnects.

Manage call settings in Microsoft Teams Phone Mobile

The call settings for Teams Phone Mobile are mostly identical to the Teams app on any mobile device, but there are a few unique features to be aware of. To learn more see Getting started with Teams Phone Mobile.

Incoming call dialer selection

You can choose whether incoming calls ring your SIM-enabled phone’s default app or the Teams app. If your IT admin allows users to change this setting, follow these steps:

  1. Tap your profile picture.
  2. Tap Settings > Calling, under the Microsoft tab.
  3. Select Incoming call settings and choose either Cellular phone or Teams app.

Note

Note: To receive calls, please ensure Focus Mode in Outlook or Viva Insights is turned off, as it suppresses notifications and routes incoming calls directly to voicemail.

Call forwarding

You can set up your calls to be forwarded to other members of your team. For instructions on how to do this, see Call forwarding, call groups, and simultaneous ring in Microsoft Teams. However, please note that these settings are only available in the Teams app itself and not through your smartphone’s settings.

Hide caller ID

You can prevent your phone number from showing up on caller ID. Instead of your name or number, outbound calls will show as “Anonymous” for others.

  1. Tap your profile picture.
  2. Tap Settings > Calling, under the Microsoft tab.
  3. Turn on Hide your phone number when dialing people who are outside Microsoft Teams.

Call transfer

Though the names are very similar, this feature is distinct from uplifting calls from your phone’s built-in calling app to Teams and joining them on other devices. Call transfer transfers one-on-one calls to anyone else in your organization or to an external number through Teams. To learn how to do this, see Transfer a call in Microsoft Teams.

Note

If you are calling through your phone’s default calling app, you must first uplift the call to the Teams app before you can transfer it to another person. Learn how at Getting started with Teams Phone Mobile.

Manage call settings

For a comprehensive list of call settings, see Manage call settings in Microsoft Teams.

View call history in the Queues app in Microsoft Teams

Call history helps you track past calls in a call queue. You can review activity, follow up on missed calls, and call someone back when needed.

In this article: Learn about personal and shared call history, how to view calls, update call status, filter the list, and view call details.

Screenshot: Screenshot showing call history in the Queues app for Teams

Personal call history (default)

Personal call history shows only your own calls. This includes:

  • Calls the agent answered
  • Calls the agent made

Use this view when you only need to track your own work.

Shared call history (optional)

Shared call history shows calls for the whole queue. This includes:

  • Missed calls across the queue
  • Calls that resulted in voicemails
  • Incoming and outgoing calls handled by any agent in the queue

Use this view to coordinate follow-ups and avoid calling the same person twice.

Note

A Teams admin must turn on shared call history. For details, see Shared Call History for Call Queues - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn.

View call history

To view call history:

  1. Open the Queues app.
  2. Under Manage queue, select Calls.

The call history list shows missed calls, calls that went to voicemail, and other recent activity.

Manage call history

You can update call status to track your progress:

  • Missed calls start as Unresolved.
  • Update the status to In progress when you are working on a follow-up.
  • Change the status to Resolved when the issue is handled.

Screenshot: Screenshot showing filtering options in the Queues app.

You can also filter the call list to find what you need:

  • Missed calls
  • Answered calls
  • Outgoing calls

Filters make it easier to prioritize and manage call queue activity.

Screenshot: Screenshot showing call filter detail in Queues app.

View call details

Select a call to see details like:

  • Caller number
  • Time and date of the call
  • Call type (Missed, Answered, or Outgoing)
  • Call status (Unresolved, In progress, or Resolved)
  • Associated voicemail (if available)

Screenshot: Screenshot of call details displayed in Queues app.

Call back from call history

To call someone back:

  1. Select a call from the list.
  2. Select Call.
  3. The call uses the queue’s calling ID (if set up). Otherwise, it uses your caller ID.

Broadcasting audio and video from Microsoft Teams with NDI and SDI technology

Teams provides two options for broadcasting Teams meeting content: NewTek NDI® (Network Device Interface) and SDI (serial digital interface)

Newtek NDI® technology allows you to broadcast the audio and video streams from a Teams meeting to your local network. When using NewTek NDI® technology in a Teams meeting, you will have unique video streams on the network that can be used in your own production.

SDI has been used in broadcast productions since 1989 and is supported on most legacy studio hardware devices. Hardware devices from AJA Video Systems and Blackmagic Design provide connectivity to legacy broadcast devices that use SDI.

Turning on NDI® technology in Teams

To start using NDI®, your admin will need to enable the broadcast production policy. Once the policy is turned on, NDI® will be available.

To start using NDI® in Teams:

  1. Select Settings and moreScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon in Teams.
  2. Select SettingsScreenshot: Settings button > App permissionsScreenshot: Permissions icon .
  3. Under Production tools, select Download Link to install the latest NDI® binaries.
  4. After installing, turn on the Production tools toggle. You can’t turn on this toggle while you’re in a Teams meeting.

Important

  • You’ll need to complete these steps after every Teams update. We recommend completing them before an event using NDI® in case you need to re-download the latest binaries.
  • To learn more about the Teams update release schedule, see Version update history for Teams.

After enabling NDI® technology in Teams, join a meeting and select More actionsScreenshot: More options button in your meeting controls. Then, select Streaming > Broadcast over NDI.

All meeting attendees who are subscribed to that NDI stream will be notified that broadcasting capabilities are turned on.

NDI®-out features

Once NDI® technology is turned on, the following streams will be available:

  • Primary speaker: A stream will be generated that automatically switches to whoever is actively speaking from all of the incoming streams. (Audio/video from your own computer won’t be included.)

  • Local: A stream will be generated of the audio/video that is being sent to the meeting from your computer. (This allows you to have the same audio/video in both the meeting and in your local NDI® production.)

  • Individual users: Each user will have a stream available over NDI®. The incoming audio for a meeting is mixed together and will be the same for all individual user streams. These streams will display the video at the same quality that is being received by the client.

    Note

    If no video is available, you’ll see a simple screen with the Teams logo. But the stream is still being received by your NDI® software/hardware.

  • Screen sharing: Any incoming screen sharing will be available as an NDI® stream.

  • Large gallery: This mode will have its own NDI® stream available.

SDI hardware-out devices

Just as with NDI®-out capabilities, SDI hardware-out capabilities must have the NDI/Broadcast policy enabled by your admin. You must also be using either Blackmagic Design (BMD) or AJA Video Systems hardware.

Once your admin has enabled you to broadcast, you’ll need to go to Settings and moreScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon next to your profile picture in Teams. Then select Settings > App permissions > then enable the toggle next to Production Capabilities. If you have any SDI devices connected, you’ll see them under Video hardware out.

Note

SDI hardware devices may need additional configuration outside of Teams. Check the manufacturer’s documentation for more information.

If the hardware-out option is available, when you’re in a meeting you’ll have the option to Send video to Hardware in More optionsScreenshot: Teams more options icon next to a meeting participant’s name.

If there is more than one kind of device available, they’ll be listed alphabetically. If a device can output more than one A/V stream, then you’ll see a list of output options to choose from.

To stop streaming a particular video, go back to More optionsScreenshot: Teams more options icon next to the person’s name and select Stop sending to.

Note

If the hardware device is in use by something other than Teams, the option will still display but will be disabled.

Technical limitations

These are some common technical issues to consider when using NDI® Technology in Teams:

  • Broadcasting NDI® signals from Teams is limited by the number of streams and quality of the streams your Teams client receives.
  • A good strategy is to first “pin” a video stream in Teams to ensure that particular video stays connected during the meeting. Under that meeting participant’s name, select More actionsScreenshot: Select to see more options and then choose Pin.

Screenshot: Teams-Pin stream button-circled

  • Try limiting the number of NDI®-out video streams to two or three on any single computer. This is another good strategy that’ll help ensure stability and performance for most users.
  • Changing to a different meeting layout such as Large Gallery will stop the video streams of other people in the meeting from coming to your computer. Your machine will then only be able to stream the selected layout via NDI®. (Returning to the Gallery layout will restore the video streams.)
  • Apple Macs with BlackMagic devices aren’t currently supported for Hardware-Out.

Call forwarding, call groups, and simultaneous ring in Microsoft Teams

You can forward calls to another number or Teams member, or ring another number at the same time as your work number.

Set up call forwarding

To start forwarding your calls, select Settings and moreScreenshot: Generic Ellipsis button next to your profile picture at the top of Teams. Then select Settings > CallsScreenshot: Call tab icon .

Under Call handling and forwarding, select the toggle to choose how all call forwarding should be handled, or set up different responses for different scenarios. You can choose to have calls sent to voicemail, to a new number or specific contact, a call group, or your delegates.

Tip

Learn how to set up a delegate and forward your calls to other people or groups.

Note

  • Call forwarding is only available in one-on-one calls.
  • If you don’t see any options for call forwarding in your settings, you likely don’t have an Enterprise Voice or Business Voice license. Also note that it can take up to 24 hours for changes in licenses to take effect.
Create a call group

Call group members can receive calls on your behalf. After you create a call group, use the forwarding instructions in the previous section to forward calls to your call group.

  1. To get started, go to Settings and moreScreenshot: Generic Ellipsis button next to your profile picture at the top of Teams. Then select Settings > CallsScreenshot: Call tab icon .

  2. Under Manage call group, select Add a call group to create a new group. If you already created a call group, select Edit to change members, settings, or call order.

  3. Under Add people, add the people you want in your call group. A call group can contain up to 25 people.

    Note

    You need to add people from your organization. Phone numbers aren’t supported.

You can select the order in which your calls are forwarded to members of your call group, or you can choose to have it ring everyone in the group at once.

  1. Select the dropdown above the list of group members to choose your ring order, either Everyone at once or In the order below.
  2. If you select In the order below, drag members of the call group into a preferred order for receiving your calls.

Screenshot: call group

Group call pickup is less disruptive than other forms of call forwarding. Recipients can choose how to be notified of an incoming call in their settings and decide whether to answer it.

Note

Mobile devices will only get call group notifications if they’re set for banner and ringtone.

Use the call forwarding quick menu

You can quickly view and change your call forwarding status directly from the Calls app without opening Settings.

The quick menu at the bottom of the Calls app shows your current call routing configuration:

  • Don’t forward: No forwarding or simultaneous ring is active. Calls ring only you.
  • Forward to [name/number]: Calls are being forwarded to that target, or simultaneous ring (“Also ring”) is configured for that target.
  • Forward to voicemail: All calls are being forwarded to voicemail.

To change your forwarding settings from the quick menu:

  1. Go to the Calls app in Teams.
  2. At the bottom of the Calls app, select the forwarding status (for example, “Don’t forward” or “Forward to [name/number]”).
  3. From the menu, choose:
    • Don’t forward: Turns off forwarding and simultaneous ring.
    • Forward to voicemail: Forwards all calls to voicemail.
    • Forward to [name/number]: Forwards calls to a target (up to three shown).
    • Forwarding to call group: Forwards calls to your call group (only shown if you have a call group configured).
    • Forwarding to delegates: Forwards calls to your delegates (only shown if you have delegates configured).
    • More Settings: Opens Settings > Calls for full configuration options.

How quick menu targets work: The menu shows up to three names or numbers. The app adds these targets based on who you most recently set as a forwarding or “Also ring” target in Settings > Calls. The most recent targets appear, and older ones are replaced as new ones are configured. To remove a target from the quick menu, set a different forwarding target in Settings to push it out of the list.

Note

If you configure “Also ring” (simultaneous ring) in Settings, the quick menu displays “Forward to [name]”, even though calls still ring you as well. To confirm whether calls are being forwarded or simultaneously rung, select More Settings or go to Settings > Calls > Call handling and forwarding and check the When you receive a call setting.

Set up call forwarding for a Teams SIP device

On the device’s main menu, select CFW soft button. The Teams Call Forwarding state will be displayed along with instructions on how to change it using dialing feature codes.

Note

The following device models currently don’t support call forwarding: Yealink T30, Yealink T30P, Cisco 6821, Poly Trio 8500, Poly Trio 8800, and AudioCodes IP Phones.

Forward always

Dial *33* followed by the forwarded-to phone number. The phone number can be in E.164 format or a dial string that’ll be converted based on your dial plan.

To forward calls to your voicemail, set a forward-to phone number redirecting to your office phone. You can do this for all forwarding settings.

  • Example: *33*+14257222217 or *33*14257222217

If the caller hears a ring tone four times or a fast busy tone, this indicates the setting is working.

Forward on timeout (unanswered calls)
  1. Dial *34*.
  2. Enter an optional time in seconds. This time must be rounded to the next 10 and can be up to 60 seconds. The default is set to 20 seconds.
  3. Dial * followed by the forwarded-to phone number.
  • Example: *34*10*14257222217 (ring me 10 seconds and if unanswered forward to 14257222217 or *34*14257222217 (ring me for 20 seconds – default and if unanswered forward to 14257222217).
Reset

Dial *32*

Set up external call routing

External call routing allows you to redirect incoming phone calls (not Teams calls) to voicemail or your unanswered call settings. This helps to filter spam calls and provides different levels of control over phone calls and Teams calls.

  1. Select Settings and moreScreenshot: Generic Ellipsis button next to your profile picture at the top of Teams.
  2. Then choose Settings > CallsScreenshot: Call tab icon .
  3. Under Call handling and forwarding > Redirect external phone calls, choose between redirecting calls to voicemail and redirecting them as unanswered. The toggle is off by default.

Note

If you don’t see this option in your call settings, it’s likely that this feature hasn’t been set up by your IT admin. Contact them to learn more.

Screenshot: Redirect calls to voicemail or unanswered

Set up simultaneous ring

If you want your incoming calls to ring you and someone else (such as a delegate) at the same time, you can set that up in Teams.

  1. Select Settings and moreScreenshot: Generic Ellipsis button next to your profile picture at the top of Teams. Then choose Settings > CallsScreenshot: Call tab icon .
  2. Under Call handling and forwarding > When you receive a call, you can choose to ring a contact, a call group, or your delegates.
  3. If you choose to ring a new number or contact, begin typing the name of the person you’d like to simultaneously receive your calls and select their name from the dropdown.
  4. Next, you can choose to delay simultaneous ring. This option directs calls to the intended recipient first, rather than notifying everyone the moment a call comes in. Select the number of seconds you’d like to delay the call from the dropdown menu, up to 20 seconds. This setting defaults to No delay.

Note

If you don’t see any options for simultaneous ring in your settings, it’s likely you don’t have an Enterprise Voice or Business Voice license. Also note that it can take up to 24 hours for changes in licenses to take effect.

Check your voicemail in Microsoft Teams

Your voicemail is a familiar tool for getting the most out of your calling experience in Teams. To access your voicemail, go to CallsScreenshot: Calls button > History and then select Voicemail.

Screenshot: Teams-Voicemail-main

Call someone back by hovering over a voicemail and selecting CallScreenshot: Calls button or by selecting More actionsScreenshot: Select to see more options and choosing Call backScreenshot: Calls button .

When you select a voicemail, you can review and access details and other information—all on the right side of Teams.

Screenshot: Teams-Voicemail-Details screen

From here, you can:

  • Listen to your voicemails by using the playback controls at the bottom.
  • Review your voicemail summaries and transcripts (if available).
  • Call someone back by using the call controls under the contact details at the top.
  • Customize voicemail settings (such as recording a greeting and specifying call answering rules).

Connect a Microsoft Teams display or desk phone to Microsoft Teams Windows desktop

Connect your Microsoft Teams display or Teams desk phone to your Windows computer to enable cross-device interaction. Your connected display or desk phone will conveniently lock and unlock when the computer is locked and unlocked.

With a connected Teams display, you’ll also be able to join and participate in meetings on both the computer and display at the same time, as well as respond to chat messages that you read on the display by using the computer keyboard. And more features are in the works.

Note

Mac, Linux, web, mobile, and 32-bit/ARM-based Teams clients are not currently supported.

Before you begin

  • The computer must be running 64-bit Teams desktop client version 1.3.00.15364 or later.
  • The computer must be Bluetooth enabled.
  • The display or desk phone must be placed near the computer.

Connect the devices

  1. Sign in to the computer and the display or desk phone as the same user.
  2. On the display or desk phone, select your picture and then select Connect a device.
  3. Select Find a device.
  4. When the display or desk phone locates the computer, select Connect.
  5. On the computer, select Connect.
