Chat with others in Microsoft Teams

  • Desktop
  • Mobile

Use Microsoft Teams to chat online with your colleagues.

Start a chat with another person

  1. Select New messageScreenshot: New chat icon at the top of your list of chats and channels.
  2. Enter a person’s name.
  3. Compose your message in the box at the bottom of the chat.
  4. To open formatting options, select FormatScreenshot: Expand button to the right of your message.
  5. When your message is ready, select SendScreenshot: Send a message icon. or press Enter to start the chat.

You can also start a one-on-one chat from someone’s profile card. Open it by choosing their picture in a channel or finding their name using the Search box.

Start a chat with yourself

You can start a chat with yourself in Teams. Compose your message just as you would in a regular one-on-one chat. Use your chat space for drafts, to send messages and files to yourself, or to get to know chat features a little better. You can drag your chat with yourself to the top of the Favorites section for easy reference.

Start and name a group chat

A group chat includes multiple people in a conversation. Create a group chat the same way you start a one-on-one chat.

  1. Select New messageScreenshot: New chat icon in Teams at the top of your list of chats and channels.
  2. Select the down arrow to the far right of To to reveal the Group name section.
  3. Type a group name.
  4. Type the names of the people you’d like to add in the To section.

This starts a new conversation. Everyone who has access to the group chat can send messages.

You can include up to 250 people in a group chat.

Add people to the conversation

  1. To add people to a group chat, select View and add participantsScreenshot: Add participants icon> Add people.
  2. Type the names of the people you’d like to chat with. If it is an existing group chat, you can also choose how much of the chat history to include.
  3. Select Add to add them to the conversation.

Note

  • You can include chat history only when adding someone to an existing group chat, not for a one-on-one.
  • Teams saves the entire chat history, all the way back to the first message. If someone leaves the group, their chat responses remain in your chat history.

See who’s in a group chat

To see who’s in a group chat, select View and add participantsScreenshot: Add participants icon in the top right corner. This will show a list of everyone’s names.

Chat with Microsoft support

Contact - Microsoft Support

Use chat in Microsoft Teams to send messages to one person or a group. You can start new chats, name group chats, and manage participants directly from your mobile device.

Start a chat with another person

  1. Tap Chat > New messageScreenshot: New chat icon .

  2. In the To field, enter a person’s name.

  3. Type your message in the compose box.

    1. To open formatting, tap More messaging options TeamsScreenshot: Teams plus button black > FormatScreenshot: Expand button .

  4. Tap Send to start the chat.

Start a chat with yourself

You can create a chat with yourself to save notes, reminders, or links.

  1. Tap Chat.
  2. Tap New messageScreenshot: New chat icon .
  3. Enter your own name in the To field.
  4. Type and send your message.

To keep this chat easy to find, drag it to the top of your Favorites list.

Start and name a group chat

Create a group chat to message multiple people at once.

  1. Tap Chat > New messageScreenshot: New chat icon .
  2. Type the names of the people you’d like to add in the To field.
  3. Type a message and tap Send.
  4. At the top of the chat, tap the participant’s names.
  5. Tap Group chat name.
  6. Enter a name for the chat, then tap Save.

Everyone who has access to the group chat can send messages.

Add people to a chat

Add more people to an existing group chat.

  1. Open the group chat.
  2. Tap the participant names at the top.
  3. Tap Add people.
  4. Enter the names of the people to add.
  5. Choose how much chat history to include.
  6. Tap Done.

Note

You can include chat history only when adding people to a group chat, not a one‑on‑one chat. Teams keeps the full chat history. If someone leaves the group, their messages remain in the chat.

See who’s in a group chat

To see who’s in a group chat, open the group chat and tap the participant’s names at the top of the screen. You’ll see a list of everyone in the chat.

Catch up on all your conversations in one place

Catch up helps you quickly review and respond to the conversations that need your attention, all in one place. It brings together unread and important messages so you can clear your badge count and stay up to date.

Catch up includes new and unread conversations across:

  • Conversations with personal mentions, wherever they appear
  • 1:1 chats
  • Group and meeting chats (unless muted)
  • Followed threads

Each conversation appears on its own swipeable card, showing the full context so you don’t lose your place. You can read, respond, and react without navigating away from the view, and mute or unfollow directly from the card header if you’re not interested in that conversation.

To open and manage Catch up:

  • Tap Catch up at the top of your list of chats. The number of cards indicates the number of conversations that need your attention to get to zero badge count in your Teams app.
  • Swipe right to mark the conversation as read. Swipe left to keep it unread. You can also use the Keep unread and Mark as read buttons at the bottom of the screen. Your read and unread states sync across mobile and desktop, so you can continue where you left off.
  • To undo one of these actions, tap Undo at the top of the screen to bring back the previous card.
  • Tap the dropdown arrow next to the chat or channel name to Mute/Unfollow or Go to a conversation.
  • Tap Sort by in the upper right corner of your screen to change the order your cards. Select from @Mentions first to see conversations with your name @mentioned first, or Recent to see the cards in order of most recent on top.

When you’ve reviewed everything, you’ll see a clear message saying You’re all caught up. If new items arrive later, a dot badge lets you know there’s more to review.

Check your spelling in multiple languages in Microsoft Teams

Similar to other Microsoft 365 products, Microsoft Teams now offers multi-language spell-checking capabilities, allowing you to confidently compose messages in various languages. To check spelling in an additional language, start by adding the language to your list of spellcheck languages.

  1. Go to Settings and moreScreenshot: Generic Ellipsis button , then select SettingsScreenshot: Settings button
  2. In the General section, go to Editor Spellcheck. Then, select Manage to add more languages.

You can also ignore certain details, such as uppercase letters, words with numbers or internet and files addresses.

Once you’ve added the language, start typing. Teams will automatically detect errors based on your chosen languages and provide suggestions accordingly.

Tip

Add languages after you’ve started writing a message by selecting More options > Manage languages.

Add words to the dictionary

Add words to the dictionary to ensure that they aren’t flagged as spelling errors in the future.

To do this, select the word then select, Add to Dictionary.

Note

Add up to 5 languages to your proofing dictionary. Multi-language proofing feature currently supports the following languages: English, Spanish, French, Italian, and German.

Ignore spelling suggestions

To ignore a spelling suggestion, select the word, then select Ignore All.

Do your one-on-ones in Microsoft Teams

Use Microsoft Teams to conduct one-on-one meetings with reports and colleagues. Whether you meet online or face-to-face, Teams can help keep things organized.

Your first impulse might be to create a team for each of your one-on-one meetings, but that can get unwieldy over time. Individual teams are really meant for groups of three or more people.

So, how should you structure your one-on-ones in Teams? The answer is chat.

  • Chat holds all the files that you’ve shared with people in Teams chats and meetings.
  • You can add important files, websites, and apps to the top of your chat for easy review.
  • If you meet virtually, either person can kick off a call right from your chat.

First, add the chat to Favorites

Add a chat to Favorites so it stays at the top of the chats and channels area. That way, you don’t have to track it down. Add a chat for each person you meet in a one-on-one.

To add a chat to Favorites, drag the chat into the order you want in the Favorites list. Now all your frequent chats are within reach.

Next, put important stuff in tabs at the top of your chat

Let’s say you’ve got a file or a link that you regularly review together during your one-on-one time. To keep it front and center, add it to the Shared tab at the top of your chat.

Your chat with a person catalogs the files you and that person share with each other in Teams—all there on the Files tab. Whether it’s a living document that you’re developing together or a one-off review, if it’s been shared in your chat, you can get it in the Files tab.

Sharing files
  1. To share a file, select the Shared tab at the top of the chat.
  2. Select Upload, and then choose Attach cloud files or Upload from this device.

The file appears under the Files tab.

Any files you share in messages for this chat also appear on the Files tab. See Send a file, picture, or link in Microsoft Teams to learn more about attaching files to messages.

Sharing links

When you share links in your messages, they appear in the Links folder at the top of your chat for future reference.

When you’re ready to meet

If you meet virtually, you can kick off the meeting right from your chat.

  • To meet, expand the More call options in the upper-right corner below your profile pic. Then, choose Video callScreenshot: Video chat button or Audio callScreenshot: Audio call button .

Once you’re in a call, either person in the chat can share their screen so you can look at the files or websites you put at the top of your chat.

Forward messages in Microsoft Teams

Forward messages in Microsoft Teams to quickly share information with others. You can forward chat messages, files, Loop components, app cards, and images to a person, a group chat, or a channel.

You can forward up to five messages at a time. When you forward multiple messages, Teams bundles them into a single message and keeps the original order. This helps recipients follow the conversation more easily. You can also start a new group chat from a forwarded message.

  1. Hover over the message and choose More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > Forward.

    1. To forward multiple messages, select More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > Forward > Multiple messages.
    2. Select the check boxes next to the messages you want to forward in your chat.
    3. Select Next.

  2. In the window that appears, begin typing the name, group chat or channel you want to share content with, then select it from the drop-down list. Adding multiple people will forward the content to a group chat.

  3. Optionally, add a message above your forwarded content for context.

  4. Select Forward to send your message(s).

  5. Select View in the notification that appears to go to the forwarded message.

Note

  • You can forward up to five images in a single message.
  • Team administrators can apply sensitivity labels that limit the sharing of content. If a team has sensitivity labels that block forwarding, you won’t see the option to forward messages from channels in that team.

How to find the original message

When you receive a forwarded message in Teams on desktop, look for the timestamp in the forwarded message header. Select the timestamp to open the original chat or channel message.

Note

If you have permission to view the original conversation, Teams will take you directly to it. If you don’t have permission, you’ll see a message indicating that the content isn’t available.

Getting started with storyline from Viva Engage in Microsoft Teams

Storyline from Viva Engage is now integrated into Microsoft Teams, making it easier than ever to access and interact with storyline content directly within your Teams workflows.

With storyline, leaders can reach their organizations and share personalized updates. People within an org can use storyline to share experiences, celebrate milestones, propose ideas, and discuss interests.

Screenshot: Profile page with mountain banner, persons photo, name, title, follower counts, and a post with a link for more info.

Access storyline in Teams

First, make sure your organization has a Viva Engage license and the storyline capability is set up in Viva Engage. Admins can learn more here: Manage Viva Engage experiences in Microsoft Teams.

Get storyline notifications in the Activity feed

Storyline notifications appear in your activity feed alongside mentions, reactions, and replies. You can manage these notifications by selecting More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon  > Notification settingsScreenshot: Settings gear icon at the top of the activity feed.

Screenshot: Activity feed with recent posts and meeting notes with reactions. The feed includes navigation and filter tabs.

Visit other people’s storyline page

While you’re in a one-on-one chat with someone, you can access their storyline as a tab at the top of the chat. From there, you’ll see their existing posts and be able to react and comment on them.

Select Follow storyline to be notified in your activity feed whenever they post something new.

View your storyline page

You can find your own storyline page as a tab in a chat with yourself. From your storyline page, you can:

  • See your existing posts and interact with them.
  • Create new posts and announcements.
  • See your followers and people you follow.
  • Access your storyline profile analytics, as well as individual conversation analytics for each post.
  • Upload or change your cover image.

Note

To upload or change your cover image, your org must have Viva Engage Premium.

Create a new storyline post

You can create a storyline post from your storyline tab in a self chat. You can also select the dropdown next to New message and choose New storyline post.

Storyline posts you create in Teams will appear in Viva Engage, and vice versa.

To learn more about different types of storyline posts and who can create them, see Write and schedule posts, articles, and announcements.

Screenshot: Text input box labeled My storyline and a Discussion button, formatting options, and placeholders for sharing, adding people, and posting.

Post or comment on behalf of someone else

If you’ve been assigned as someone’s delegate, you can post to their storyline or comment on a storyline post on their behalf.

To post as a delegate, go to the storyline page in your one-on-one chat. From there, you can type your post and send it.  

To comment as a delegate, open the comment option on any storyline post, select the person you’re commenting on behalf of from the dropdown next to Comment as, and leave your comment. 

To learn more about how to assign and manage delegates in Viva Engage, see Delegation in Viva Engage.

Note

To post on behalf of someone, your org must have Viva Engage Premium.

Screenshot: A drop-down menu for selecting a commenter, a text box for writing comments with bold and italic options, and a Post button.

See your storyline analytics

Get access to engagement information on your storyline posts by accessing conversation analytics for individual posts. Select More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > View analytics in the upper-right corner of any of your storyline posts.

For more advanced analytics, access your storyline profile analytics by selecting More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > View profile analytics at the lower-right corner of your storyline cover image.

To view premium analytics features, your org must have Viva Engage Premium which is bundled with the Viva Suite and Employee Communications and Communities license. Conversation, live event, and some community analytics are available without a premium license. Audience analytics are only viewable by people who have at least one primary assigned audience and their delegates. Learn more about licensing. Learn more about analytics.  

Admins can learn more about leader and audience identification here: Identify leaders.

Troubleshooting

If you’re having trouble accessing or using storyline in Teams, please try the following:

  • Make sure that your org has a Viva Engage license and that the storyline capability is turned on.
  • Check your internet connection and make sure that you’re able to access other websites and services.
  • Try refreshing your browser or restarting your computer.
  • If you’re still having trouble, please contact your IT admin or the Viva Engage support team.

Hide a chat, remove chat history or leave a chat thread in Microsoft Teams

  • Desktop
  • Mobile

In Teams, you can remove chats from your chat list in different ways. Each option has a different result.

Hide a chat: Temporarily remove a one‑on‑one chat from your list. You can find it again by searching.

Remove chat history: Remove a one‑on‑one chat from your list and search. This affects only you.

Leave a chat: Leave a group or meeting chat so it no longer appears in your list and you can’t send messages.

To delete individual messages from a chat thread, see Edit or delete a sent message in Teams.

Hide one-on-one chats

  1. In your list of chats and channels, select the one-on-one chat you want to change.
  2. Select More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft teams More options icon. > HideScreenshot: Hide chat button to no longer see the chat.

Remove chat history in one-on-one chats

When you remove chat history:

  • It applies only to you.
  • The other person still sees the chat.
  • You can’t access the chat again, including through search.
  1. In your list of chats and channels, select the one-on-one chat you want to remove.
  2. Select More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft teams More options icon. > Remove chat historyScreenshot: Delete button trashcan icon to remove the chat from your list.

Leave a group or meeting chat

  1. Select the chat you want to change and select More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft teams More options icon. > LeaveScreenshot: Teams leave chat icon .
  2. Select the check box to confirm that you want to remove chat history from your chat and search lists when you leave. Select Leave.

If you’re a meeting owner, you can’t delete or leave the meeting chat. However, if you’re a participant in the meeting chat, you can delete or leave it.

When a one-on-one, group, or meeting chat thread isn’t needed and you want to clear it from your chat list, leave it. To delete individual messages from a chat thread, see Edit or delete a sent message in Teams.

  1. From the Chat tab, select the chat and press and hold it.
  2. Confirm that you want to remove chat history from your list when you leave. For a one-on-one chat, tap Delete. For a group chat, tap Leave.
  3. Confirm your choice by selecting Delete or Leave.

When you leave a conversation, the chat history stays, but you can’t send messages in this chat.

Hide, unhide, mute, add a chat to Favorites, or mark a chat as unread in Microsoft Teams

There are many ways to organize your chats in Microsoft Teams.

  • Hide or mute chat conversations from your chat list to stop receiving notifications.
  • Add frequent conversations to the top of your Favorites list for quick access.
  • Mark a message as unread as a quick way to remind yourself to look at it again later.
  • Leave a chat thread or delete individual messages you’ve sent.

Hide a chat

  1. Go to the chat, then point to reveal More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon .
  2. Select HideScreenshot: Teams hide chat icon to hide the conversation.

The chat and its history are hidden until someone posts a new message to it.

Tip

Use your keyboard to hide a chat by typing /hide in the compose box, and then pressing Enter. See Use commands in Microsoft Teams for more keyboard shortcuts.

Unhide a chat

Unhide a chat that you’ve hidden before by using search.

  1. In the SearchScreenshot: Select to start a search. box at the top of Teams, type the name of the person you were chatting with and select it from the list of returned names. You’ll see that the chat history is hidden and the name appears in italic text to mark it as hidden.
  2. Select More optionsScreenshot: More options button > Unhide next to the name. The conversation now appears in your list.
  3. If you don’t see it right away, select FilterScreenshot: Select to start a search. to search for it. Once you find the conversation, select More optionsScreenshot: More options button > Unhide.
  4. Select Show hidden chat history to see the conversation.

Mute a chat

When you mute a chat, you’re still included in the conversation, but you won’t get notifications from it. You’re only notified of @Mentions.

  1. Go to the chat, then point to reveal More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon .
  2. Select MuteScreenshot: Teams chat mute icon to mute the conversation.
  3. If you change your mind, select More optionsScreenshot: More options button > UnmuteScreenshot: UnMute Chat Button Icon .

Muted chats are organized in a Muted section at the bottom of your chat list that’s turned on by default. When you mute a chat, it automatically moves to the Muted section unless it’s already in a custom section. Muted chats still show bold text for unread messages, but they don’t add to the chat badge count.

You can turn the Muted section off to send muted chats back to your recent chat list. Turn it back on anytime in Settings > Chat and channels > Show meeting chats in their own section.

Tip

The Mute symbol Screenshot: Teams chat mute icon appears next to the names of the chat participants to remind you that the chat has been muted.

Add a chat to the Favorites list

For quick access, you can add frequent conversations to the top of your Favorites list.

  1. In your list of chats and channels, drag the chat to the Favorites list. You choose the order for the list items.
  2. If you change your mind, select More optionsScreenshot: More options button > Remove from section.

You can also hover over the chat to reveal More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > Move to > Favorites.

Mark a message as unread

One way to remind yourself to read a message later is to mark it as unread.

  1. Go to the chat, then point to reveal More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon .
  2. Select Mark as unreadScreenshot: glasses with a line through it .

The next time you open the chat, it’ll appear unread.

When you leave a group chat, other people are informed that you’ve left. You also won’t be able to post or get messages from the group chat.

To undo the priority label on a message:

  1. In the message, select EditScreenshot: Edit icon
  2. Select Actions and appsScreenshot: Actions and apps button .

To help make sure your message gets noticed, mark it as important.

  1. Tap the plus sign Screenshot: The Plus button in Teams next to the box where you type your message.

Mark a message as important at any time before sending it with the steps above. If you’ve already sent your message, edit your message and assign a priority to it.

Open a chat in a new window in Microsoft Teams

It’s simple and quick to open your one-on-one or group chat in a separate window. Then, resize, reposition, or close the window if you want to. It’s a good way to get more done when you’re in a meeting or in a call.

You can open multiple conversations in new windows, but not the same chat twice.

Tip

To do other things (like scheduling meetings, attaching a OneDrive File, adding apps), return to the main app to find those familiar features. You don’t need to close the chat window.

There are a few options to open a chat in a new window in Teams. Here are a few different methods:

From a chat

  1. Find the chat you want.
  2. Select More optionsScreenshot: Three asterisks indicating more options menu > Open chat in new windowScreenshot: New breakout icon .
  3. You can also double-click the chat name to open the chat in a new window.

From a profile picture

Double-click the profile picture of the person or group you want to have a conversation with to open a new window.

Personalize your group chat image in Microsoft Teams

Make your group chat stand out by customizing the image. Upload your own image, or choose from a gallery of illustrations and emoji.

Note

  • Images can be added, changed, or removed on Desktop or Web.

  1. Select ChatScreenshot: Teams Chat Tab icon on the left side of Teams, and click the group chat you’d like to personalize.

  2. Above the chat, hover over the profile picture to the left of the group’s name to select Change profile picture.

  3. A new window will open with the option to upload your own image or choose a pre-set illustration, or an emoji.

    Screenshot: Screenshot showing options for group chat avatar images

  4. If choosing an illustration or emoji, simply find the one you want, and select Save.

  5. If you’d like to use your own image, select UploadScreenshot: Upload icon , find the image in your files, then select Save.

  6. To edit the image again, or to return to the default image, repeat the steps to select the default or a different image.

Note

  • Maximum size for photo upload is 4MB.
  • Images are currently not supported in meeting chats or 1:1 chats.
  • Muted group chats will show the mute icon instead of the group chat image.

Pin a chat message to the top of a chat in Microsoft Teams

Sometimes you might want to pin a particular chat message for reference in a one-to-one or a group chat. A pinned message appears at the top of the chat and remains there until removed or replaced.

Things to know about pinned chat messages:

  • When someone pins a message in a chat, everyone in that chat can see it.
  • Only one message can be pinned at a time.
  • A pinned message doesn’t affect an ongoing chat.
  • Anyone in a chat, except guests, can unpin any pinned message or replace it with a different message.
  • If someone selects a pinned message, they’ll go to the original message in the chat.

Pin a chat message

  1. In a chat conversation, hover over the specific message that you want to pin.
  2. In the menu that appears above the message, select More optionsScreenshot: More options icon .
  3. In the More options menu, choose Pin for everyoneScreenshot: Pin a message . The pinned message appears at the top of the chat. It also includes the name of the author and the date or time it was originally posted.

Note

A pinned chat message may be any length. However, only a single line of text that fits within the width of the chat window will be visible.

Screenshot: Screenshot showing a pinned chat message at the top of a chat

Unpin a pinned chat message

  1. Go to the pinned message at top of the chat.

  2. Select More optionsScreenshot: More options icon > Unpin for everyoneScreenshot: Unpin chat message .

Prevent spam or phishing attempts from external chats in Microsoft Teams

When Teams detects potential spam or phishing activity (also known as impersonation) from someone requesting to chat with you from outside your organization, you’ll see a notification.

Impersonation is a common type of cyberattack where the sender adopts the identity of a specific person or entity with the intention of deceiving the recipient.

When you see the following screen in a one-on-one chat or group chat, please take these actions to ensure your security:

Screenshot: Screenshot showing the warning message that appears when Teams suspects an external contact may be attempting to spam, phish, or impersonate.

  1. Double-check the sender’s identity, including their name and email address.
  2. Preview the message and check for anything that looks unusual or suspicious.
  3. Only accept the conversation if you’re sure the sender is trustworthy.

Choose Accept if you trust the sender. Choose Block to stop receiving any Teams communications from them.

Preview messages in Microsoft Teams

Sometimes you want to know what a message is about before reading it. In Microsoft Teams, you can preview chat messages and notifications before opening them.

Preview messages in chat

To keep your list of chats simple, you won’t automatically see message previews.

Screenshot: Screenshot of messages with no message preview and a time stamp.

However, you can turn them on if you prefer.

Screenshot: Screenshot of messages with a message preview that also shows the time stamp.

To turn them on,

  1. From Settings and moreScreenshot: Generic Ellipsis button select SettingsScreenshot: Settings button .
  2. Select Chats and channels.
  3. Turn on Show message previews for chats and team names for channels.

Note

If you’re using multiple accounts, you’ll need to choose the same message previews settings for all of your accounts.

Show time stamps

There’s also the option to Show time stamps. This displays either the day that the message was sent, or the time if the message was sent today.

Time stamps are separate from message previews. You can choose to show them, but not show a preview of the message. However, you can’t show message previews without also showing time stamps. 

Note

If you are using a screen reader, you’ll need to turn on message preview to hear the preview. 

Preview messages in notifications

You can also show message and content previews in your notifications.

  1. From Settings and moreScreenshot: Generic Ellipsis button then select SettingsScreenshot: Settings button.
  2. Select Notifications and activity.
  3. Under Display, select Show message and content previews in notifications.

Protect against impersonation attempts in Microsoft Teams calling

When Teams detects a potential impersonation attempt during an incoming call from outside your organization, you’ll see a warning notification that says Scam suspected to help you make an informed decision before answering or continuing the conversation.

Screenshot: Screenshot of a Scam suspected call in Microsoft Teams.

Impersonation is a common type of cyberattack where a caller pretends to be a trusted person, company, or organization in an attempt to gain your trust or obtain sensitive information.

When Teams identifies that a caller may not be who they claim to be, the app displays a warning to help you stay protected.

If you see a potential scam caller warning

When you receive a call that has been flagged as potentially suspicious, review the information carefully before answering or continuing the call.

In this scenario, if you’ve already answered the call, Teams will display a message, We recommend that you leave the call now, unless you’re sure of the caller’s identity.Screenshot: Screenshot of a suspected spam call label.

Verify the caller’s identity

Before sharing any information:

  • Double-check the caller’s name and organization.
  • Consider whether you were expecting the call.
  • Verify the caller’s identity using a trusted communication channel if necessary.
  • Be cautious if the caller creates urgency or requests sensitive information.

Look for suspicious behavior

Be alert if the caller:

  • Requests passwords or verification codes.
  • Asks for personal, financial, or confidential information.
  • Pressures you to take immediate action.
  • Claims to represent a company or person you do not recognize.

Decide how to respond

If you trust the caller and believe the warning is incorrect, you can continue with the call.

If you’re unsure about the caller’s identity:

  • End the call.
  • Contact the authentic person or organization directly using a trusted phone number, website, or previous conversation.
  • Do not share sensitive information until the caller’s identity is confirmed.

Report a suspicious caller

If you believe the caller is attempting to impersonate someone or engage in fraudulent activity:

  1. Select Screenshot: Calls buttonCalls in Teams.
  2. In History, select the call, and then select Screenshot: MoreMore.
  3. Select Report call (if available in your organization).
  4. Follow the prompts to submit your report.

Reporting suspicious calls helps your organization and Microsoft improve detection and protection capabilities.

If a legitimate caller is flagged

Detection systems continuously improve, but occasionally a legitimate caller may be identified as suspicious. If you know the caller is legitimate:

  • Continue using your organization’s normal verification processes.
  • Proceed only after you have confirmed the caller’s identity.
  • Provide feedback if your organization offers a mechanism to indicate that the warning was incorrect.

Best practices for staying safe

  • Verify unexpected requests through another communication channel.
  • Never share passwords or authentication codes during a call.
  • Be cautious of urgent requests involving money, credentials, or sensitive data.
  • Report suspicious activity when available.
  • Follow your organization’s security guidance.

Record a video or audio clip in Microsoft Teams

  • Desktop
  • iOS

In Teams, you can record up to a minute of video or audio and send it to people in one-on-one chats, group chats and channel discussions. They can watch the video or listen to the audio directly in the conversation.

Record a video clip using your camera

  1. Go to any one-on-one, group chat or channel discussion.

  2. Select Actions and appsScreenshot: Cross icon at top of the screen underneath where you type a message.

  3. Select Record a video clipScreenshot: Chat video clip button .

  4. Select Start recording to record. Screenshot: Screenshot of option to record a video clip in Microsoft Teams

    Tip

    You can pause and continue the recording as many times as you need.

  5. If desired, select Trim to trim your video clip by moving the sliders in the editing tool. Select Confirm trimScreenshot: checkmark to accept the changes. Screenshot: Screenshot of a video clip in Microsoft Teams with the option to trim the clip.

  6. When you’re done recording, select ContinueScreenshot: Continue icon in Microsoft Teams in the lower-right corner.

    Tip

    If you need to, you can record the video clip again by selecting the left arrow in the lower-left corner. You can choose to delete your previous recording or record more clips.

  7. Once processed, you’ll see your video where you type a message. Select SendScreenshot: Send icon to add it to the conversation.

Record a video clip from a screen

You can record things that happen on your screen, like walkthroughs and presentations, and send them to a chat or channel as a video clip.

  1. Go to any one-on-one, group chat or channel discussion.

  2. Select Actions and appsScreenshot: Cross icon at top of the screen underneath where you type a message.

  3. Select Record a video clipScreenshot: Chat video clip button .

  4. Select Screen, then select Start screen recording. Screenshot: Screenshot of the option to start screen recording in Microsoft Teams.

  5. On the next screen, choose the screen or window you want to record from and select Share.

    Note

    The recording will automatically end once it’s reached one minute long.

  7. Review your clips. If desired, select Trim to trim the clip by moving the sliders in the editing tool. Select Confirm trimScreenshot: checkmark to accept the changes.

  8. To send you recording, select ContinueScreenshot: Continue icon in Microsoft Teams in the lower-right corner. You can also select BackScreenshot: Icon for back in Microsoft Teams to make more edits or delete and start over.

Record an audio clip using your microphone

You can also record an audio only clip with your microphone to send in a chat.

  1. Go to any one-on-one, group chat or channel discussion.

Download and save your video, audio or transcript

  3. Select Download TranscriptScreenshot: Teams download arrow icon or Download videoScreenshot: Teams download arrow icon . The .mp4 file is in your Downloads folder.

Tip

Find your file in the download window that appears in the upper right corner of Microsoft Teams. Hover over the file name and select Screenshot: View in folder iconShow in folder to go directly to the downloads folder.

Turn closed captions on or off

Video clips shared in Teams have auto-generated captions. If you want to turn off the captions for a video clip you’re watching, select CaptionsScreenshot: The Closed Captions icon for Teams video clips . To turn them back on, select CaptionsScreenshot: The Closed Captions icon for Teams video clips again.

Record a video clip using your camera

Add background effects to your videos

  • No background to remove any background effects.

Report messages in Microsoft Teams

If you see a concerning chat or channel message with internal or external users in Teams, you can report it as either a security risk or inappropriate content.

Note

  • Depending on your organization, you may not be able to choose your reason for reporting the message, or you may not see the option to report a message. Check with your admin to confirm whether reporting is enabled.
  • Currently, if you’re using Copilot in Teams, you can’t report a message in the Copilot app.

To report a message

  1. Go to the chat or channel message and select More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > **Report this message.

  2. Choose the reason why you want to report the message. Reasons can include:

    • Security concern - spam, phishing, or malicious content 

    • Not a security concern - incorrectly identified as a concern

      Note

      • Selecting this option opens a text box where you can enter an optional explanation.
      • Only messages that have URL warnings can be reported as not a security concern.

    • Inappropriate - harassment, violence, nudity, or disturbing content

  3. Select Report. You’ll receive a message confirming your report was sent.

Save a chat or channel message in Microsoft Teams

Easily save chat messages and channel posts for later reference in Teams.

  • To save a message or post, hover over it and select More optionsScreenshot: Generic Ellipsis button > Save this messageScreenshot: Save message icon in Teams .
  • Once you have saved one or more messages, you’ll see a Saved section at the top of your list of chats and channels. This is where all your saved messages and posts appear.
  • Filter your saved items by selecting chats or channels under Saved.
  • To view a saved message in context, go to Saved and select the message. The chat or channel will open in a new pane, showing you the message or post within the chat or channel conversation.
  • To remove a post or message from Saved, hover over it, select More optionsScreenshot: Generic Ellipsis button > Unsave this message. You can also do this from the original chat or channel conversation.

Note

  • If you have no saved messages or posts, you will not see the Saved section.
  • If the author of the message edits the message after it’s saved, the saved message will reflect those edits.
  • If a message is deleted after it’s saved, the message title will still appear in the Saved section with the note Message has been deleted by author. Selecting the deleted message will still open the chat or channel so you can see the deleted message in context.

Search for chats and channels with the GoTo command

If you participate in many chats and channels, the GoTo command is a fast way to go directly to the chat or channel you want.

  1. In the Search box, type /, and select /goto.
  2. Select a chat or channel from the list or type a chat or channel name and press Enter.

Search your current location with Ctrl+F

Press Ctrl+F (cmd+F on macOS) to search messages within a particular chat or channel in Teams.

  1. Go to the area you want to search. Examples are a recent chat or a channel within a team.
  2. Press Ctrl+F, type your search term, then select GoScreenshot: arrow . Your results appear on the right, in Find in chat.
  3. Choose from the available results to jump to the item you want.

Search on desktop

Search for messages

  1. Type a keyword or a person’s name in the Search box. Teams returns results immediately.

  2. To filter results further, select Messages. Choose from the results to view the message.

  3. If your search doesn’t return what you’re looking for, select View all messages to see more results. The top results appear.

  4. Press Enter to see all results for that keyword or name.

  5. To search in more detail, choose the following:

    • Type: Choose to search in Chats or Channels.
    • Teams and channels: Start to type a name and suggested teams and channels are displayed for you to choose.
    • From: Type the name of the person who sent the message.
    • Date: Choose when the message was sent or add a date range to search.
    • More: Select More to filter @Mentions for your name, messages with attachments, or to hide messages about apps and bots.

Tip

For more detailed results, press Enter to filter messages by who sent them, when and where they were sent or if they have links or attachments.

Search for files

  1. Locate a file by typing its name or a keyword.

  2. To filter results further, select Files.

  3. If your search doesn’t produce what you’re looking for, select View all messages to see more results. The top results appear.

  4. To search in more detail, select the following:

    • Team: Type in a team name.
    • File Type: Choose the file type from the list.
    • Modified by: Type the name of the person who edited or changed the file.
    • Date: Choose when the message was sent or add a date range to search.
Search for group chats

  1. Locate a group chat by typing its name or a keyword.

  2. To filter results further, select Group Chats.

  3. If your search doesn’t produce what you’re looking for, select View all messages to see more results. The top results appear.

  4. To search in more detail, select the following:

    • Team: Type in a team name.
    • File Type: Choose the file type from the list.
    • Modified by: Type the name of the person who edited or changed the file.
    • Date: Choose when the message was sent or add a date range to sear ch.
Search for teams and channels
  1. Type the name of the team or channel in the Search box.
  2. Select Teams and Channels and then choose the result to go directly to that team or channel.
Search within a channel

Search keywords in channel discussions to quickly find the conversation you’re looking for. Glance at your search results as well as the channel interface in a single view, without leaving your workflow.

  1. In the Posts tab of any channel, select Open channel details in the top right corner.
  2. Select Find in channelScreenshot: Search button .
  3. Enter your keyword terms in the search bar, and select the arrow or Enter to search.
  4. You’ll see a preview of the search results appear. After selecting a search result, you will be taken to the specific message in the channel post.

Scoped search within Viva Connections

If your organization has Viva Connections set up, you can scope your search to results within your Connections experience.

Select the search box within Viva Connections. As you type, you’ll be provided with the option to “Search in Viva Connections” (or the name your organization chose for Connections), in addition to being able to search in Teams.

Select a search result to go to the corresponding Connections (or Teams) experience.

Note

Viva Connections is available to all Microsoft 365 or Office 365 enterprise plan users.

Optimize your search

Use search modifiers

For richer search results in messages, use KQL (Keyword Query Language). The following are the modifiers that Teams supports:

Note

Remember that there’s no space between the colon and the search terms.

  • From: Person’s name
  • In: Channel or group chat name
  • Subject: Keyword from a channel message with a subject line
  • Sent: Date
Search tips from the pros
  • Use an asterisk * to get results for any words with a matching prefix. Type the first few letters of a word followed immediately by an asterisk. For example, type “serv*” into the search box, and you’ll get results for all words that start with those four letters (for example, server and service).
  • Use quotation marks to search for an exact match on a word or phrase. Example: “annual budget”.
  • The search box also supports certain spell corrections and nickname matches when searching for people.

Note

For more info about using KQL, see the developer documentation at Keyword Query Language (KQL) syntax reference.

Search on a mobile device

  • Tap SearchScreenshot: Search button and enter a search term or phrase. Tap Messages, People or Files to narrow your results.

  • Desktop

When you’re in a chat, you can send messages that include files, pictures, and links.

Send a link

  1. To send a link, select FormatScreenshot: Teams format icon from beneath the message box.
  2. Then select Insert linkScreenshot: Link icon from the top of the message box.
  3. Add display text and the address, select Insert, or copy and paste the link into the message box, and then select SendScreenshot: Teams chat send button icon .

Or

  1. Copy a link.
  2. Select the text you want to link on and select Ctrl+V.

Note

  • Teams has its own ATP Safe Links security to verify that any link that you send or receive is safe to choose. As an added layer of protection, we’ll let you know about a potentially unsafe link.
  • Additionally, Teams may truncate long URLs for readability (e.g., https://www.example.com/very/long/link…). If you’d like to paste the full link without formatting or truncation, use paste without formatting: press Ctrl + Shift + V on Windows or Command + Shift + Option + V on Mac.

Attach a file or picture

  1. To include a file or picture in a chat or channel message, select Actions and appsScreenshot: Actions and apps button > Attach fileScreenshot: Teams assignment attach icon .
  2. Select from the list of recently opened files, or choose to Attach cloud filesScreenshot: Attach cloud files icon or Upload from this deviceScreenshot: 358ec935-76b6-477f-8c6d-5813b150ebec , depending on where your file is saved.

Messages with image, video and many types of document attachments will automatically include a preview of the attached files. Those with more than three attachments will include the preview after the message is sent. Messages containing a single PDF or 3D files (GLB, STIL, FBX, .OBJ) can be previewed inline. Select PreviewScreenshot: Play button to preview video to view the file directly within the chat or channel.

Note

  • If you don’t have permission to view the file or the file is encrypted using certain sensitivity labels, you won’t see a preview. However, you can request permission to access the file. Messages sent in chats with external users also won’t include file previews.
  • Certain file types, such as .zip files, can’t be previewed.

View links next to a chat

When you open a webpage link from a Teams chat while logged into Microsoft Edge, the chat window opens in the Edge browser to view the content and chat side-by-side. This makes it easy to view links without needing to switch back and forth between apps.

To learn more, see Web links from Outlook emails and Teams chats open in Microsoft Edge.

Send a link

Enter or paste a link into your message box.

Attach a picture

To attach a picture to a message, tap the Photo iconScreenshot: Take photo for windows icon next to the compose box to take a photo or to open your photo library.

Attach a file

To attach a file to a message, tap the Plus sign Screenshot: plus sign icon next to the compose box, select AttachScreenshot: Choose file icon beneath the message box and then go to the file location.

From a chat or meeting, tap the attachment to open it with a Microsoft 365 app. In a channel conversation, tap the attachment or go to Tabs > Files.

Send an emoji, GIF, or sticker in Microsoft Teams

  • Desktop
  • iOS
  • Android

Emoji, animated GIFs, and stickers are a great way to express yourself and add some fun to your chats. Browse galleries of trending GIFs, find your favorite sticker packs, and personalize your emoji skin tones – all in one place.

Your recently used emojis and reactions are synced across desktop and mobile.

Send an emoji, GIF or sticker

To insert an emoji, GIF or sticker in a chat or channel message:

  1. Select Emoji, GIFs and StickersScreenshot: Screenshot of Teams emoji for chat on the right side of the message box.
  2. From here, you can search for a specific emoji, GIF, or sticker, or navigate through the galleries above the search bar.
  3. Select the emoji, GIF, or sticker that you want from the gallery.
  4. Once you’ve selected the item you want, it will appear in the chat compose box. When you’re finished, select SendScreenshot: Teams chat send button icon .

Send a quick reaction

Say more, more quickly, with quick reactions. Hover over a message and select the one you want. Then watch it appear in the lower-left corner of the message.

Select More reactionsScreenshot: 337174f0-bc44-417b-93c2-6e8fdc21cfb7 to choose from a full list of reactions. Repeat the process to add up to 20 reactions per message.

Go to Like or react to messages in Microsoft Teams to learn more about reactions.

Screenshot: Screenshot showing quick reaction emoji above a chat message

Insert an emoji with a keyboard shortcut

  1. In the compose box, type : and start typing the emoji name (for example, :smile:) to filter suggestions.
  2. Select the emoji from the suggestion list or press Enter to insert the top match.

Personalize your emoji

Some emoji—those that include a gray dot in the corner—can be personalized for different skin tones. Just right-click on any emoji with a gray dot to open a series of variations for that emoji, and choose the one that you want to send.

Screenshot: Screenshot showing how to change your emoji skin tone

Customize a meme or sticker

Some memes and stickers can be customized with your own captions.

  1. Find a meme or sticker that has an edit icon in the lower right corner.
  2. Click the meme or sticker, type your (hilarious) caption in the text box, and select Done.
  3. Your customized meme or sticker will appear in the chat box. Now all you have to do is select SendScreenshot: Teams chat send button icon .

Screenshot: Screenshot showing memes and stickers in the fun picker

Add an emoji

To add an emoji to a message, tap EmojiScreenshot: Smile emoji icon beneath the box, choose an emoji gallery including Smilies, Hand gestures, People, Animals, Food, Travel and places, Objects, Activities, and Symbols, and then choose the emoji that you want to send.

Even more fun and expressiveness is here with an expanded selection of over 800 emojis over nine galleries that introduce a wide range of diversity and representation. Select the emoji that fits your mood with a new gallery selector, skin tone selector, and shortcode picker.

Add a reaction

To add an emoji reaction, tap and hold the message you’d like to add a reaction to. Then, tap the reaction you want, and watch it appear in the upper-right corner of the message. Repeat the process to add up to 20 reactions per message.

Go to Like or react to messages in Microsoft Teams to learn more about reactions.

Add a GIF

To add an animated GIF to a message or a channel conversation, just select GIFScreenshot: GIF icon in Teams beneath the box. Use the search bar at the top of the window to look for something specific (like “cats playing piano”) or browse the collection of popular GIFs.

To add custom memes or stickers, use the desktop or web app.

Add an emoji

To add an emoji to a message, tap EmojiScreenshot: Smile emoji icon beneath the box, choose an emoji gallery including Smilies, Hand gestures, People, Animals, Food, Travel and places, Objects, Activities, and Symbols, and then choose the emoji that you want to send.

Even more fun and expressiveness is here with an expanded selection of over 800 emojis over nine galleries that introduce a wide range of diversity and representation. Select the emoji that fits your mood with a new gallery selector, skin tone selector, and shortcode picker.

Add a reaction

To add an emoji reaction, tap and hold the message you’d like to add a reaction to. Then, select the reaction you want, and watch it appear in the upper-right corner of the message. Repeat the process to add up to 20 reactions per message.

Go to Like or react to messages in Microsoft Teams to learn more about reactions.

Add a GIF

To add an animated GIF to a message or a channel conversation, just select GIFScreenshot: GIF icon in Teams beneath the box. Use the search bar at the top of the window to look for something specific (like “cats playing piano”) or browse the collection of popular GIFs.

To add custom memes or stickers, use the desktop or web app.

Send and read messages in Microsoft Teams

  • Desktop
  • Mobile

Chat makes it easy to send and read messages, so you can quickly share info with your teammates.

Send a message

  1. Select New messageScreenshot: Chat icon in Teams. at the top of the app.
  2. Type the name or names into the To box at the top of your new chat.
  3. Compose your message in the box at the bottom of the chat. To open your formatting options, select FormatScreenshot: Format button in Teams to the right of the message text.
  4. When you’re ready, select SendScreenshot: Send a message icon. . Everyone who has access to the chat can see your message.

Send more messages

Once the chat starts (either in a group or one-on-one), choose it to open it and send more messages.

Edit or delete a sent message

  1. To delete a message you’ve sent in a chat, open the chat, and find the message you want to delete.
  2. Select More optionsScreenshot: More options button > DeleteScreenshot: Delete button . The message disappears, and in its place, you’ll see an Undo button.
  3. To edit a message, hover over the message, then select EditScreenshot: Teams edit button . Edit your message as needed and select DoneScreenshot: Teams confirm message edit .

Mark a message as unread

If you want to remember to read a message later, you can mark it as unread. Go to the top of the message and select More OptionsScreenshot: More options button > Mark as unread.

Say more with a reaction

You can quickly respond to any message with an emoji reaction. For the full set, hover over a message and select the one you want. Then, watch it appear in the upper-right corner of the message.

To customize your default reactions, and for more about emoji, see Send an emoji, GIF, or sticker in Microsoft Teams.

Improve message readability

If you need to translate or read text out loud, try the following options:

  • Translate a message
  • Use Immersive Reader

Send a message

Tap ChatScreenshot: 585608f5-11ce-4851-a9d5-d3fd68a928e5 > New messageScreenshot: New chat button and type the name of the person or people you want to chat with. Then compose your message and tap SendScreenshot: Send button .

When you receive a message, there are several actions you can take on that message.

Mark a message as unread or saved

If you want to remember to read a message later, you can mark it as unread or saved. For chat messages, press and hold the message and select Save this message or Mark as unread.

Add an emoji reaction to a message

You can quickly respond to any message with an emoji reaction. Tap and hold the message you’d like to add a reaction to. Then, select the reaction you want, and watch it appear in the upper-right corner of the message.

Send code snippets in a message in Microsoft Teams

Important

You’ll no longer be able to create code snippets after May 30, 2025, but you can still use those that are already created. To send code in a chat or channel, use code blocks.

To send a code snippet in a chat or channel message:

  1. In the message box, select FormatScreenshot: Expand button .

  2. Choose Code snippetScreenshot: Code snippet button to reveal the space to place your code snippet.

  3. Add your code and create a title for the snippet. Select the option next to Wrap text if you want your text to wrap. Then, select the drop-down to choose your programming language.

  4. Select Cancel or Insert to add the snippet to your message.

    Screenshot: Screenshot showing expanded code snippet box

Syntax highlighting and auto-indentation help you write your code the way you want. When you send your snippet, it’s included in the message as a card, and the recipient can view it inline with the syntax highlighting intact.

Tip

Use your keyboard to add a code block by typing /code in the compose box then press Enter. See Use commands in Microsoft Teams for more keyboard shortcuts.

To edit your code snippet after you’ve sent it, select More optionsScreenshot: More options button > EditScreenshot: Edit button on your message, then EditScreenshot: Edit button again on the snippet card.

Send messages to Skype for Business users from Microsoft Teams

  • Desktop
  • Mobile

Coexistence and interoperability between Teams and Skype for Business are determined by TeamsUpgrade modes. Everyone using Skype for Business is assigned a TeamsUpgrade mode, either by default or by their admin.

If someone has been assigned a coexistence mode, they’ll be able to receive messages you send them from within Teams. Search for them in Teams, type your message, and then send it. You’ll see a Skype for Business icon next to the chat in your chat list.

For more info about TeamsUpgrade modes, see Coexistence with Skype for Business.

Group chat with Skype for Business users

Group messages can’t be sent to people using Skype for Business. However, whenever someone invites you to a group conversation from Skype for Business, you’ll get a notification in Teams. You’ll then be able to join the conversation back in Skype for Business.

Skype for Business vs. Teams

Being able to chat with someone on Skype for Business from within Teams is great, but you’ll miss out on fun things like emoji, file attachments, and tabs.

Turn off Skype for Business

You can’t completely turn off the integration with Skype for Business. However, if you want to turn off the chat option, talk to your IT admin.

Note

If your IT admin turns off chat, you’ll still see all your Skype for Business meetings but you won’t be able to chat with Skype for Business users.

If you want to chat one-on-one with someone who’s using Skype for Business, you can do that from the mobile app. And while that’s great, keep in mind that you’ll be missing out on fun things like emoji, file attachments, and tabs.

Creating group chats with people who use Skype for Business isn’t available yet.

Send Praise to people in Microsoft Teams

Send acclaim to your employees and coworkers with Praise. Deliver in a chat, or for wider recognition, send it in a channel conversation.

  • Desktop
  • Mobile

To praise someone on your team:

  1. Select ChatScreenshot: teams-chat-tab-icon in Teams.

  2. Open the chat conversation with the person you want to praise.

  3. Select Actions and appsScreenshot: Plus sign icon > PraiseScreenshot: Praise icon in the chat compose box.

    Screenshot: Screenshot showing how to send praise to someone in a chat

  4. Titles default to Awesome. To send a different title with your praise message, select a new one from the Title section. Scroll to the right to find more options.

  5. Add an optional note of up to 500 characters.

    Screenshot: test

  6. Select Preview.

  7. Once it’s ready to go, select Send.

To praise someone on your team:

  1. Next to the compose box for a new message or reply, tap More optionsScreenshot: The Plus button in Teams> PraiseScreenshot: Praise icon .
  2. Choose a badge.
  3. Add recipient(s), and then tap the note area to add a note.
  4. Tap next.
  5. Once it’s ready to go, select Send.

Share a contact in a chat or channel

Contact sharing in Microsoft Teams lets you quickly and easily share contact information with other people. This is useful when introducing or providing contact details to a colleague.

When you share one or more contacts, their contact card’s included in the message. Your organization determines what’s included on that contact card. To learn more, see Profile cards in Microsoft 365.

Share a contact:

  1. In the compose box of a chat or channel, type @.
  2. Select Share someone’s contact info. Enter the name of the person whose contact info you want to share. You can share one or more contacts.
  3. Select OK. This will share a link to the person’s contact card. Unlike a @mention, sharing a contact doesn’t notify the person.

Screenshot: Screenshot showing how to pull up a contact to share using @mention.Screenshot: Screenshot showing a contact ready to share in the compose box.

Select the shared name to open the contact’s profile in Teams. From there, view more information, such as their job title, department, and location. You can also send a message to the contact, or start a video call with them.

Note

You can only share contacts with people who are in your organization.

Share a link to a specific message

Group chat members can easily share a link to a specific message, enabling them to quickly navigate to that message and find relevant information. This feature also enables group chat members to start a separate chat with anyone from the original group for a deeper dive into the topic.

  1. Hover over the message and select More optionsScreenshot: Three asterisks indicating more options menu > Copy link.
  2. After the link is copied, you can paste it in the same Teams chat, in another Teams chat or channel, in email, or in any other window.

Other group chat members can click the message link, which takes them to the specific message in the conversation history. The shared message will now be highlighted. If the message has been deleted, anyone trying to open it will receive a notification bar at the top of their screen.

Anyone not in the original group chat will not be able to access the chat message.

Tip

If you want to copy the contents of a message in Teams, see Copy and paste in messages in Microsoft Teams.

Share your screen in a chat in Microsoft Teams

You can share what’s on your screen while in a chat without sharing your video or audio.

  1. Select More chat optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon in the upper-right corner, then select Screen sharingScreenshot: Teams Share icon . Screenshot: Share your screen in a MS Teams chat

    Note

    Linux users can’t share screens in a Teams chat at this time.

  2. Choose the screen you’d like to share or select Window to select from open programs.

Other chat participants will receive a notification to accept your screen share. Once they do, they’ll be able to see your screen and continue the chat.

Tip

Screen sharing opens a muted call. Unmute the call or turn on your camera while screen sharing to start an instant meeting.

End your screen share

  1. Go to your meeting controls and select Stop sharing.
  2. Go to the meeting call window and select Leave.

Note

If you’ve shared your screen in a group chat and you’re not the last person to leave, it won’t end. You can rejoin by opening the group chat and selecting Join. When the last person leaves the call, the meeting has ended.

Show chat info in Microsoft Teams

To see chat details, select Open Chat detailsScreenshot: Chat info pane icon. in the top right corner of a chat. A pane showing a member list, pinned posts, and shared links and files will open to the right of the chat. You can also select Find in chatScreenshot: Search magnifying glass button to search within the chat. To close the pane, select Close chat detailsScreenshot: Close pane image .

Screenshot: Screenshot of how to reveal a chat info pane that includes a list of 3 people, 1 pinned message, and 1 shared document.

Note

The chat details are available for one-on-one, group and meeting chats.

People

The People section shows up to seven members of the chat and their current status. To start a chat with someone, simply select their name. Select See all to show everyone in the chat.

Pinned messages

The Pinned messages section lists up to 10 pinned messages for everyone to see. You’ll also see the most recently pinned message as a banner at the top of the chat.

Tip

To pin a message, select More options at the top right corner of the message and select Pin.

Shared

In the Shared section, you’ll find a list of all the files and links that have been shared in the chat. To open one, just click on it. Select More options on the right to copy, download or view files and links in the chat. Select See all to see links and files in a separate shared tab.

Translate a message in Microsoft Teams

  • Desktop
  • Mobile

When you receive a message in another language, you have the option to translate it into your preferred language. You can also choose to have incoming messages automatically translated. A translated message will have an icon above it to let you know it’s been translated.

Translate a message

To translate a message, select Translate above the message.

Disable translation suggestions by selecting Never translate (language) above the message.

Screenshot: Choose to translate or never translate messages.

If you don’t see the “Translate” suggestion, you can still request translation. Translate any message to your default language by hovering above the message and selecting More optionsScreenshot: More options button > TranslationScreenshot: Teams translate message icon >TranslateScreenshot: Teams translate message icon

Automatically translate messages

If desired, Teams can automatically translate received messages. To turn on automatic translations:

  • Hover over a message that was originally in another language and select More optionsScreenshot: More options button .

Screenshot: Hover over a message to reveal more options.

  • Select TranslationScreenshot: Teams translate message icon , then select Turn on auto-translation.Screenshot: Select more options to turn on auto-translations

To turn off automatic translations:

  • Select Translation optionsScreenshot: Teams translate message icon above the message

Screenshot: Select translation options over a translated message to reveal more options.

  • Select SettingsScreenshot: Settings button , then go to Translation to change your translation settings.

Note

  • Automatic translation settings are based on the language. You can choose to translate some languages while not translating others. We won’t offer to translate any language you’ve added to the Never translate list.
  • Automatic translation is not supported for short messages.

Change your translation settings

To access your translation settings:

  • Go to Settings and moreScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > SettingsScreenshot: Settings button > GeneralScreenshot: Settings button > Translation

To update your settings:

  • Select Translate messages into this language to choose the language you want messages to be translated into.

  • Choose How to handle messages in other languages:

Ask me before translating

See translation suggestions and decide if you want to translate individual messages.

Auto-translate all messages

Messages received in other languages are automatically translated.

Never translate

This option disables translation suggestions.

  • Select Never translate messages in these languages to exclude certain languages from translation suggestions and automatic translation.

Note

Translation suggestions and automatic translation features are only available for messages in Chat.

Give feedback on translations

Improve translation results by sharing feedback. To give feedback, click Translation optionsScreenshot: Teams translate message icon > Give feedbackScreenshot: Teams on Windows 11 Chat give feedback button .

Screenshot: Give feedback to Teams about translation results.

Note

If you don’t see the translate option in Teams, contact your IT admin to make sure that it’s turned on.

Use code blocks in Microsoft Teams

Code blocks let you share and edit code within the compose box of Microsoft Teams. You can use code blocks to share any kind of code, like Java, Python, or Bash.

Code blocks created on desktop render on mobile with line numbers, syntax highlighting, and automatic text wrapping, allowing you to clearly view code. Code blocks can only be created on desktop.

Insert a code block

You can add a code block to your message in a few different ways:

  • Slash Command: Type /code in the compose box.
  • Keyboard Shortcut: Select Ctrl + Shift + Alt + B on Windows and web. Select Cmd + Shift + Option + B on Mac.
  • Markdown: Type three backticks (\0`) in the compose box.

You can also select Show Formatting optionsScreenshot: teams-format-icon in the compose box, then select Code BlockScreenshot: teams-code-block-button-icon .

Select a language

  1. Once you insert a code block, select the dropdown to choose your language (such as Python or Plain Text) from the list of languages.

    Note

    There’s no need to choose a language every time you share code. Code Block remembers the last language you used.

  2. The code block will format the code using syntax highlighting based on the chosen language.

    Tip

    If the syntax highlighting isn’t working, check that you’ve selected the right language for your code.

Write and edit code

Write and edit code directly in the compose box. Once you’re done, select Send to send the message.

Note

Anyone can copy the code directly from a sent message.

Wrap text

If your code has long lines, you can wrap the text. This keeps the code block from getting too wide. To wrap text, select More optionsScreenshot: microsoft-teams-more-options-icon-001 inside the code block. Then select Wrap text under Display option in the code block.

Make it collaborative

Turn your code block into a Loop component before sending it so anyone in the chat can edit it.

  1. Before sending the code, select More optionsScreenshot: microsoft-teams-more-options-icon-001 inside the code block.
  2. Select Make this collaborative.

Note

  • You’ll only see the option to make it collaborative before sending the code block. If you’re having trouble with collaborative editing, make sure everyone has the necessary permissions to edit Loop components.
  • If you paste code that has more than 30,000 characters into a code block, it will be converted to a collaborative code block. This allows you and others to see all the code you want to share while maintaining syntax highlighting.

Use collaborative notes in Microsoft Teams chats

Collaborative notes make it easy to stay on the same page in one-on-one chat or group chats. You can create agendas, share ideas, and track tasks—all without leaving the chat. Notes update in real time, so everyone sees changes instantly.

Collaborative notes are powered by Loop components. They let you:

  • Add an agenda for your team.
  • Take notes together.
  • Assign tasks to people right in the chat.

Everything stays in one place, so you don’t have to switch apps or copy information later.

Start a new note in a group chat

  1. Open your group chat in Teams.
  2. At the top right of the chat window, select the Open notesScreenshot: Teams collaborative notes icon icon.
  3. Start typing: add agenda items, notes, or tasks.

Tip

Use @mentions to assign tasks. The person you tag will see it in their To Do and Planner apps.

To close the notes window, select the same icon (Close notes). Your notes will remain there until you edit or delete them.

Note

  • Collaborative notes are available in Teams group chats on desktop and web.
  • External guests can’t edit notes.
  • Notes sync across Microsoft 365 apps, so updates show everywhere.

Use commands in Microsoft Teams

Slash commands are keyboard shortcuts for performing common tasks in Teams. Use them to quickly access apps, manage conversations, update your status, add details to your messages, and join or leave meetings.

Note

Slash commands are currently unavailable in Teams for mobile.

Use slash commands

To use slash commands:

  • Type / in the search box at the top of Teams. Select a command from the list and press Enter.
  • Type / in a chat compose box. Select a command from the list and press Enter or Tab.

The following table shows available commands, what they do, and where you can use them.

  • /apps
    • Add an app
  • /available
    • Set status to available
  • /away
    • Set status to away
  • /brb
    • Set status to be right back
  • /busy
    • Set status to busy
  • /chat
    • Send a quick message
  • /code
    • Insert a code block
  • /createworkflow
    • Set up a workflow
  • /dnd
    • Set status to do not disturb
  • /gif
    • Insert a GIF
  • /goto
    • Go to a chat or channel
  • /hide
    • Hide the current chat
  • /hidelivecaptions
    • Turn live captions off
  • /leavechat
    • Leave the current chat
  • /loop
    • Insert a Loop paragraph
  • /meetnow
    • Start or join a quick meeting
  • /mute
    • Mute the current chat
  • /notifications
    • Manage channel notifications
  • /offline
    • Set your status offline
  • /participants
    • See participants in current chat/channel
  • /record
    • Record a video clip
  • /reset
    • Reset your status
  • /schedulemessage
    • Schedule a message
  • /settings
    • Open settings
  • /shortcuts
    • Open keyboard shortcuts
  • /showlivecaptions
    • Turn live captions on
  • /starttranscription
    • Start meeting transcription
  • /stoplivetranscription
    • Stop meeting transcription
  • /unmute
    • Unmute current chat
  • /window
    • Open in a new window
  • /Github, /Youtube, /Jira, etc.
    • Commands for installed apps
  • Your recent commands will stay at the top of your menu. To explore other commands, type / in the search or compose boxes.
  • Commands are available to everyone using Teams. However, you might see additional commands depending on where you use them.
  • Some commands may be unavailable due to policies set by your org.

Use /goto command

The /goto command helps you navigate chats or channels from the search bar or as a keyboard shortcut.

From the search bar

  1. Click the search bar at the top of Teams.
  2. Type /goto followed by the name of the chat or channel you want to access. Or you can select one of the options from the drop-down menu that appears.
  3. Press Enter to jump directly to your destination.

Use the keyboard shortcut

  1. Press Ctrl+G to activate “Go to” mode.
  2. Start typing the name of your chat or channel. Or you can select one of the options from the drop-down menu that appears.
  3. Select your destination from the suggestions and press Enter.

Use Custom Emoji in Microsoft Teams

Create and communicate with user-uploaded emoji in Microsoft Teams. These custom emoji help build culture and identity, reinforce branding, provide tone, and add clarity to messages. Share custom emoji with anyone in the organization, including external users in shared channels.

Your recently used emojis and reactions are synced across desktop and mobile.

Create a custom emoji

Users can create custom emoji from an image or GIF file for anyone in their organization to use as reactions and emoji.

Note

Admins may limit who can create custom emoji before they can be used. Additionally, anyone can right click on any custom emoji to see who created it and when.

To create a custom emoji:

  1. Select Emoji, GIFs and StickersScreenshot: Teams emoji icon for chat on the right side of the message box, then choose Emoji.

  2. At the bottom, you’ll see various emoji options. Select Your org’s emoji Screenshot: Access your orgs emoji options.** .**

  3. On the left, select Add emojiScreenshot: plus button to choose any image or GIF file. Then create a name for your emoji. Screenshot: Select the plus sign to add custom emoji.

    Note

    When selecting emoji to upload, follow these guidelines:

    • Upload JPEG, PNG, or GIF files.
    • We recommend using square images.
    • Images will be compressed; select files under 256K.

  4. Select Add emojiScreenshot: plus button to include it in the list of custom emoji.

You can also add emoji when reacting to a message. To do so, hover over the text you’d like to react to. Then select More reactionsScreenshot: 337174f0-bc44-417b-93c2-6e8fdc21cfb7 > Your org’s emojiScreenshot: Access your orgs emoji options. to choose your file and create your emoji.

Tip

Create custom reactions to help identify status or categorize responses during multi-step processes. For example, create unique emoji for each of your team members to show participation in collaborative projects. Or try using custom emoji to signify completion of specific processes. Learn more about liking or reacting to messages.

Choose a custom emoji

Use custom emoji in channel, chat, and meeting messages, and replies. You can also use them to react to existing messages.

To choose a custom emoji:
  1. Select Emoji, GIFs and StickersScreenshot: Teams emoji icon for chat on the right side of the message box, then choose Emoji.
  2. Select Your org’s emojiScreenshot: Access your orgs emoji options. from the bottom right corner to browse custom emoji options. You can also search all emoji options from the Emoji tab at the top. Screenshot: Search all emoji options.
  3. Select the emoji to add it to your message. Repeat the process to add additional emoji.

Tip

Any custom emoji or reaction that you’ve created will always show up at the top. Find recently used emoji by selecting Recent on the bottom left corner of Emoji, GIFs and StickersScreenshot: Teams emoji icon for chat .

To react with a custom emoji, hover over the text you’d like to react to. Then, select More reactionsScreenshot: 337174f0-bc44-417b-93c2-6e8fdc21cfb7 to search for the emoji.

Tip

Celebrate team accomplishments and shared experiences with custom reactions and emoji celebrating birthdays, work anniversaries, launches and events.

Delete a custom emoji

Note

Teams admins may limit who can delete custom emoji.

If you’re able to delete a custom emoji, you’ll see the option when you right-click on it.

  • To delete the emoji, select Delete. Then confirm your choice.

Deleting it will immediately remove it from your list. However, it may take a few days to no longer appear to everyone.

Tip

Still seeing a deleted emoji? Try clearing your cache to instantly remove it.
