Use Markdown formatting in Microsoft Teams

  • Desktop
  • Mobile

With Markdown, you get a live preview of your formatted text inside your compose box as you type, and you can always undo your formatting by pressing Ctrl+Z. These actions are also available by expanding your compose box.

Note

Teams uses a Markdown-style syntax. While we refer to it as “Markdown,” it doesn’t fully match standard Markdown, and some formatting may behave differently.

Available markdown actions in Teams

  • Bold text
    • Action: *bold text*
    • Example: bold text
  • Italic text
    • Action: _italic text_
    • Example: italic text
  • Strikethrough
    • Action: ~strikethrough~
  • Numbered list
    • Action: 0 Item one
    • Example: 1. Item one 2. Item two
  • Unordered list
    • Action: * Item one OR - Item one
    • Example: · Item one · Item two
  • Hyperlink
    • Action: [Text](URL)
    • Example: Here’s a link.
  • Multi-line code block
    • Action: \0`[code block]
  • Inline block of code
    • Action: \0
  • Heading 1
    • Action: # Header text
  • Heading 2
    • Action: ## Header text
  • Heading 3
    • Action: ### Header text
  • BlockQuote
    • Action: >

Use Markdown to share inline code

Markdown with inline code lets you highlight specific code snippets in a paragraph. This makes it easier to find and understand the code in the paragraph.

Screenshot: Screenshot of inline code in a Microsoft Teams chat

To add an inline block of code (monospace), start and end the text with a backtick (`) key. This is located next to the 1 on your keyboard, followed by a space. You can also use one of the following alternate keys to start an inline code block:

  • Shift+`+Space
  • Shift+Alt+´
  • The keyboard manager, Ukelele.

After selecting one of these keys, type your code and then press the same key again to end the code block.

Use Markdown to share a block of code

To add a multi-line block of code, preface your text with \0` and then paste it into your compose box. You’ll get a live preview of your code, and you can undo any formatting by hitting Ctrl+Z. To learn more, read Use code blocks in Microsoft Teams.

For now, you can view but not generate Markdown-formatted messages on your mobile device. Use the desktop or web app to collaborate and share code.

Use read receipts for messages in Microsoft Teams

  • Desktop
  • Mobile

Want to know if people have read or seen messages you’ve sent? Use read receipts. When they read your message the SeenScreenshot: Read receipt icon in Teams confirmation appears next to it. Otherwise, you’ll only see a confirmation that your message was sent Screenshot: Delivered message icon in Teams .

Note

By default, Read receipts are on for everyone. Your admin decides whether you have this feature and the ability to turn it off.

What counts as someone having read your message?

  • Everyone must have read receipts turned on If you’re chatting with someone who has it turned off or someone who’s outside your org, you won’t see read receipts from that person.
  • Activity in the chat window marks a message as a read receipt You won’t get a read receipt if someone sees your message in a notification or in the Activity feed. Or, if they see or respond from a banner notification. You’ll only get a read receipt if someone is active in the chat and responded there.

What doesn’t trigger a read receipt?

As previously mentioned, a message will have a read receipt only if the recipient is active in the chat window. Read receipts won’t mark a message as seen if viewed from a quick entry point like someone’s profile or a banner notification.

Turn on or turn off read receipts

To see or change this option, select Settings and moreScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon next to your profile at the top of Teams, and then select Screenshot: Settings gear iconSettings > Chats and channels. From there, turn on or off Read receipts.

Important

Your admin decides whether you can turn this setting off.

See who’s read your message in a group chat

The Read by option shows who’s seen your message in a group chat of 20 people or fewer. When everyone has read your text, the SeenScreenshot: Read receipt icon in Teams confirmation appears next to your message.

Screenshot: Read receipts who read

To see who’s read your message, go to that message in a group chat, and select More optionsScreenshot: Format icon in Teams. > Read by. Everyone with a read receipt confirmation appears in the list.

Note

When you use a Loop component, everyone has the ability to view who’s editing it. To learn more about using a Loop component in Microsoft Teams, read the following help article: Send a Loop component in Teams chat.

To see or change this option, select your profile picture at the top of the app, then select Settings > General. From there, turn on or off Read receipts.

Copilot in Teams

Catch up on meetings with Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams

How to use Copilot in a meeting

Copilot summarizes key discussion points, including who spoke and what they said. It also suggests action items and answers any questions you have, in real time during or after a meeting.

Note

  • Transcription isn’t required for turning on Copilot in a meeting. However, to prompt Copilot about the meeting or see Copilot’s conversation history after the meeting ends, make sure to turn on live transcription during the meeting.
  • Copilot won’t work in meetings that are hosted outside the participant’s organization.
Set up meetings with Copilot

As a meeting organizer, you can decide how and if participants can use Copilot. Even if you don’t have a license, you’re in control of Copilot for meetings you organize.

Depending on your org’s policy, sensitivity label, and template settings, you can choose from the following values for the Allow Copilot and Facilitator meeting option.

This setting is available in the meeting scheduler under Screenshot: Settings buttonOnline meeting options > Copilot and other AI.

  • During and after the meeting
    • Copilot actions available: Transcription is required to use Copilot. Copilot starts as soon as someone in the meeting begins transcribing. Stopping transcription will also stop Copilot. Selecting Copilot in the meeting controls will send a prompt to start transcription; confirming will start Copilot and transcription for the meeting.
  • Only during the meeting
    • Copilot actions available: Copilot starts as soon as it’s selected in the meeting controls. Copilot uses speech-to-text data to provide insights about what is said in the meeting. If someone starts transcribing the meeting, Copilot will be available during and after the meeting for portions that were transcribed. After the meeting ends, speech-to-text data that wasn’t transcribed and interactions with Copilot will no longer be available. Selecting Copilot in the meeting controls will send a prompt to select the correct spoken language for the speech-to-text data; confirming will start Copilot for the meeting.
  • Off
    • Copilot actions available: Copilot is disabled for the meeting. Recording and transcription are also disabled for the meeting to prevent Microsoft 365 Copilot from accessing any sensitive information that may have been shared.
Have a more effective meeting

Copilot helps you stay on track by reasoning over the discussion and meeting chat to answer to your questions about the meeting. Select Screenshot: Copilot IconCopilot from the meeting controls to start your private chat with Copilot.

Select Screenshot: view-prompts-copilot-iconView prompts in the Screenshot: Copilot IconCopilot pane to see prompt suggestions or ask Copilot questions of your own using the compose box. Here are some ideas:

  • Where do we disagree on this topic?

  • How did [a meeting participant] respond to this proposal?

  • What questions can I ask to move the meeting forward?

  • Where are some holes in [a meeting participant’s] argument?

  • Create a table with the ideas discussed and their pros and cons.

  • List the ideas, including people’s feedback, from transcript and chat.

Visit the Copilot Prompt Gallery to explore more prompts and learn about how to get the most out of Copilot.

If you join a meeting more than 5 minutes after it started and Copilot is active, Copilot will send a notification offering to catch you up. Select Open Copilot and wait for the summary to generate on the right side of your meeting window.

While using the Teams desktop app, select Screenshot: Help Pop out buttonOpen private Copilot in new window to pop out the Screenshot: Copilot IconCopilot pane into a new window and multitask during your meeting.

Edit Copilot’s responses in Word or Excel

Copilot in Teams for meetings can help your team get started on important documents that can be exported to Word or Excel for further collaboration.

  • If Copilot’s response is over 1300 characters, select Screenshot: Microsoft Word app logoOpen in Word to open Copilot in Teams’ response in Word.
  • If Copilot’s response is formatted as a table, select Screenshot: Microsoft Excel app logoOpen in Excel to open Copilot in Teams’ table in Excel.

If you added a sensitivity label to your meeting that doesn’t allow participants to export content from the meeting, you can’t export Copilot’s responses to Word or Excel.

If you turned on the meeting option Turn off copying and forwarding of meeting chat, live captions, and transcripts, you can’t export Copilot’s responses to Word or Excel.

How to use Copilot after a meeting

You can access Copilot after the meeting from the meeting chat and from the Recap tab. To ask questions about what was said in the meeting after it ends, there must be a meeting transcript available.

From the meeting chat

Copilot provides comprehensive information and insights using what was written in the chat and spoken content captured in the meeting transcript, if one is available.

To get started, select Screenshot: Copilot IconOpen Copilot in the upper-right corner of the chat. Then, send a prompt in the compose box. For example, asking “What ideas were discussed?” results in a response that incorporates ideas shared out loud and in the chat. Copilot’s response will also cite which sources were used to provide the answer.

Screenshot: copilot entry from meeting chat

Before the meeting starts, you can use Copilot in the meeting chat thread, just like any other chat. If someone starts transcription in the meeting, Copilot will include chat data from up to 24 hours before the meeting along with the transcript. As long as the transcript is available, Copilot can use both chat and transcript as sources in the meeting chat.

Note

  • If Allow Copilot is set to Only during the meeting and no transcript was started, Copilot in the meeting chat will only include information from the chat.
  • If Allow Copilot is set to Off, Copilot in the meeting chat will still be available and only include information from the chat.
From the Recap tab

If transcription was turned on during the meeting, Copilot can also be accessed from the Recap tab in the meeting chat. Open Screenshot: Copilot IconCopilot to see the same conversation history with Copilot as the one accessed from the meeting chat. ​​​​

Important

Any previous conversation history with Copilot in a recurring meeting will no longer be available if a later meeting in the series is transcribed. If the transcript from a transcribed meeting is no longer available, Copilot will be unavailable and all previous conversation history with Copilot will be removed.

Screenshot: Copilot in meeting recap revised

Note

  • Intelligent recap is available as part of Teams Premium, an add-on license that provides additional features to make Teams meetings more personalized, intelligent, and secure. To get access to Teams Premium, contact your IT admin.
  • Intelligent recap is also available as part of the Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

Facilitator in Microsoft Teams meetings

The Facilitator agent works within Teams meetings for more effective collaboration, including the following features:

  • Generates real-time AI-generated notes during meetings, allowing everyone to co-author and collaborate seamlessly.
  • Summarizes key decisions and open questions from meeting discussion.
  • Answers open-ended questions in the meeting chat from the meeting participants.
  • Documents insights from the meeting discussion.
  • Checks for a meeting agenda from the meeting invite and the meeting notes Loop component and then send the agenda in the meeting chat so all participants are aware of the topics to be discussed.
  • Prompts participants to define meeting goals if no agenda is detected.
  • Helps the discussion stay on agenda and on time by showing topics in an agenda timer with time allocations and marking when a discussion has started for a topic.
  • Manages time by starting and showing a countdown timer to all participants, alerting participants when the timer ends to help the meeting stay on track.
  • Alerts participants when the meeting runs over the scheduled end time and help participants schedule necessary follow-up meetings.
  • @mentions absent participants in the meeting chat when they’ve been mentioned multiple times during the meeting.

Important

A Microsoft 365 Copilot license is required to add Facilitator to a meeting or turn it on during a meeting. However, any meeting participant (excluding external participants) can see all real-time updates in Chat and Notes.

The following Facilitator agent features are available as part of the public preview program and might undergo further changes before being released publicly.

  • Ask Facilitator to create a loop or word document based on the conversation.
  • Ask Facilitator to help manage your tasks by @mentioning Facilitator to create, update, or query for tasks related to that meeting.
  • Tasks created by Facilitator will automatically sync to a meeting plan associated with that meeting instance.

To get access to these and other upcoming features, switch to Teams public preview.

Note

To prompt Facilitator about the meeting after it ends, make sure to turn on transcription before or during the meeting. If Copilot is set to start without transcription, Facilitator will start without transcription as well.

Add Facilitator to a meeting when scheduling

Note

Facilitator can only be added to scheduled meetings, and can’t be added to channel meetings, instant meetings, or Teams calls.

To add Facilitator when scheduling a meeting:

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: teams-calendar-tab-icon in Teams.
  2. Select NewScreenshot: Calendar icon with plus sign .
  3. Turn on the Teams meeting toggle.
  4. Select OptionsScreenshot: skype-teams-mobile-icon-settings > Copilot and other AIScreenshot: copilot-icon .
  5. Make sure Allow Copilot and Facilitator is set to Only during the meeting or During and after the meeting.
  6. Turn the Facilitator toggle on.
  7. Select Apply.

Create an agenda for the meeting

Facilitator will automatically search for an agenda in the meeting description and Loop meeting notes file. For Facilitator to extract an agenda from meeting notes or the meeting invite, complete the following steps:

  1. Write an agenda in the meeting description or the meeting notes Loop component before the meeting starts.
  2. Turn Facilitator on during scheduling or at the start of the meeting.

Facilitator will read the agenda and send a message in chat. The agenda can also be provided by @mentioning Facilitator in chat during the meeting. For example, “@Facilitator, here’s the agenda: introductions (5 minutes), product discussion (25 minutes).”

Note

If Facilitator isn’t showing an agenda you added in the meeting invite or notes, it might be because:

  • Only the organizer has joined: Facilitator can’t read the organizer’s copy of the meeting invite due to privacy requirements. The agenda will become available after at least one non-organizer participant joins.
  • Encrypted or sensitivity-labeled content: If the meeting invite or notes have a sensitivity label (such as Confidential or another label that requires encryption), Facilitator can’t read or extract the agenda.

Add Facilitator during a meeting

To turn Facilitator on during a meeting:

  1. Select More actionsScreenshot: generic-ellipsis-button-icon from the meeting controls.
  2. Select Turn on FacilitatorScreenshot: facilitator-icon-teams from the menu.

When you turn on Facilitator, you’ll be asked to select a language if a language for the meeting hasn’t already been selected. Once Facilitator is on, it can provide insights throughout the duration of the meeting.

Screenshot: Moderation skill for the Facilitator agent working in a Teams meeting.

The Notes icon in meeting controls will change to Screenshot: AI-generated notes icon , indicating that AI-generated notes are on. AI-generated notes won’t appear immediately but will start a few minutes later based on the discussion captured in the transcript.

Note

Mobile meeting participants can see live notes being generated. Only meeting participants who are organizers or presenters and are using Teams for web or desktop can turn Facilitator on or off during a meeting.

Turn off Facilitator during a meeting

To turn Facilitator off during a meeting:

  1. Select More actionsScreenshot: generic-ellipsis-button-icon from the meeting controls.
  2. Select Turn off FacilitatorScreenshot: facilitator-icon-teams from the menu.

Turning off Facilitator stops automated notetaking but won’t remove notes that have already been taken.

Use an agenda to keep the meeting on track

Facilitator will automatically track the agenda when an agenda is found in the meeting invite or meeting notes, or when an agenda is provided in chat.

  • To start tracking, @mention Facilitator and provide the agenda. For example, “@Facilitator, here’s the agenda: introductions (5 minutes), product discussion (25 minutes).”
  • To edit the agenda, @mention Facilitator and ask it to make the change. For example, “@Facilitator, add ‘Strategy review’ to the agenda for 15 minutes.”

Facilitator helps participants keep track of time against those agenda items by sharing the agenda in a timer on the meeting stage. If the agenda has time allocations, the timer will help keep track of time for each topic.

Facilitator listens to the meeting discussion and marks topics with a checkmark once the discussion for that topic has started.

  • Facilitator marks topics with checkmarks at intervals during the meeting, not immediately after the discussion has started.
Ask Facilitator to start a timer

You can also ask Facilitator to start a timer that isn’t tied to the meeting agenda.

  1. In the meeting chat, @mention Facilitator and ask it to start a timer.

    1. For example, “@Facilitator, add a timer for five minutes.”

  2. Facilitator begins a timer during the meeting.

  3. You can also @mention Facilitator for actions such as resetting, pausing, and stopping the timer.

Take notes with Facilitator on mobile

Instantly capture, transcribe, and organize in-person meeting notes—complete with speaker distinction and actionable recaps—directly from your mobile device.

To take notes with Facilitator:

  • iOS
  • Android

  1. Make sure your device has the latest version of Teams installed. Visit the Apple app store for updates.

  2. Open the Teams mobile app.

  3. Tap CalendarScreenshot: teams-calendar-tab-icon .

  4. Tap MeetingScreenshot: meet-icon-teams-mobile .

  5. Tap Take notes with Facilitator.

  6. Turn off native iOS voice isolation features:

    1. During a call, swipe down from the top-right corner of your screen to open the Control Center.
    2. Tap Mic Mode.
    3. Select Standard.

Your iOS voice isolation settings will persist across future meetings.

  1. Make sure your device has the latest version of Teams installed. Visit the Google Play store for updates.

  2. Turn off native Android voice isolation features:

    • Refer to the manufacturer-specific steps to turn off the feature or set to Standard mode.

  3. Open the Teams mobile app.

  4. Tap CalendarScreenshot: teams-calendar-tab-icon .

  5. Tap MeetingScreenshot: meet-icon-teams-mobile .

  6. Tap Take notes with Facilitator.

It may take a few minutes for live notes to generate as spoken content is gathered. After the meeting ends, you’ll be able to view the notes or get a shareable link. To access the notes later, as well as Copilot, open the meeting in your calendar or chat list and view the recap.

To learn more about meeting notes in Teams, see Take meeting notes in Microsoft Teams.

Review AI-generated content after a meeting

Any content generated by Facilitator during the meeting can be accessed both through meeting chat and meeting notes in Recap after a meeting ends.

  1. Select ChatScreenshot: teams-chat-tab-icon in Teams.
  2. Select a meeting chat where you turned on Facilitator.
  3. Select Recap at the top of the meeting chat. You can also open the meeting chat and select View recap from the meeting thumbnail.
  4. Select Screenshot: AI-generated notes iconNotes.

Screenshot: Finding AI-generated notes after the meeting is over in the Recap tab of a Teams chat.

AI-generated meeting notes are stored in a Microsoft Loop page, and any meeting participant can edit the Loop page before, during, or after the meeting, as well as edit the AI-generated notes during and after the meeting. In addition to the real-time AI-generated notes in the Notes tab, the AI summary tab includes a full-transcript summary generated after the meeting.

Ask questions to Facilitator in a meeting chat

Facilitator acts as a collaborative team member in the meeting chat and can help search the web and answer questions about the conversation in the meeting. Just @mention Facilitator to:

  • Get quick summaries to catch up.
  • Ask questions about the meeting/chat or shared documents.
  • Find answers about the conversation or general topics.
  • Keep the team updated with key insights.
  • Search the web for relevant information to share.
  • Ask questions about the agenda and time.

Manage your tasks

Facilitator can help you manage tasks from a meeting. Facilitator automatically captures tasks during the meeting that you can access in Notes. Select ‘Accept to sync’ in Follow-up tasks to sync these tasks to Planner.

You can also ask Facilitator directly through the meeting chat to create, edit, and assign other tasks. The tasks that you ask Facilitator to create automatically syncs to Planner. You can also query for specific tasks or all tasks related to that meeting.

Create a document

Facilitator can create a Word or Loop document based on a particular topic from the meeting by typing @Facilitator, along with the request. Facilitator will also offer to assist when document creation is being discussed. In these cases, you’ll have to accept and acknowledge Facilitator to generate that draft.

How to use Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams chats and channels

Copilot in Microsoft Teams chat and channels helps you get up to speed on conversations by quickly reviewing the main points, action items, and decisions without having to scroll through long threads.

Note

Copilot references information from the message thread in which it is opened, with a 30-day history as the default time frame unless you specify otherwise. Copilot can’t summarize images, loop components, or files shared in the chat thread.

Use Copilot in a one-on-one or group chat

Screenshot: A view of Copilot in a Teams chat

  1. Go to Chat on the left side of Teams, then select a specific chat from the list.
  2. Select Open Copilot in the upper-right corner of the chat—you’ll see the Copilot icon.
  3. Under the compose box to the right of your chat, select a prompt or choose Show more to see other suggestions.
  4. Select or type a prompt in the compose box, then select Send. Try these: *- Summarize what I’ve missed.
    • What were the key takeaways from last month?
    • What did [a member of the chat] say?
    • What links were shared?*
  5. Once Copilot responds, try this to further refine your results:

  • Include a clear time frame to get targeted results, like “December 2023” or “last month”. Copilot will only consider the messages sent within the specified time period, as reflected by the timestamp in Copilot’s response.

    Tip

    If the timeframe you’ve specified is above the limit for Copilot, select Generate next response to view the rest of the response.

  • Select CopyScreenshot: Icon for the copy button for Copilot in Word on mobile devices to paste into the chat, a channel conversation, or anywhere else.

  • See citations by selecting Sources at the end of the response. Select a specific source and the chat to the left of the Copilot pane will scroll to that particular message in the chat thread.

Interpreter in Microsoft Teams meetings and calls

Note

20 hours of interpretation are included per person per month with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. Access beyond the hours included is subject to available capacity.

Remove language barriers in multilingual Microsoft Teams meetings and calls with the Interpreter agent. The interpreter agent helps participants speak and listen in their preferred languages through real-time speech-to-speech interpretation.

Screenshot: Screenshot showing general Interpreter experience in a Microsoft Teams meeting.

Interpreter in meetings and calls

Make Teams meetings and calls more inclusive with the Interpreter agent when participants don’t share a common language. Interpreter is ideal for meetings and calls where participants speak different languages and you’d traditionally rely on a human interpreter.

Interpreter helps bridge communication gaps by translating speech into each participant’s preferred language—allowing everyone to speak and listen in the language they’re most comfortable with and fully engage in the conversation.

When you turn on Interpreter, you’ll be able to hear Interpreter translate other participants into your preferred language.

Interpreting: When someone speaks in a language other than your preferred language, you’ll hear the translation over the original speaker’s audio. You’ll also see an indicator on the original speaker’s video feed that shows their speech is being translated.

Screenshot: Screenshot of the indication that appears when someones speech is being interpreted in a Teams meeting.Interpreting for others: When you speak in a language different from other participants’ preferred languages, they’ll hear your speech translated into their chosen languages. An indicator on your video feed will show that your speech is being translated for others.

Additionally, after you’ve finished listening to interpreted audio, if others are still listening in their preferred languages, you’ll see an indicator prompting you to wait until everyone has finished listening before speaking again.

Screenshot: Screenshot showing Interpreter indicator that someone is still listening to an interpretation.

People who don’t have Interpreter turned on will also see an indicator that someone’s speech is being translated. This provides everyone with a visual cue to let translation finish before they unmute and start speaking.

Supported languages

Interpreter currently supports the following languages: English, Spanish, Portuguese, Japanese, Simplified Chinese (Mandarin), Italian, German, French, Korean and Taiwanese.

Note

  • Some spoken languages can be recognized by Interpreter, but interpretation accuracy isn’t guaranteed.
  • Regardless of the input language, the interpretation output will always be in one of the supported languages listed above.

Turn on Interpreter in meetings

Turn on Interpreter in meetings with up to 1,000 participants, where multiple languages are being spoken.

When you turn on Interpreter, multilingual speech recognition will also be turned on automatically, allowing participants to set their spoken and translated languages. Multilingual speech recognition can be turned on independently of Interpreter by the organizer in the meeting options.

  • Desktop
  • Mobile

To turn on Interpreter:

  1. Select More actionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon in your meeting controls.

  2. Select Language and speechScreenshot: Language and speech menu item icon > InterpreterScreenshot: Interpreter icon in Microsoft Teams > Turn on for meScreenshot: Interpreter icon in Microsoft Teams .

  3. In Interpreter settings:

    • Select the language you want Interpreter to translate into from the Listen to meeting in dropdown menu.
    • Adjust the Balance volume slider to hear more original or interpreted audio.
    • Choose the voice you want other participants to hear your interpreted speech in from the Choose your voice when interpreted options. To learn more about voice simulation, see Voice simulation in Interpreter.

  4. Select Turn on.

To adjust Interpreter settings or turn off Interpreter, select the Interpreter indicator in your meeting window.

Select Manage settings to open Interpreter settings or Turn off for me to turn Interpreter off for yourself.

Screenshot: Screenshot highlighting Interpreter indicator in a Microsoft Teams meeting.

To turn on Interpreter:

  1. Tap MoreScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon in your meeting controls.

  2. Tap Turn on InterpreterScreenshot: Interpreter icon in Microsoft Teams .

  3. In Interpretation language, tap the language you want Interpreter to translate into.

  4. In Interpretation audio:

    • Adjust the Balance audio slider to hear more original or interpreted audio.
    • Choose the voice you want other participants to hear your interpreted speech in from the Your voice representation options. To learn more about the Simulate my voice option, see Voice simulation in Interpreter.

  5. Tap Turn on Interpreter.

To adjust Interpreter settings, tap MoreScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon in your meeting controls. Then, tap Language settingsScreenshot: Teams translate message icon > AI Interpretation languageScreenshot: Language and speech menu item icon or Interpretation audioScreenshot: Teams audio settings .

To turn off Interpreter, tap MoreScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > Turn off InterpreterScreenshot: Interpreter icon in Microsoft Teams .

Note

  • Interpreter settings will persist across future meetings.
  • Interpreter isn’t currently supported in ad-hoc meetings, meetings using Microsoft Teams Rooms with personal devices, town halls, webinars, or Teams Free meetings.

Turn on Interpreter in calls

  2. Select Language and speech > Turn on Interpreter for me.

Choose your Interpreter settings

After you turn on Interpreter, the Interpreter settings pane opens automatically.

If the settings pane is not open, select the Interpreter icon in the call window, and then select Manage settings.

In Interpreter settings, do the following:

  • In Listen to the call in, select the language you want Interpreter to translate into.
  • Use the Balance volume slider to adjust how much original audio or interpreted audio you hear.
  • In Choose your voice when interpreted, select Simulate my voice to have Interpreter use voice data to simulate your voice. Choose Automated voice to select the voice other participants hear when your speech is translated.

Select Turn on.

Change settings or turn off Interpreter

  • Select the Interpreter icon in the upper left corner of the call window.
  • Select Manage settings to change your preferences, or select Turn off for me to stop using Interpreter.
Spoken language auto-detection

When Interpreter is turned on, spoken language is automatically detected and updated across Interpreter, live captions, and live transcription.

To turn off auto detection for live captions or transcription:

  • In the Transcript pane, select Language settingsScreenshot: teams-language-settings-icon and change the selection in the Your spoken language dropdown menu from Auto-detect to your preferred language.
  • Next to live captions, select Open caption settingsScreenshot: skype-teams-mobile-icon-settings > Language settingsScreenshot: teams-language-settings-icon . In the Your spoken language dropdown menu, change your selection from Auto-detect to your preferred language.

When Interpreter is turned off, spoken language won’t update automatically if participants switch languages during the meeting which can result in inaccurate content.

Voice simulation in Interpreter

When you use Voice simulation in Interpreter, translated speech is generated in your own voice, so other participants will hear translations as if you’re speaking their language directly. Short segments of your speech are briefly analyzed by the system in real time to simulate your unique tone, style, and voice characteristics.

Voice samples or biometric data are never stored. AI instantly creates a natural-sounding voice in the selected language, preserving your authentic tone, pitch, and speaking style without exaggerating emotions. This ensures a familiar and seamless multilingual conversation experience.

Data privacy

Voice data is processed immediately, in real time, without ever storing your voice samples or biometric information. To learn more, see Manage Interpreter agent for your organization.

Voice simulation policy and settings

If your IT admin has turned on the Voice simulation policy, the setting Simulate my voice will be turned on automatically. If the policy isn’t turned on, your speech will be translated using a default automated voice.

To manage your voice preferences during a meeting:

  1. Select More actionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon in your meeting controls.

  2. Select Language and speechScreenshot: Language and speech menu item icon > InterpreterScreenshot: Interpreter icon in Microsoft Teams > Interpreter settingsScreenshot: Teams translate message icon .

  3. In Choose your voice when interpreted, select:

    • Simulate my voice for others to hear your translated speech presented in your simulated voice.
    • Automated voice for others to hear your translated speech presented in a default automated voice (e.g., Ava).

  4. Select Confirm.

Best practices for Interpreter

Follow these best practices for a smooth, effective multilingual meeting experience:

When to use Interpreter
  • In meetings without a common language: ideal when participants don’t share a common language.
  • In structured discussions: best for structured conversations where one person is speaking at a time.
Tips for effective multilingual communication
  • Speak one language at a time. Stick consistently to a single language, especially if you’re bilingual.
  • Be clear and concise. Use short sentences, pause frequently, and simplify technical language to improve interpretation accuracy.
  • Raise your hand. Select RaiseScreenshot: raise-hand-icon in your meeting controls to indicate when you want to speak, preventing overlapping speech.
  • Allow interpretation to finish. Look out for visual indicators showing that others have finished listening to interpretation before continuing or changing topics.
  • Support your message visually. Share your screen or use chat features to provide additional context (links, screenshots, documents).
  • Turn on your camera. Visual cues can create a more engaging and natural multilingual conversation.
Meeting setup recommendations
  • Ensure the meeting organizer has either a Microsoft 365 Copilot or Teams Premium license. Turn on multilingual speech recognition in your meeting options so all participants can individually select their spoken languages and translation settings for live captions for clear communication with or without Interpreter.
  • Easily catch up on key discussions through intelligent meeting recap, now supporting multilingual meetings. After the meeting, your recap is automatically generated in the translation language you selected for live transcription and captions.

Interpreter limitations

  • Meeting recordings only capture the original meeting audio and don’t include interpretation audio.
  • Translated transcripts are only available live during the meeting. After the meeting ends, only the original (spoken) language is shown in the transcript.
  • Interpreter isn’t optimized for meetings with rapid exchanges, interruptions, or overlapping dialogue, as the translation may take longer than the original speech, making it harder to follow and respond naturally.
  • Interpretation of people’s names, genders, or technical terms may be inaccurate.

FAQ

How does voice simulation work?

If you turn on voice simulation, Interpreter will sample brief segments of your voice to simulate your tone, style, and voice characteristics. When Interpreter translated your speech for others, people will hear the translation in your simulated voice. Turn off voice simulation anytime and choose a different voice style in Interpreter settings.

Voice simulation only processes your voice in real time and doesn’t store your biometric data or add emotional sentiment beyond what’s being spoken. If you can’t access Interpreter, contact your IT admin.

What technology powers Interpreter?

The Interpreter agent in Teams enables real-time speech-to-speech (STS) translation using Azure AI Services. It automatically detects spoken languages in a meeting and support multi-speaker, multilingual conversations.

How it works:

  1. Speech Recognition (ST): Converts spoken language into English text.
  2. Translation (MT): Translates English text into the selected language(s).
  3. Voice Generation (TTS): Produces translated speech in the target language. It can simulate the speaker’s voice or use a predefined voice based on their preference and IT admin policy.
  4. A bot transmits meeting audio for cloud-based processing and returns translations instantly.
Does Interpreter support meetings with people from other orgs?

Yes. People from other orgs can use Interpreter if they join from verified M365 accounts with valid M365 Copilot licenses. People joining anonymously or as guests can’t use Interpreter because their identities and license statuses can’t be verified.

We’re always looking for ways to improve features. To provide feedback, select the Interpreter indicator Screenshot: Interpreter icon in Microsoft Teams in your meeting window. Select either the thumbs up or down button.

Screenshot: Screenshot highlighting Interpreter feedback buttons.

Add your feedback and select Submit to send your comments directly to Microsoft.

Listen to audio recaps of your meetings

Teams Meeting Audio recap is a feature that uses the power of large language models (LMM) to capture and summarize key topics discussed during your Teams meetings, using transcripts from up to 8 meetings during the time period you choose. Summaries are provided in audio format, enabling efficient review of the highlights without going through individual recaps.

The summary is generated by AI and should be checked for accuracy.

Important

Copilot in Teams is available on Windows, Mac, web, Android, and iOS. You must have a Microsoft 365 and a Microsoft 365 Copilot license in order to access Copilot in Teams features, like audio recaps.

How audio recap works

Audio recaps can be generated using your meeting transcripts and are stored in your OneDrive. Only meetings that have transcripts can be used to generate audio recaps.

Note

  • Meeting transcripts expire after 120 days unless deleted sooner by the meeting organizer. You can’t create audio recaps of meetings that are older than 120 days.
  • Audio recaps may be subject to daily usage limits.
Supported languages

Chinese, variations across English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese, Spanish

How to access audio recaps in Teams

To listen to an audio recap of your meetings, you have several entry points to choose from: the Meet app in Teams, the meeting’s chat, and the meeting’s detail page.

Note

For instructions on how to access and use audio recaps on your mobile device, see How to use meeting audio recaps on mobile devices.

Find audio recaps in the Meet app
  1. On the left side of Teams, select … View more apps.
  2. Search for and select the Meet app.
  3. In the Meet app, select the Audio recaps tab.
Find meeting recaps from the meeting’s chat

  1. Open a meeting chat in the Teams Chat app.

  2. Next to meeting chat’s title, select the Recap tab.

    1. You may need to select + to see the Recap tab.

  3. Near the top of the Recap tab, select the Screenshot: Call iconAudio recap button.

    1. You will be taken to the Meet app in Teams with the Audio recap tab open.
Find meeting recaps from the meeting’s detail page

  1. From the Calendar app in Teams, select a meeting to open its meeting details page.

  2. Scroll down the page to the Meeting recap section.

  3. Select the View recap button.

    1. Teams will open a new window with the meeting’s recap details.

  4. Near the top of the meeting recap window, select the Screenshot: Call iconAudio recap button.

    1. You will be taken to the Meet app in Teams with the Audio recap tab open.

How to generate a meeting recap

Once you’re in the Meet app, can listen to, create, and manage your audio recaps.

  1. In the Meet app, select the Audio recaps tab.

  2. On the left side list of audio recaps, select Screenshot: Add icon to set up a new audio recap.

    1. If this is your first time creating an audio recap, the Audio recaps tab will take you directly to the setup page for a new audio recap.

  3. From the dropdowns, choose a time period and a style for your audio recap.

    1. You can select up to 8 meetings that have transcripts for one audio recap.

  4. Select the Generate button, and Copilot will generate an audio recap.

  5. You can select Screenshot: Icon of audio recap pause buttonPause, Screenshot: Icon of audio recap play buttonPlay, Screenshot: Icon of the skip back arrowSkip backwards and Screenshot: Icon of the skip forward arrow forwards by 10 seconds, and choose a playback speed for the audio recap.

    1. You can also view Chapters of the recap and skip to a specific section of the recap by selecting the chapter from the chapter list.
    2. Lastly, you can select the Transcript button to view the entire transcript of the audio recap.

  6. The generated audio recap is accessible to you for 60 days. After 60 days, the audio recap expires and is automatically deleted.

Manage your audio recaps

By default, transcriptions of Teams meetings are retained for 120 days unless manually deleted earlier by the meeting organizer. The generated audio recap is exclusively accessible to you and will expire after 60 days. You can manage your audio recaps in OneDrive, where you have the option to delete any audio recap that is no longer needed. Once an audio recap is deleted from OneDrive, it’s no longer available on your Teams Audio recap listing page.

To learn more about how audio recap data is handled in Copilot in Teams, see Frequently asked questions about Copilot in Teams audio recap.

Use Copilot Call Delegation in Microsoft Teams

Copilot Call Delegation in Teams helps you manage incoming calls. It answers calls on your behalf, gathers context, and takes action based on your availability and settings.

Copilot Call Delegation is an AI‑powered voice agent. It can screen calls, collect caller intent, schedule follow‑ups, and route urgent calls to you.

Copilot Call Delegation is supported on:

  • Windows desktop (English)
  • Mac desktop (English)
  • Web

Copilot Call Delegation is not supported on:

  • iOS
  • Android

This article explains how to turn on and configure Copilot Call Delegation in the Teams desktop app.

Note

  • Copilot Call Delegation is available as part of the Microsoft 365 Copilot Frontier program. Frontier provides Join Frontier to get early access to select Copilot and AI features before general availability. Features available through Frontier are shared for evaluation and feedback, and may change before general release. To learn more and get access to Frontier program features, visit: Explore AI Early Access in Microsoft 365 | Microsoft Frontier.
  • During the Frontier program access period, individual users require a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. Service limits may apply within individual calls and across monthly tenant usage, including:
    • Call length limit of 4 minutes
    • Monthly usage limit of 15,000 minutes per tenant
    • AI model processing limitations subject to the number of concurrent calls within a rolling two-minute window
  • The service limitations help ensure fair usage across customers and maintain service reliability. When service limitations are reached, incoming calls may revert to your pre-existing call routing logic or voicemail until the AI screening experience is restored. Licensing details and service limits are subject to change and additional information will be communicated at general availability.
  • Copilot Call Delegation is currently available only when your Teams app language is set to English.

What Copilot Call Delegation can do

When you turn on Copilot Call Delegation, you can use these features:

  • Call screening: Screens calls before they reach you and helps block spam or fraudulent calls.
  • Caller context: Collects the caller’s reason for calling so you can decide how to respond.
  • Call routing and follow‑ups: Routes urgent calls to you or schedules callbacks and meetings when you are unavailable.
  • Out‑of‑office assistance: Detects when you are out of office and schedules meetings after you return.
  • Transparency and control: Notifies you when Copilot Call Delegation takes action. You can customize settings at any time.

Turn on Copilot Call Delegation

Copilot Call Delegation replaces your existing call routing settings.

To turn on Copilot Call Delegation:

  1. In Teams, go to Settings and more > Settings > Calls.
  2. Under Manage Copilot Call Delegation, select Set up Copilot Call Delegation.

If you do not see this option, contact your Teams admin.

What to expect in Teams

The first time you open the Calls app after Copilot Call Delegation is enabled, you see a welcome screen. The screen explains how Copilot Call Delegation works and what it can do.

During a call:
  • You receive a notification when Copilot Call Delegation answers a call.
  • A banner shows that the call is being screened.
  • You can join the call at any time by selecting Pick up from Call history.
  • Callers see an avatar and hear an announcement that they are speaking with an attendant, not a person.
  • Urgent calls may be escalated to you with a topic shown in the notification.
  • You can open a live preview from the screening banner or call history.
After a call:
  • A post‑call summary appears in Call history when available.

Configure Copilot Call Delegation settings

After you turn on Copilot Call Delegation, you can adjust how it handles your calls.

Call handling options:
  • Choose which calls are screened: Select whether Copilot Call Delegation screens internal or external calls.
  • Default language: Select the language Copilot Call Delegation uses when speaking with callers.
  • Filter spam‑likely calls: Automatically routes suspected spam calls to voicemail.
Privacy and content options:
  • Recordings and transcription: Turn call recording and transcription on or off for Copilot Call Delegation calls.
  • Schedule follow‑ups: Allow Copilot Call Delegation to schedule meetings on your behalf.

Configure Bookings calendar

Copilot Call Delegation uses a private Bookings calendar to schedule follow‑ups. This calendar is not created by default.

When you turn on Schedule follow‑ups, Copilot Call Delegation creates a private bookings calendar in the background.

To manage the calendar:

  1. In Call settings, select Schedule follow-ups.
  2. Review or update scheduling follow-ups, which can include:
  • How soon can someone a follow-up
  • How far in advance to schedule on your calendar
  • Set your available hours

Important

Save all changes. Updates do not take effect until they are saved.

You can report issues or share feedback in two ways.

Report from Teams settings:

  1. In Teams, select Settings and more at the top of the app.
  2. Select Feedback > Report a problem.
  3. Choose Copilot Call Delegation as the category.
  4. Describe the issue or feedback.

Report from call history:

  1. Go to Calls > Call history.
  2. Select a call handled by Copilot Call Delegation.
  3. In the side pane, select Report a problem with Copilot Call Delegation.
Known issues
  • Presence status is not considered. Calls are screened based only on your Copilot Call Delegation settings.
  • Background noise may affect call handling in some cases.
  • Live preview is not available when recording and transcription are turned off.
  • Post‑call summaries are not created if the caller hangs up early.
  • In Recap, Copilot Call Delegation may be attributed incorrectly.

Use Copilot without transcribing or recording a Teams meeting or call

Engage with Copilot during calls and meetings without recording or transcribing to protect confidential information. Copilot can generate AI notes and tasks during the conversation without transcription and recording enabled.

Transcription won’t start automatically when Copilot is turned on for a call or meeting. You’ll be able to prompt Copilot during the call or meeting, but to prompt or view Copilot’s conversation after the call or meeting ends, make sure to turn on live transcription.

Note

Meetings refer to scheduled events that are set up through Teams or Outlook calendar, even if attendees participated via a dial-in or audio only connection. Calls refer to unscheduled interactions initiated through the Teams video call or audio call options for VoIP or through the Calls app dialer for  PSTN calls.

Teams meetings

If you’re organizing a confidential meeting discussing sensitive information and prefer not to record or transcribe, you can still use Copilot to help with notetaking and task management.

Important

Depending on your org’s Microsoft Purview retention policies, Copilot prompts and responses during meetings may be retained for compliance purposes, even if recording and transcription are turned off.

Before a scheduled meeting:

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: Meetings button in Teams.

  2. Select a meeting you organized.

  3. Select OptionsScreenshot: Settings button .

  4. Scroll down to Copilot and other AIScreenshot: copilot-icon and make sure Only during the meeting is selected from the dropdown menu.

    Note

    If you don’t see this option, contact your IT admin.

  5. Select Apply.

During a meeting, select CopilotScreenshot: copilot-icon in your meeting controls. Then, select Turn on from the notification to open the CopilotScreenshot: copilot-icon pane.

Copilot can generate notes, list tasks, and much more during the live meeting. And remember, other people in the meeting can’t see your conversation with Copilot.

Screenshot: Copilot no transcript meeting

After the meeting, Copilot won’t be available in the meeting’s Recap tab unless transcription or recording was turned on during the meeting. Then, Copilot and the content of your conversation with Copilot will continue to be available, starting from the moment the transcript or recording was turned on.

Learn more about Copilot in Teams Meetings.

Teams Calls

Copilot-only mode for calls is a setting that is enabled by your IT admin. After initiating the call, select CopilotScreenshot: copilot-icon in your call controls. Then, choose Turn on from the notification to open the CopilotScreenshot: copilot-icon pane.

Note

If you don’t see this option, contact your IT admin.

Screenshot: Copilot in calls without transcription

After the call, Copilot won’t be available in the associated chat thread for VoIP calls or the Calls app call history. However, if someone turns on transcription or recording during the call, your conversation with Copilot will be available afterward.

Tip

If there’s content that you’d like to save from your conversation with Copilot, copy and paste it in another place before the call ends. 

Learn more about Copilot in Teams Phone.

FAQs

If Copilot is set to “Only during the meeting” or “Only during the call”, does Copilot start as soon as the meeting or call starts?

No. Participants must select CopilotScreenshot: copilot-icon in the meeting or call controls to start Copilot.

Once Copilot starts, can I turn it off?

Once Copilot starts, it will be on for the duration of the meeting or call.

If Copilot is set to “Only during the meeting” or “Only during the call”, can I still use Copilot if the transcription or recording gets turned on?

Yes, Copilot will still work. If transcription is turned on, interactions with Copilot during and after the meeting or call will contain information from the speech-to-text data and the transcript.

After the meeting or call ends, only information from the point that the transcript was turned on will be accessible.

If someone joins the meeting or call late, can they use Copilot to access information from earlier in the conversation?

Yes, late-joining participants will be able to access any content from the moment Copilot was initiated by a another participant in the meeting or call.

By policy, I’m not allowed to start a transcript or recording. Can I still use Copilot only during the meeting or call?

Yes. Transcription isn’t required to use Copilot during a meeting or call. You’ll still be able to see Copilot’s conversation history after the meeting or call ends. However, all Copilot interactions will be available through Purview based on your org’s retention policy.

How can Copilot work only during the meeting or call?

Copilot uses meeting audio and contextual signals to generate responses during the meeting. While meeting transcripts are not created when transcription is turned off, Copilot prompts and responses may be retained in accordance with your org’s Microsoft Purview retention policies.

Is there an audit log of prompts and responses?

Copilot prompts and responses may be retained in the Microsoft 365 compliance substrate and are subject to your org’s Microsoft Purview retention policies.

What are the plans for eDiscovery?

Copilot prompts and responses may be discoverable through Microsoft Purview eDiscovery, depending on your organization’s retention policy configuration.

Why is the meeting option for how to use Copilot visible to all members of an organization, whether they are licensed or unlicensed?

This ensures meeting organizers can set how Copilot will be used in their meetings, even if they themselves don’t have a license.

Can external participants access Copilot only during the meeting or call?

No. If a licensed external participant joins a meeting or call with this option enabled, they won’t be able to interact with Copilot. Copilot can’t access external transcripts or speech-to-text data. This applies to channel meetings and internal meetings and calls.

Can people in a multi-tenant organization (MTO) access Copilot only during the meeting or call when in meetings or calls hosted by a different organization in the MTO?

No. MTO users are treated as external users for this scenario.

If my org disables transcription for all company meetings or calls, and someone with Microsoft 365 Copilot enables Copilot only during the meeting or call, will that person be able to use Copilot during the meeting or call?

Yes. If transcription is turned off for the meeting or call and someone enables Copilot only during the meeting or call, people with Copilot licenses can use Copilot during the meeting or call.

However, one exception for calls is if the admin selects a setting that Copilot requires persistent transcription to work and then limits the user from using transcription. Copilot will not work during calls under this scenario.

Why does Copilot ask me what language everyone is speaking? What does this do?

Selecting the language that everyone is speaking helps ensure that audio processing happens in the right language. The speech-to-text data and any citations will be generated in the spoken language you select. However, you can ask Copilot a question in any language, and it will respond in that language. 

How do I change the spoken language after Copilot starts?

The spoken language can be changed through the live captions settings. To learn more, see Use live captions in Microsoft Teams meetings.

Add third-party apps to the Files app on iOS in Microsoft Teams

Add and access all your files from your iOS device’s Files app, including third-party apps like OneDrive, Dropbox, Box, Google Drive, and Adobe Creative Cloud. The files you save to the Files app on your iOS device show up automatically, but you’ll need to set up other third-party cloud storage services to get access to them in Files.

Add third-party apps on iOS

  1. Download the app from the iOS App Store and log in to it.
  2. Open the Files app.
  3. Tap Browse (in the bottom right corner).
  4. In the top right corner tap MoreScreenshot: Microsoft teams More options icon. > Edit.
  5. Turn on the third-party app by swiping right on the toggle.
  6. Tap Done.

Note

These are directions for iOS 13 and later. For devices running on iOS 12 or earlier, open the Files app and then tap Locations > Edit to add third-party apps.

Now, when you go to upload a file to Teams from your iOS device, you’ll be able to access them from any of your third-party apps.

Collaborate on files in Microsoft Teams

Simplify your workflow with others by collaborating on files in Microsoft Teams. Share them to allow others to view and edit them with you (editing in Visio requires a license).

Share a file in Teams

Work on files together by sharing them with members of your team using OneDrive in Teams. To share a file from OneDrive:

  1. In Teams, go to OneDriveScreenshot: 3230d89e-d913-43c4-ba36-b48fc14f87f7 > My Files.

  2. Find the file you want to share.

  3. Hover over the file and select ShareScreenshot: Share icon .

    1. Enter the name, group, or email you want to send your file to.
    2. Add an optional message to give the recipient context.
    3. Select Sharing settingsScreenshot: Settings icon to change file permissions.
    4. Select Copy linkScreenshot: Forms Link button to copy the file link to your clipboard.

  4. Select SendScreenshot: Send button .

Channel files

Each channel in Teams has its own file folder where you can share files for that specific channel.

To access channel files:

  1. Select TeamsScreenshot: Teams button in Teams.
  2. Select the channel you want to access files in.
  3. Select Shared at the top of the channel.
Syncing in a channel

Each team has a corresponding SharePoint site. Changes made to files in SharePoint automatically sync with Teams (and vice versa). You can also manually sync the file libraries.

To sync files in a channel:

  1. Select TeamsScreenshot: Teams button in Teams.
  2. Select the channel you want to sync files in.
  3. At the top of your channel, select Shared > More commandsScreenshot: Teams settings and more button > SyncScreenshot: Sync icon in Teams .

You can also select SyncScreenshot: Sync icon in Teams in SharePoint to make sure files reflect the latest changes made in Teams.

Reverting a deleted, renamed, or un-synced folder

If the SharePoint folder associated with the channel was deleted, renamed, or hasn’t been synced, you can revert a renamed folder or sync a folder following these steps:

  1. Select TeamsScreenshot: Teams button in Teams.
  2. Select the channel you want to sync files in.
  3. Select Shared > More commandsScreenshot: Teams settings and more button > Open in SharePoint.
  4. In the upper-right corner of your screen, open the Details pane.
  5. Under Activity, rename the folder using the original name.

To sync a folder, go to the channel’s Shared tab and select SyncScreenshot: Sync icon in Teams .

Upload a file

To upload a file to OneDrive in Teams:

  1. Open Teams for desktop and select OneDriveScreenshot: 3230d89e-d913-43c4-ba36-b48fc14f87f7 .
  2. Select Create or uploadScreenshot: Plus sign icon > Files upload.
  3. Select a file and select Open.

The file will automatically start uploading.

To upload a file to a channel in Teams:

  1. Select TeamsScreenshot: Teams button in Teams.
  2. Select the channel you want to upload a file in.
  3. Select Shared.
  • Drag and drop the file from where it’s currently located into the Teams window among the files.
  • Select Upload and select the file (or files) you’d like to upload. Then, select Open.

Any files you upload will be accessible by any member of your channel.

Create a file

To create a new file in Teams:

  1. Select OneDriveScreenshot: 3230d89e-d913-43c4-ba36-b48fc14f87f7 in Teams.
  2. Select Create or uploadScreenshot: Plus sign icon .
  3. Choose the type of file you want to create.
  4. Enter a name for the file and select Create.
  5. The new file will open for you to start editing.

Note

Linux users won’t be able to open files with the desktop Office app.

Collaborate with others in files by uploading and sharing them in Teams.

To share a file and start collaborating with others:

  2. Find the file you want to share.

To download a file from a Teams channel:

  1. Open a channel in Teams.
  2. Select the Shared tab.
  3. Find the file you want to download and select More actionsScreenshot: More options button > DownloadScreenshot: Download button .
Download a file from OneDrive

To download a file from OneDrive in Teams:

  1. In Teams, select the OneDriveScreenshot: OneDrive icon tab.

  2. Find the file you want to download and select More actionsScreenshot: more actions button-duplicate > Open > Edit in Teams.

  3. When the file opens, select File > Create a CopyScreenshot: Copy link button > Download a CopyScreenshot: Download button .

    • This option may not be available, depending on permissions set by the file owner.

You can also select a file from the OneDriveScreenshot: OneDrive icon tab and select More actionsScreenshot: more actions button-duplicate > DownloadScreenshot: Download button .

Change where to save downloaded files
  1. In Teams for desktop, select Settings and moreScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon .
  2. Select SettingsScreenshot: Settings button > Files and linksScreenshot: Icon used on Pages tab in Journal .
  3. Under Downloads > Location, select Change.
  4. Decide where you want to save files and choose Select Folder.
  5. Turn the Always ask where to save downloaded file toggle on to choose where to save files each time you download one.

Any future files you download from Teams will be saved to the location you specified.

Note

This action isn’t currently supported on Teams for web or mobile.

Edit a file in Microsoft Teams

Open and edit files directly in Teams or in their respective desktop or web apps.

Edit a file in Teams

To open and edit a file in Teams, select a file from any of these locations:

  • The files list when you select OneDriveScreenshot: OneDrive icon on the left side of Teams
  • The Shared tab at the top of a chat or channel
  • The message where the file was attached

By default, the file opens inside Teams with the standard Office tools available at the top of the screen.

Change your file open preference

To change where you want to open Word, PowerPoint, and Excel files in:

  1. Select Settings and moreScreenshot: More options button > SettingsScreenshot: Settings button in Teams.

  2. Select Files and linksScreenshot: Icon used on Pages tab in Journal .

  3. In File open preference., select the dropdown menu to choose where you want files to open:

    • Teams
    • Desktop app
    • Browser

Your changes will be applied automatically.

Note

  • Non-Office files must be edited in their corresponding apps and then uploaded to Teams again.
  • To edit files on your mobile device, open them in their respective Office mobile apps.

Rename a file in OneDrive

To rename a file in OneDrive:

  1. Select OneDriveScreenshot: OneDrive icon in Teams.
  2. Find the file or folder you want to rename under My FilesScreenshot: Folder button , or select More actionsScreenshot: More options button > Open in OneDriveScreenshot: OneDrive icon .
  3. Hover over the file or folder and select More actionsScreenshot: More options button > Rename.
  4. Enter the new name and select Update to save the new file name.

Rename a file in a channel

To rename a file in a channel:

  1. Under ChatScreenshot: Teams Chat Tab icon , go to Channels.

  2. Select the team you want to delete a file from.

  3. Select the Shared tab.

  4. Select More actionsScreenshot: More options button > Rename next to the file or folder.

  5. Enter the new name and select Rename.

  6. Additional tools

When you open your file within Teams, you will have these options:

  • CommentsScreenshot: chat This will show you any comments made in the file.

  • Catch upScreenshot: Catch Up icon See the changes others have made since you last viewed the file.

  • EditingScreenshot: Editing icon Here you can indicate whether you want to work with the file as an editor (the default) or reviewer.

  • Share Screenshot: people To share the file with others, select:

    • Share Screenshot: share - Enter names of people you want to send your file to and select Send. You can also manage editing access by selecting People in your organization with the link can edit.
    • Copy LinkScreenshot: Copy Link icon - Generate a shareable link to send others and manage editing access by selecting People in your organization with the link can edit.
    • Manage AccessScreenshot: Settings button - See the links to your file and who has access. To change who can open the file and whether they can edit or download it, select People in your organization with the link can edit and make your choices.

  • Close - This will close the file and take you back to where you were in Teams when you first opened the file.

Edit an Office file in its desktop or web app

Before attempting to edit an Office file in its desktop app, make sure:

  • You’re using the Teams desktop app for Windows or MacOS.
  • You have an Office 365 E3 or E5 license.
  • To download the desktop apps for PowerPoint, Word, and Excel (Office version 16 or newer).

  1. Right-click a file from any of these locations:

    • The files list when you select OneDriveScreenshot: OneDrive icon on the left side of Teams
    • The Shared tab at the top of a chat or channel
    • The message where the file was attached

  2. Select Open in and choose Desktop app or Open in browser.

If you’re using Teams on the web, you can choose between Teams and Browser.

You can also manually choose where a file is opened without changing your default setting by going to the file and selecting More optionsScreenshot: More options button > Open.

Access files in Teams for desktop

Files in channels and chats

Files you upload to a channel are stored in your team’s SharePoint folder. These files are available in the Shared tab at the top of each channel.

Files you send in chat are stored in your OneDrive for Business and only shared with the people in that conversation. You can find them in the Shared tab at the top of a chat.

Note

The OneDrive files you see in Teams are OneDrive for Business files associated with your Microsoft 365 account, not your personal OneDrive. Teams can’t currently connect to your personal OneDrive.

  3. Tap the name of the chat or person you’re chatting with at the top of the conversation.

  3. Tap AddScreenshot: Select to add an item. > Files.
  4. Select a file and tap Open.

Note

Files you upload in a one-on-one or group chat are stored in the Microsoft Teams Chat Files in your OneDrive for Business folder and are shared only with the people in that conversation.

Files you upload to a channel are stored in your team’s SharePoint folder.

To upload files:

  2. Tap Files > OneDrive.
  3. Tap AddScreenshot: Select to add an item. > Files.
  4. Select a file and tap Open.

Files you upload in a one-on-one or group chat are stored in the Microsoft Teams Chat Files in your OneDrive for Business folder and are shared only with the people in that conversation.

Share a file from cloud storage in Microsoft Teams

OneDrive for Business cloud storage is available by default in Teams. To share files from other cloud storage apps, first add a cloud storage service to Teams.

Sharing files in OneDrive

  1. Select the OneDriveScreenshot: 3230d89e-d913-43c4-ba36-b48fc14f87f7 app on the left side of Teams, and go to My files.

  2. Hover over the file you want to share and select More ActionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon .

  3. You have several options to share the file:

    • Select ShareScreenshot: OD share icon to add people and a message when sharing the file.
    • Select Copy linkScreenshot: Insert Link button to copy a link you can paste into a chat or post.
    • Choose Manage accessScreenshot: People or Show Participants button to manage the file permissions.

Share a folder from OneDrive

  1. Go to the OneDriveScreenshot: OneDrive icon tab on the left side of Teams.
  2. Select the folder you wish to share and click on Show more actions for this itemScreenshot: Ellipsis icon .
  3. From here, you have three options: ShareScreenshot: Share icon in Teams for iOS , Copy link, and Manage access.

Note

  • If you are trying to share a folder from a third-party cloud storage service, note that third-party cloud storage options are now supported through individual apps you can add to Teams. You will no longer see the “Add cloud storage” in the OneDrive app on Teams’ left navigation bar and within the Files tab in Teams channels. Now you can add the third-party storage app directly from the Teams App Store.
  • Contact your IT admin if cloud storage options don’t appear.

Sharing files in third-party cloud storage

You can add third-party apps to Teams for more storage options. You won’t see the Add cloud storage in OneDriveScreenshot: 3230d89e-d913-43c4-ba36-b48fc14f87f7 in Teams, or in the Shared tab in channels.

Add third-party storage apps directly in Teams by selecting AppsScreenshot: Add an app or tab button on the left side of Teams.

Meetings

Access meeting chat in Microsoft Teams

Access to a Microsoft Teams meeting chat varies depending on an attendee’s relation to the org the meeting is organized in, the way they were invited to the meeting, the type of meeting, and lobby bypass settings.

To learn more about participating in Teams meeting chats, see Chat in Microsoft Teams meetings.

Types of meeting chat access

Temporary access

If an attendee has temporary meeting chat access, they can access the meeting chat from the time they join the meeting until the meeting ends. People who join anonymously retain access until they leave the meeting.

Permanent access

If an attendee has permanent meeting chat access, they can view, send, and receive messages in the meeting chat during and after the meeting until they leave the chat. They also might have access to meeting chat before the meeting starts, depending on how and when they were added.

Important

Only those with meeting chat access when a meeting recording is saved will have automatic access to the recording. To learn more about managing recording access, see Play, share, and download a meeting recording in Microsoft Teams.

Meeting chat capacity

Meeting chat capacity is the maximum number of attendees who can access chat before, during, and after a meeting. Meeting capacity fluctuates based on the type of meeting and when the chat occurs.

  • Before meeting
    • Single-instance meeting: 750 people
    • Meeting series (entire series or single instance): 750 people
  • During meeting
    • Single-instance meeting: 1,000 people
    • Meeting series (entire series or single instance): 1,000 people
  • After meeting
    • Single-instance meeting: 1,000 people
    • Meeting series (entire series or single instance): 750 people
  • Chat capacity is reduced before single-instance meetings to provide more space for people who weren’t directly invited but engage in the meeting (e.g., were requested to join, joined via link, etc.). Up to 1,000 attendees will have permanent access to the meeting chat when the meeting ends.
  • Up to 750 people invited to a meeting series will have permanent chat access at the time the series is scheduled. Up to 250 additional attendees who join the meeting will have chat access until the meeting ends. This provides buffer space in case additional people are invited to future occurrences.
Chat access for contact lists

Inviting a contact list (or contact group) to your meeting invite is an easy way to bulk-invite a large group of people within your org. If the number of people in a contact list exceeds the meeting chat capacity, there are a few nuances to consider:

  • In a meeting series, all members of contact lists that exceed 150 people will have temporary chat access while they’re in the meetings. They won’t have access to chat before or after the meetings.
  • In single-instance meetings, members of contact lists that exceed 150 people will have permanent chat access after they join the meeting. They won’t have access to chat before joining.

To learn more about creating contact lists, see Create, edit, or delete a contact list.

Access meeting chat and chat history

The relation someone has to your org significantly impacts their access to your Teams meeting chat. Their access varies depending on whether they’re:

  • In your org
  • In a trusted org
  • Joining from a trusted Teams (free) account
  • Joining anonymously

Learn more about how meeting chat access varies based on relation to your org below.

People in your org
  • Single instance
    • Invite type: Added to meeting invite , forwarded meeting
    • Chat access (permanent or temporary): Permanent; chat access starts when they’re forwarded or added to the meeting.
    • Invite type: Requested to join during meeting
    • Chat access (permanent or temporary): Permanent; chat access starts when they’re requested to join, regardless of whether they join.
    • Invite type: Joined via link
    • Chat access (permanent or temporary): Permanent; chat access starts when they join the meeting.
    • Invite type: Added directly to meeting chat
    • Chat access (permanent or temporary): Permanent; chat access starts when they’re added to the meeting chat.
  • Meeting series
    • Invite type: Added to meeting invite, forwarded meeting
    • Chat access (permanent or temporary): Permanent; chat access starts when they’re forwarded or added to the meeting.
    • Invite type: Requested to join during meeting
    • Chat access (permanent or temporary): Temporary; chat access starts when they’re requested to join until the meeting ends.
    • Invite type: Joined via link
    • Chat access (permanent or temporary): Temporary; chat access starts when they join until the meeting ends.
    • Invite type: Added directly to meeting chat
    • Chat access (permanent or temporary): Permanent; chat access starts when they’re added to the meeting chat.
  • Single instance of meeting series
    • Invite type: Added to meeting invite, joined via link, forwarded meeting
    • Chat access (permanent or temporary): Temporary; chat access begins when they join until the meeting ends.
    • Invite type: Requested to join during meeting
    • Chat access (permanent or temporary): Temporary; chat access starts when they’re requested to join until the meeting ends.
    • Invite type: Added directly to meeting chat
    • Chat access (permanent or temporary): Permanent; chat access starts when they’re added to the meeting chat.
People from trusted orgs

People from trusted orgs belong to orgs that your IT admin has established a connection with. To learn more, contact your IT admin.

  • Single instance
    • Invite type: Added to meeting invite , forwarded meeting
    • Chat access (permanent or temporary): Permanent; chat access starts when they’re forwarded or added to the meeting. If they can’t bypass the lobby, access begins when they’re let into the meeting.
    • Invite type: Requested to join during meeting
    • Chat access (permanent or temporary): Permanent; chat access starts when they’re requested to join, regardless of whether they join.
    • Invite type: Joined via link
