Teams meetings basics

Join a meeting without a Teams account

Join a meeting without an account in Microsoft Teams

You can join a Teams meeting anytime, from any device, without signing into a Teams account.

If you’re having trouble joining a Teams meeting, try I can’t join a Teams meeting.

Important

 For some meetings, admin settings prevent unverified people from joining the meeting. Depending on the meeting, you may have to enter a one-time passcode sent to your email or create a Teams account.

  • Desktop
  • Mobile

Join the meeting before it starts to test your setup from the pre-join screen. From there, you can enter the meeting up to 15 minutes before its start time to troubleshoot or see how Teams works. Meeting participants and organizers will be notified when you enter the meeting.

To join a Teams meeting without signing into an account:

  1. Open the meeting invite and select the link next to Join or select Join the meeting now.

  2. When prompted, select Continue on this browser or Join on the Teams app. You don’t need to install the Teams app to join the meeting.

    • You can join Teams for web on Microsoft Edge or Google Chrome. You may be prompted to give Teams access to your mic and camera. When you select Allow, you can always turn off your mic and camera once you join the meeting.

  3. Select Join now.

    • In meetings where admin settings prevent unverified people from joining, you’ll be prompted to enter your email address. Enter your email address and select Next. Enter your password if you already have a Microsoft account or select Send code and enter the one-time passcode sent to your email if you don’t have an account. Once verified, select Join now.

Note

People who are signed in will have access to more meeting features than those who aren’t signed in.

If you enter the meeting lobby, wait for someone in the meeting to admit you. If no one admits you within 30 minutes, you’ll be removed from the lobby. If that happens, you can try rejoining.

Depending on how you joined the meeting, other participants will see a label next to your name. If you joined:

  • without entering your email address, everyone will see Unverified next to your name.
  • using a one-time code sent to your email, everyone will see Email verified next to your name.
  • with your Microsoft account, everyone will see External next to your name.

Organizer’s view

If you’re the meeting organizer, we’ll alert you when someone is waiting in the lobby.

Select Admit to let them right into the meeting, or View lobby to see a list of everyone in the lobby and admit or deny them.

Note

Anyone who doesn’t have a Teams account and joins the meeting without entering a one-time passcode sent to their email will be labeled Unverified. Anyone who doesn’t have a Teams account and joins the meeting after entering a one-time passcode sent to their email will be labeled Email verified.

To join a meeting from the Teams mobile app without signing in:

  1. In the meeting invite, tap the link next to Join.

    • If you haven’t downloaded the Teams mobile app, this will take you to the app store to download it. Download the app and tap the meeting link again from the invite.

  2. In the Teams mobile app, allow Teams to access your mic so people in the meeting can hear you.

  3. Tap Join as a guest.

  4. Type your name and tap Join meeting.

    Note

    Depending on policies set by the meeting organizer or their admin, you may be prompted to sign in with an authorized account or enter a one-time passcode sent to your email at this step to join the meeting. In this case, sign in with an authorized account or enter the one-time passcode sent to your email to join.

Once in the meeting, tap the center of your screen to view the meeting controls. From the meeting controls, you can turn your camera and mic on or off. Tap again to hide the controls.

Join a Microsoft Teams meeting on a second device

  • Desktop
  • Mobile

If you’ve joined a meeting on one device, you can join it on another device at the same time. For example, if you’re already in a meeting on your laptop, you can also join on your phone to share live video, control a presentation with your phone, and much more.

You can either transfer the meeting to the second device or keep both devices in the meeting. 

Transfer a meeting from one device to another

  1. While you’re in a meeting on one device, open Teams on the second one (the device you want to transfer the meeting to).
  2. From the new device, select Join call. Screenshot: Banner message with button to join the meeting
  3. Select Transfer to this device. Screenshot: Buttons to add this device or transfer to this device
  4. You can set your audio and video preferences for the meeting on the new device, then select Join.

Once you’re in the meeting on the new device, your first device will leave the meeting. 

Add a second device to a meeting

  1. While you’re in a meeting on one device, open Teams on the second one.
  2. From the second device, select Join call. Screenshot: Banner message with button to join the meeting
  3. Select Add this device. Screenshot: Buttons to add this device or transfer to this device

To prevent an echo effect, Teams will automatically turn off the camera and mic on the second device before it enters the meeting. Once it’s joined, you’ll be able to turn the mic and camera on or off as needed.

With both devices in the meeting, you can now share content from either one.

Leave a meeting on all devices

Ensure your privacy by leaving your meeting from all the devices you joined on with one tap. Whether you entered the meeting from a mobile phone, desktop, or Teams Room, you can close out your call on everything at once.

To leave a meeting on all devices:

  1. In your Teams meeting window, select the arrow next to Leave to open the Leave meeting dropdown menu.

  2. Select Leave on all my devices.

    Screenshot: Screenshot of Leave meeting dropdown in Teams for desktop.

You can use your phone as a companion device for both in-person and virtual meetings.

Important

Make sure you’ve updated to the latest version of Teams on your phone before joining it as a companion device.

Add your mobile device as a companion device to a nearby meeting

If you’re attending an in-person meeting that has a Microsoft Teams Room or Surface Hub set as the location, you can join with your mobile device once you’re there. You can join when the meeting starts, or any time during the meeting.

Note

You must be in the same org as the Teams Room or Surface Hub meeting to use your iPhone as a room companion device.

Note

This feature is available for Android and iPhone. For Surface Hub, the room remote option on your iPhone may not work. Room remote support on Surface Hub coming soon.

  1. From your device, turn on Bluetooth and make sure it’s enabled for Teams.

  2. Open Teams while you’re in the meeting room.

  3. Tap Join with room at the bottom of your screen or Join at the top of your screen. You’ll be joined in the room and on your iPhone at the same time.

To prevent an echo effect, Teams will automatically turn off the speaker, camera, and mic on the second device before it enters the meeting. Once it’s joined and you’ve moved away from the meeting room, you’ll be able to turn the speaker, camera, and mic on or off as needed and you can react, chat, share, and more.

Add your phone as a companion device to a virtual meeting

If you’ve joined a meeting on your laptop, you have the option to join it on your phone at the same time. This can come in handy if, for example, there’s some content on your phone you’d like to share. 

  1. While you’re in a meeting on one device, open Teams on the second one. Tap Join.
  2. Tap Add this device. Screenshot: add this device to meeting

To prevent an echo effect, Teams will automatically turn off the speaker, camera, and mic on the second device before it enters the meeting. Once it’s joined and you’ve moved away from the meeting room, you’ll be able to turn the speaker, camera, and mic on or off as needed.

Turn on your speaker, camera, or mic from a companion device

If you’ve moved away from a nearby or virtual meeting, you can turn on your speaker, camera, or mic from your companion device to engage in the conversation.

  1. To turn on your speaker, tap SpeakerScreenshot: teams speaker icon off at the bottom of your screen. Screenshot: teams select speaker on companion device
  2. To turn on your camera or mic, tap CameraScreenshot: teams show video icon or MicScreenshot: teams unmute icon at the bottom of your screen.
  3. Tap Enable.

Leave a meeting on all devices

Ensure your privacy by leaving your meeting from all the devices you joined on with one tap. Whether you entered the meeting from a mobile phone, desktop, or Teams Room, you can close out your call on everything at once.

To leave a meeting on all devices:
  1. In your Teams meeting window, tap LeaveScreenshot: Leave meeting icon .
  2. Tap Leave on all my devices.

Join a meeting in Teams

Meetings in Teams

Join a Microsoft Teams meeting or event outside your org

Collaborate across companies and departments by joining Microsoft Teams meetings and events outside your org. Ensure a smooth experience regardless of your access level or organizational affiliation by joining as a guest, externally, or from different accounts.

Note

Depending on admin policies, event type, or event settings, external or anonymous join may not be supported.

Join as a guest

A guest is someone who belongs to a different org than the meeting organizer but has been invited by that org’s admin to have guest access.

Redeem your guest account

To join another org’s meeting as a guest, you’ll first need to redeem your guest account. Typically, redeeming guest access is a two-step process: first, the other org will invite you to be a guest. Next, you’ll receive an email invitation where you can accept access.

Sign in to your guest account

To sign in to your guest account:

  1. Launch a new Edge InPrivate window and navigate to the Teams sign in page.

  2. On the Teams sign-in page, select Sign-in optionsScreenshot: key-16x16 .

  3. Select Sign into an organization.

    Screenshot: Screenshot highlighting sign in options for Microsoft Teams.

  4. Enter the other org’s domain name:

    • To find the domain name, open your guest invitation email and look for the domain name next to Domain. You can also find the domain name after the **@** symbol in the sender’s email address.

  5. Enter your guest account’s login information.

  6. Select Accept to approve permissions.

  7. Allow Teams to finish signing in.

  8. Close the browser window.

Join a meeting or event as a guest

To join a meeting or event as a guest:

  1. Sign in to Teams for desktop using your guest account.

  2. Select your profile picture to open your account manager.

  3. To switch orgs, select the option that shows the org you want to switch to. The following example demonstrates switching to the TEST org.

    Screenshot: Screenshot showing how to switch orgs in Microsoft Teams.

  4. Once you’ve switched orgs, select Calendar in Teams.

  5. Select the meeting or event you want to join.

  6. On your pre-join screen, make sure the correct domain name is displayed across the top of the window.

    Screenshot: Screenshot showing how to switch orgs in Teams pre-join screen.

    • If you don’t see the correct domain name at the top-right corner of your Teams window, select Change at the top of the pre-join screen to choose the correct org. Guest orgs will have a briefcase icon Screenshot: briefcase-icon next to them.
    • If you don’t see multiple domain options when you select Change and have redeemed your guest account, quit and restart Teams.

  7. Select Join now.

Join externally

To join a Teams meeting externally, join from the meeting link in your meeting invitation email. From there, choose to join the meeting from your browser or in the Teams for desktop app.

To learn more, see Join a meeting in Microsoft Teams.

Join anonymously or from a different account

To join a Teams meeting from a different account:

  1. Select the meeting in your Teams calendar.

  2. Select Join.

  3. Select Change at the top of the meeting pre-join screen.

  4. Select the account you want to join the meeting with.

    • If you don’t see the account you want to join from, select Add another account. Then, add an existing account, or select Create or use another account to create or sign into a new one.

  5. Select Join to enter the meeting.

To join a Teams meeting anonymously:

  1. Select the meeting in your Teams calendar.
  2. Select Join.
  3. Select Change at the top of the meeting pre-join screen.
  4. Select Join without signing in.
  5. Type your name in at the top of the pre-join screen.
  6. Select Join to enter the meeting.

Install the Teams add-on

Install the Teams add-on directly from the Google Workspace Marketplace or from your Google calendar.

To install the Teams add-on from your Google calendar:

Sign in to the Teams add-on

Troubleshooting

Authorization error

If you receive an Authorize error when you try to add a Microsoft Teams meeting to your Google calendar event, you need to give the add-on access to your Google account.

To give the add-on access to your Google account:

  1. Select the Authorize error text in your Google calendar event, or open the add-on from the side panel.

If you are a Google Workspace admin and have installed the add-on on behalf of our users through the Google Workspace Admin Console, you can authorize the add-on on behalf of all your users.

  1. Open your Google Workspace Admin Console.
  2. Select Apps > Google Workspace Marketplace apps > Apps list.

Not able to enter account information for sign-in

A separate browser window is launched to collect your Microsoft Teams sign-in information. If you don’t see a separate window appear after you’ve selected Sign in, please check your browser settings to make sure pop-up windows are allowed.

Setup Teams and Google calendar sync

The Teams meeting add-on doesn’t currently sync with Google Calendar. To sync your Teams and Google calendars, contact your IT admin.

Laser point or draw on PowerPoint slides in Microsoft Teams meetings

When using PowerPoint Live to share content in a Teams meeting, emphasize your points and engage viewers with the colorful laser pointer and drawing tools. Your “ink” will be visible to everyone in the meeting.

Only the presenter can point and draw on the slides.

To begin sharing, see Share PowerPoint slides. You’ll see the laser pointer and drawing tools beneath the current slide.

Screenshot: Pointer and drawing tools below current slide

Focus viewer attention with the laser pointer

Highlight and connect ideas with the drawing tools

Live event organizer checklist in Microsoft Teams

Important

The Teams live event experience is retiring on June 30, 2026. Please switch to Teams town halls for the newest event features and experience. For more information, please read this blog post.

Equipment setup (non-webcam)

  • If your event requires you to have your own (non-webcam) cameras, make sure you have the right equipment:

    • Cameras
    • Microphones
    • Converter to ingest video into your computer (for example, Magewell)
    • Tripod
    • Cords for connections

Event information

  • Basic information

    • Title
    • Date
    • Location
    • Description

  • Invite everyone who will be producing or presenting (including Q&A moderators) as part of the event group. Wait to invite attendees until you’ve created your event and you have an attendee link.

  • If anyone will be sharing a PowerPoint, invite them as a producer or presenter.

Event settings

  • Carefully set the access to your live event. This is very important if you plan to share sensitive information.

  • Select Q&A if you want to have one.

    • If you select Q&A, make sure someone plans to moderate it (and that you make them a producer or a presenter).

  • Make sure your support link points to the right support info for your attendees.

  • Select Recording available to attendees if you want your attendees to be able to watch a recording of the event on demand.

  • Select Recording available to producers and presenters if you want to get an MP4 file of the recording after the event.

Invite attendees

  • Send the event link to all your attendees as you see fit—share it in a Teams channel, send an email, share it on a website, or add it to a collaboration group.

Test run

  • Make sure all your equipment works and the connections are solid.

  • Connect your Magewell (or other converter) to your USB port and test video and audio. Make sure your video and audio are set properly in your device settings.

  • Confirm that you have good lighting. We recommend choosing a room with natural light.

  • DO NOT click Start during testing. You can’t stop and restart the event later—you’ll have to schedule a new one to send to attendees. (If you want to test this, we recommend that you have a rehearsal live event a few days prior with a small group of people.)

  • Check the attendee link everywhere you’ve sent it to your audience.

    • Your link should point to the actual event. If you follow it, you should see a blue screen that says “The live event hasn’t started.”

  • Make sure you and any presenters have the event content ready to share.

Lock a meeting in Microsoft Teams

In a Teams meeting, meeting organizers and co-organizers can choose to lock their meetings to prevent subsequent join attempts. Anyone attempting to join a locked meeting from any device will be informed that the meeting is locked.

When a meeting is locked, no one else will be able to join, but invitees can still access the meeting chat, the recording, and other meeting info.

  • Desktop
  • Mobile

After joining the meeting:

  1. Select ControlsScreenshot: controls-icon in your meeting controls.
  2. Select Lock meeting > Lock.

To unlock the meeting:

  1. Select ControlsScreenshot: controls-icon in your meeting controls.
  2. Select Lock meeting > Unlock.
  • After joining the meeting, select More actionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > Lock the meetingScreenshot: Privacy settings button (or Unlock the meetingScreenshot: Privacy settings button when locked).

When a meeting is locked, no additional participants can join, but invitees can still access the meeting chat, recording, and other meeting info.

Note

After participants leave the meeting, they cannot join again until the meeting is unlocked.

Manage a live event recording and reports in Microsoft Teams

Important

The Teams live event experience is retiring on June 30, 2026. Please switch to Teams town halls for the newest event features and experience. For more information, please read this blog post.

Once an event is over, producers can take the following actions on the recording and associated reports (if they were configured).

  • Attendee report
    • View in Teams: No
    • Download: Yes
    • Delete: Yes
  • Live event recording
    • View in Teams: No
    • Download: Yes
    • Delete: Yes
  • Hive Insights report
    • View in Teams: No—opens the Hive link in a browser
    • Download: N/A
    • Delete: N/A
  • Q&A report
    • View in Teams: No
    • Download: Yes
    • Delete: Yes
  • Transcript
    • View in Teams: No
    • Download: Yes
    • Delete: Yes

Note

Recordings from live events produced in Teams are currently not saved in Microsoft Stream. You can download the recording from the meeting details and upload it manually to Microsoft Stream after the event.

To manage the reports, select CalendarScreenshot: Meetings button , select the live event, and go to the Event resources section. Screenshot: Event resources

  1. To download a recording or report, select Download next to the item.

  2. To delete all the listed items, select Delete all.

    Note

    If you delete something by mistake, you have up to seven days to restore it.

  3. Select Refresh to see the latest reports related to the live event.

Manage attendee audio and video permissions in Microsoft Teams meetings

Do you organize large meetings or present material in them? To avoid random noise and visual distractions, you can disable attendee mics and cameras. Then, when you want someone to speak or be seen, you can let them turn their mic or camera back on.

Note

Currently attendees who call in to a meeting using the phone number provided in the meeting details won’t be prevented from turning on their mic and camera.

For info on which meeting participants are classified as “attendees,” see Roles in a Teams meeting.

  • Desktop
  • Mobile

Prevent mic and camera use

Before the meeting

After scheduling the meeting and sending out the invite, the meeting organizer can disable the mics and cameras so that attendees can’t use them during the meeting. All attendees (but not presenters) will join the meeting with mic and camera off.

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: Teams Calendar tab icon in Teams.
  2. Double-click the meeting to open its details.
  3. Select OptionsScreenshot: skype-teams-mobile-icon-settings .
  4. Select ParticipationScreenshot: Icon for Participation in Microsoft Teams .
  5. Turn off the Allow mic for attendees or Allow camera for attendees toggles.
  6. Select Apply.
During the meeting

Organizers, co-organizers, and presenters can turn off the mic or camera of all the attendees, or of individuals, at any time during the meeting.

Note

Currently this option isn’t available to organizers and presenters who join the meeting from Teams room devices.

To disable all attendee mics or cameras
  1. In the meeting controls, select ControlsScreenshot: controls-icon > View more options. You can also access these options by selecting OptionsScreenshot: Settings button when scheduling the meeting.
  2. Select Roles. Change Who can present from Everyone to the desired level of control in the meeting. If this is set to Everyone, the mic and camera won’t be disabled for attendees.
  3. Select ParticipationScreenshot: Icon for Participation in Microsoft Teams .
  4. Turn off the Allow mic for attendees or Allow camera for attendees toggles.
  5. Select Apply.

Attendee mics and cameras will appear dimmed.

Return to these settings later to enable everyone’s mic or camera.

Mute an attendee

To mute a specific attendee, without turning off mics:

  1. Select PeopleScreenshot: People or Show Participants button .
  2. In the Participants pane, hover over the person you want to mute.
  3. Select More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > Mute participantScreenshot: Muted microphone button .

To mute all participants without disabling their mics, select Mute all.

Tip

Attendees can signal that they want to speak by raising their hands.

Prevent mic and camera use

Before the meeting

After scheduling the meeting and sending out the invite, the meeting organizer can disable the mics and cameras so that attendees can’t use them during the meeting. All attendees (but not presenters) will join the meeting with mic and camera off.

  1. Tap CalendarScreenshot: Teams Calendar tab icon in Teams.
  2. Tap the meeting.
  3. In Details, tap See more > Meeting options.
  4. In ParticipationScreenshot: Icon for Participation in Microsoft Teams , turn off the Allow mic for attendees or Allow camera for attendees toggles.
  5. Tap Save.
During the meeting

The meeting organizer, co-organizers, and presenters can turn off attendee mics and cameras anytime during the meeting.

To turn off all attendee mic and cameras
  1. In the meeting controls, tap MoreScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon .
  2. Tap People > Manage audio and videoScreenshot: Settings button .
  3. In Participant Settings, turn the Disable mic for attendees and Disable camera for attendees toggles on.

Tip

If you just want to mute participants without disabling their mics, go to the participant list and select Mute all next to In the meeting.

To turn off an individual attendee’s mic
  • Tap and hold the person’s name, either on the main screen or in the participant list, and tap Mute participantScreenshot: teams unmute icon .

Tip

Attendees can signal that they want to speak by raising their hand.

Manage audio settings in Microsoft Teams meetings

In Teams, easily adjust your audio settings before and during a call or meeting.

Note

Make sure your device audio settings and browser audio settings are configured to give Teams access to your device speakers and mic.

  • Desktop
  • Mobile

Change audio sources

When you join a Teams meeting, you can choose your source of audio from the meeting pre-join screen. Available audio settings vary depending on the source you choose.

If you’re joining from the Teams desktop app, you can choose from several audio source options before you join.

Screenshot: Choose your audio source for a meeting from the pre-join screen.

  • Computer audio
    • When you choose this…: Your computer’s default speaker and mic will be used during the meeting.
  • Phone audio
    • When you choose this…: Your phone mic and speakers will be your audio source during the meeting. After you join, you’ll have two options: Enter your phone number to receive a call connecting you to the meeting from your phone. Select Dial in manually to view a phone number you can call into the meeting with. You’ll still be able to participate in the meeting from the device you originally joined from, but that device will be muted and your phone mic and speakers will be the audio sources.
  • Room audio
    • When you choose this…: You’ll add or select a meeting room from the dropdown menu. The room’s audio system will be your meeting audio source.
  • Don’t use audio
    • When you choose this…: You’ll join the meeting muted.

If you choose an audio source other than Computer audio, you can choose to switch back to computer audio during the meeting by selecting UnmuteScreenshot: Muted microphone button in the Teams meeting controls.

Change speaker and mic settings

Adjust your speaker and mic settings in your Teams settings or when you join a Teams meeting. You can change settings before you join or while you’re in a meeting.

Note

Some audio settings may be unavailable depending on policies set by meeting organizers or your IT admin.

In Teams

To open your audio device settings:

  1. In Teams, select Settings and moreScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > SettingsScreenshot: Settings button .

  2. Select DevicesScreenshot: Teams settings device icon .

  3. In Devices, select Manage devices to connect or disconnect your audio devices.

  4. In Audio > Audio settingsScreenshot: Teams audio settings :

    • Select the connected speaker you want to use from the Speaker dropdown menu.
    • Select the connected mic you want to use from the Microphone dropdown menu.
    • Turn the Automatically adjust mic sensitivity toggle on to ensure everyone hears you at a level volume during a meeting.
    • Turn the Sync device buttons toggle on to sync your Teams audio device and use all its buttons during a meeting.

  5. Select Make a test callScreenshot: Test call button icon to test your settings.

  6. In Noise suppression:

    • Select Background noise only to suppress noises around you and minimize disruption during a call.

    • Select Voice isolation to suppress other voices that might come through your mic and make sure others in your meeting only hear your voice.

      Note

      This requires creating a voice profile if you’re not using a headset.

  7. Turn on the Spatial audio toggle to experience more immersive sound during your Teams meeting. To learn more, see Spatial audio in Microsoft Teams meetings.

In a meeting

Change audio settings from the meeting pre-join screen or in the meeting window after you join.

To access audio settings from the pre-join screen:

  1. Join a meeting from your Teams calendar.

  2. On the pre-join screen, select your audio source.

    Screenshot: Choose your audio source for a meeting from the pre-join screen.

    • If you select Computer audio, select Audio settingsScreenshot: Meeting options icon to access more audio settings. Changes to your audio settings will be applied when you join the meeting.

  3. Select Join now.

To access audio settings after you join a meeting:

  1. In the meeting controls, select MicScreenshot: Teams microphone icon to mute yourself or MicScreenshot: Muted microphone button to unmute yourself.
  2. Select the dropdown arrow next to Mic for other settings. To see advanced audio settings, select More audio settings.

Audio setting changes made during a meeting will take effect immediately.

Share sound while screensharing

If you’re sharing your screen during a meeting, you can include sound to let others hear what’s playing on your shared screen.

To share sound while screensharing:

  1. Join a Teams meeting.

  2. Select ShareScreenshot: Teams share screen icon in the meeting controls.

  3. Turn on the Include sound toggle.

    Screenshot: Turn on the Include sound toggle to share sound from the window youre sharing.

  4. Select the window you want to share to start screensharing. Participants will be able to hear audio from content on that screen while you’re sharing.

Change audio sources

When you join a Teams meeting, you can choose your source of audio from the meeting pre-join screen. Available audio settings vary depending on the source you choose.

Note

Make sure your device audio settings are configured to give Teams access to your device speakers and mic.

If you’re joining a Teams meeting from your mobile device, your device will be your default audio source. Before you join, you can change your audio source by tapping More join options on the meeting pre-join screen.

You can choose from several audio source options.

Screenshot: Select an audio source from the mobile meeting pre-join screen.

  • Join without audio
    • When you choose this…: You’ll instantly join the meeting with your device’s mic and speakers muted.
  • Call me
    • When you choose this…: You’ll be prompted to enter a phone number to a different device. Tap Call to receive a call on that device that connects you to the Teams meeting. The device you call will be the audio source for that meeting, but you’ll be able to participate in other meeting capabilities, like chat and content sharing, from the device you originally joined on.
  • Dial in
    • When you choose this…: You’ll be given a phone number to dial into the meeting from. When you tap Call , you’ll be prompted to call the Teams meeting through your mobile device. Note: If you’re dialing in as a meeting organizer, you’ll need to enter your meeting PIN to join. If you’re dialing in as an attendee, you’ll be placed in the lobby until someone lets you into the meeting.
  • Join a meeting room
    • When you choose this…: You’ll be prompted to add or select a meeting room to join from. Tap Join to enter the meeting. When you join from a meeting room, the room’s audio system will be your meeting audio source.

Mute and unmute your mic

Before a meeting

  1. Tap a meeting on your Teams Calendar.

  2. Tap Join.

  3. On the meeting pre-join screen:

    1. Tap MicScreenshot: Teams microphone icon to mute yourself.
    2. Tap MicScreenshot: Muted microphone button to unmute yourself.

  4. Tap Join now.

During a meeting

  1. In the meeting controls:

    1. Tap MicScreenshot: Teams microphone icon to mute yourself.
    2. Tap MicScreenshot: Muted microphone button to unmute yourself.

Change your speaker

Before a meeting
  1. Tap a meeting on your Teams Calendar.
  2. Tap Join.
  3. Tap SpeakerScreenshot: teams speaker icon on the pre-join screen.
  4. Tap the speaker you’d like to use.
  5. Tap Join now.
During a meeting
  1. In the meeting controls, tap SpeakerScreenshot: teams speaker icon .
  2. Tap the speaker you’d like to use.
  3. Tap Audio off to turn off your mic and speaker.

Manage breakout rooms in Microsoft Teams

Foster connections and meaningful discussions in medium to large Teams meetings by creating breakout rooms. Create and manage breakout rooms when you use Teams for desktop to organize a meeting with up to 300 people.

To learn more about participating in breakout room sessions, see Join a breakout room in Microsoft Teams meetings.

Note

These features aren’t currently available in breakout rooms:

  • Adding people to the meeting from the participant’s panel
  • Adding additional people to the meeting chat
  • Copying the Join meeting info

Create breakout rooms

To create breakout rooms, you must be a meeting organizer or a presenter in the meeting organizer’s organization who’s been appointed a breakout rooms manager.

Before a meeting

To create breakout rooms before a meeting, first schedule a meeting and send invites. Then:

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: Teams Calendar tab icon in Teams.

  2. Select a meeting.

  3. Select View event .

  4. Select More options > Breakout rooms .

    This option will only appear after invites have been sent to attendees.

  5. Select Create rooms.

  6. Choose the number of rooms you want (up to 50) and select Add rooms.

  7. Select Assign participantsScreenshot: Add people icon .

  8. Choose how you want participants to be assigned and select Next > Save.

If you create breakout rooms before a meeting starts, you can invite up to 300 people. As soon as the meeting starts, you can open the breakout rooms.

During a meeting

To create breakout rooms during a meeting:

  1. Select RoomsScreenshot: Breakout rooms icon in the meeting controls.
  2. Choose the number of rooms you want to create (up to 50).
  3. Choose how you want participants to be assigned.
  4. Select Create rooms.

To add another breakout room during the meeting, select RoomsScreenshot: Breakout rooms icon   > Add roomScreenshot: Add button in the meeting controls.

Note

You won’t be able to automatically assign people to breakout rooms later in the meeting.

Manage breakout room settings

Adjust breakout room settings before a meeting to ensure your meeting and rooms run smoothly. Choose how participants will be assigned to rooms, set room time limits, and more.

Room settings are flexible and can also be changed during the meeting. Rename rooms, open and close them, and make other adjustments as you go.

Before a meeting

To manage breakout room settings before a meeting:

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: Teams Calendar tab icon in Teams.

  2. Select a meeting.

  3. Select View event .

  4. Select More options > Breakout rooms .

    This option will only appear after invites have been sent to attendees.

  5. Select Rooms settingsScreenshot: Settings icon .

  6. Select Save to apply changes.

During a meeting

To manage breakout room settings during a meeting:

  1. Select RoomsScreenshot: Breakout rooms icon in the meeting controls.
  2. Select Rooms settingsScreenshot: Settings icon .
  3. Select Save to apply changes.

Set breakout room time limits

Set breakout room time limits to keep your meeting on-track across breakout rooms. Rooms will automatically close when the time expires and participants will rejoin the main meeting.

Note

Turn off the Automatically move people to rooms toggle in breakout room settings to allow participants to either rejoin the main meeting or leave altogether after time expires.

Before a meeting

To set a breakout room time limit before a meeting:

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: Teams Calendar tab icon in Teams.

  2. Select a meeting.

  3. Select View event .

  4. Select More options > Breakout rooms .

    This option will only appear after invites have been sent to attendees.

  5. Select Rooms settingsScreenshot: Settings icon .

  6. Turn the Set a time limit toggle on.

  7. Set a time limit using the dropdown menus.

  8. Select Save.

During a meeting

To set a breakout room time limit during a meeting:

  1. Select RoomsScreenshot: Breakout rooms icon in the meeting controls.
  2. Select Rooms settingsScreenshot: Settings icon .
  3. Turn the Set a time limit toggle on.
  4. Set a time limit using the dropdown menus.
  5. Select Save.

Appoint breakout room managers

Appoint breakout room managers in a meeting for more help managing the rooms. Breakout room managers can:

  • Assign and reassign participants to rooms
    • Set time limits for room sessions: Send announcements
  • Open and close rooms
    • Set time limits for room sessions: Recreate rooms
  • Join any room

To make someone a breakout room manager, first invite them to the meeting and make them a presenter. To learn more, see Roles in Microsoft Teams meetings.

Before a meeting

To appoint breakout room managers before a meeting:

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: Teams Calendar tab icon in Teams.

  2. Select a meeting.

  3. Select View event .

  4. Select More options > Breakout rooms .

    This option will only appear after invites have been sent to attendees.

  5. Select Rooms settingsScreenshot: Settings icon .

  6. Turn the Assign presenters to manage rooms toggle on.

  7. Select Search for presenters and designate room managers.

  8. Select Save.

During a meeting

To appoint breakout room managers during a meeting:

  1. In the meeting controls, select RoomsScreenshot: Breakout rooms icon .
  2. Select Rooms settingsScreenshot: Settings button .
  3. Turn the Assign presenters to manage rooms toggle on.
  4. Choose presenters from the dropdown menu.
  5. Select Save.
Manage breakout rooms

Only one breakout manager can take control of breakout rooms at a time.

To take control of breakout rooms as a breakout room manager:

  1. Select RoomsScreenshot: Breakout rooms icon in the meeting controls. You’ll be able to see who currently has control of the rooms.
  2. Select Manage rooms.

You’re now in control of the breakout rooms. Join open rooms, make announcements, and more.

Rename breakout rooms

If you want, rename a breakout room to reflect its purpose (for example, what people in that room will be discussing or working on).

Before a meeting

To rename a breakout room before a meeting:

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: Teams Calendar tab icon in Teams.

  2. Select a meeting.

  3. Select View event .

  4. Select More options > Breakout rooms .

    This option will only appear after invites have been sent to attendees.

  5. On the room you want to rename, select More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > RenameScreenshot: Edit icon .

  6. Enter a new name.

  7. Select Rename.

During a meeting

To rename a breakout room during a meeting:

  1. Select RoomsScreenshot: Breakout rooms icon in the meeting controls.
  2. Hover over the room you want to rename
  3. Select More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > RenameScreenshot: Edit icon .
  4. Enter a new name.
  5. Select Rename.

Send an announcement to all breakout rooms

Communicate with people across all breakout rooms by sending an announcement. Offer discussion ideas, update participants on what’s next, and more.

To send an announcement to all breakout rooms:

  1. Select RoomsScreenshot: Breakout rooms icon in the meeting controls.
  2. Select Make an announcementScreenshot: Announcement icon. .
  3. Enter your announcement and select Send.

People will see your announcement in their room’s chat, marked as IMPORTANT. If they reply to your announcement, you’ll see it in the chat for that breakout room in your main chat list.

Open and close breakout rooms

Open rooms

Open breakout rooms when you’re ready to start the sessions. If you chose to manually or randomly assign participants to rooms, they’ll join the open rooms right away unless you turn off the Automatically move people to rooms toggle in breakout room settings. If you choose to let participants self-select their rooms, they can view and join the open rooms.

To open and start breakout room sessions in a meeting:

  1. Select RoomsScreenshot: Breakout rooms icon in the meeting controls.

    • Select Open rooms to open all the rooms at the same time.
    • Hover over a room and select More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > Open to open that specific room.

Rooms will remain open until you manually close them or, if you set a time limit, the time expires.

Close rooms

Close breakout rooms when you’re ready to end the sessions and have participants return to the main meeting.

To close and end breakout room sessions in a meeting:

  1. Select RoomsScreenshot: Breakout rooms icon in the meeting controls.

    • Select Close rooms to close all the rooms at the same time.
    • Hover over a room and select More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > Close to close that specific room.

A room has successfully closed when its status changes to Closed. If you reopen rooms in a meeting where participants were assigned to rooms, participants will return to the rooms they were assigned to.

Delete breakout rooms

To delete a breakout room, the room must be closed first. If people are in the room, reassign them to different rooms before closing the room they’re in, or close the room to move them back into the main meeting automatically.

Before a meeting

To delete breakout rooms before a meeting:

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: Teams Calendar tab icon in Teams.

  2. Select a meeting.

  3. Select View event .

  4. Select More options > Breakout rooms .

    This option will only appear after invites have been sent to attendees.

  5. Select Remove roomsScreenshot: Delete button trashcan icon to delete all the breakout rooms.

    • Hover over a room and select More options > DeleteScreenshot: Delete button trashcan icon to delete that room only.

  6. Confirm.

During a meeting

To delete breakout rooms during a meeting:

  1. Select RoomsScreenshot: Breakout rooms icon in the meeting controls.

    • Select Remove roomsScreenshot: Delete button trashcan icon to delete all the breakout rooms.
    • Hover over a room and select More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > DeleteScreenshot: Delete button trashcan icon to delete that room.

  2. Confirm.

Attendance reports for breakout rooms

If you organize a meeting, you can gain insight into its participants and their breakout room activity through attendance reports. Learn which breakout room each person has joined, when they entered it, and when they left.

To view breakout room data from a meeting:

  1. Select Chat in Teams.
  2. Select Meeting chats and open the meeting chat.
  3. Select Attendance.
  4. Under Participants, select an attendee to see which breakout room they entered and what time they joined and left it.

To reference breakout room data later, download the attendance report in CSV format.

Note

  • Only meeting organizers can view attendance reports.
  • Attendance reports don’t include data from deleted breakout rooms.

Manage meeting attendance reports in Microsoft Teams

Enable attendance reports to view and download important attendance details, like who attended and what time people joined and left, during and after your meeting. Only organizers and co-organizers can view and download attendance reports.

  • Desktop
  • Mobile

Turn attendance reports on or off

Organizers can turn attendance reports on or off in meetings they create.

Before a meeting

To turn attendance reports on or off before a meeting:

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: Teams Calendar tab icon in Teams.
  2. Select an event and select View eventScreenshot: teams-expand-icon .
  3. Select OptionsScreenshot: Settings icon .
  4. In ParticipationScreenshot: Icon for Participation in Microsoft Teams , turn the Allow attendance report toggle on or off.
  5. Select Apply.

For more help managing meeting attendance reports, contact your IT admin.

During a meeting

To turn attendance reports on or off during a meeting:

  1. Start a Teams meeting.
  2. Select ControlsScreenshot: controls-icon> View more options in your meeting controls.
  3. In ParticipationScreenshot: Icon for Participation in Microsoft Teams turn the Allow attendance report toggle on or off.
  4. Select Apply.

View and download attendance reports

View and download Teams attendance reports directly in Teams after an event ends. Reports are stored along with the organizer’s other data, like emails and contacts.

Organizers and co-organizers can view and download attendance reports in the event chat about five minutes after the event ends. Recurring meetings will have a unique attendance report for each instance of the series.

To view and download an attendance report:

  1. Select ChatScreenshot: Teams Chat Tab icon in Teams.
  2. Open the past meeting or event chat.
  3. Select the Attendance tab.
  4. Select DownloadScreenshot: Teams download arrow icon to download the attendance report as a .csv file.

You can also download an attendance report during a meeting by selecting PeopleScreenshot: People or Show Participants button in your meeting controls and selecting More actionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > Download attendance listScreenshot: Teams download arrow icon in the Participants pane.

Note

  • If the event organizer leaves the org, reports are permanently deleted and can’t be retrieved.
  • Co-organizers can only view and download reports from events scheduled in Teams, not Outlook.

Hide identity in attendance reports

You can decide whether you want your identity shown in attendance reports.

To hide your identity in attendance reports:

  1. Go to Settings and moreScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > SettingsScreenshot: Settings button in Teams.
  2. Select PrivacyScreenshot: Privacy settings button .
  3. Turn the Identify me in attendance reports toggle on or off.

Engagement information

Organizers can view and download meeting engagement data such as total reactions, raised hands, cameras turned on, and more in the Attendance tab after a scheduled meeting or event.

Screenshot: Engagement information available in the Attendance tab of a meeting.

Known issues and limitations

  • In meetings with more than 120 participants, the attendance report available during the meeting will only include some attendees. The post-meeting report will contain all attendees.
  • The report doesn’t include insights from deleted breakout rooms.
  • The report doesn’t currently include view-only attendees.
  • If a channel meeting is in progress and someone starts a second meeting within the same channel conversation, an attendance report will be available only for the second meeting.
  • If someone waits in the lobby and doesn’t get admitted to the meeting, they won’t be included in the report.
  • When a participant is on hold in a meeting, their info is still included for this period of time in the attendance report.
  • Attendance reports aren’t supported for instant channel meetings.
  • Engagement reports limit how many actions are logged for each attendee (hand raises, mutes/unmutes, etc.).
  • Co-organizers can’t access attendance reports for channel meetings.

View attendance reports directly in the Microsoft Teams mobile app to gain insight into your meetings and webinars. See webinar registration data, times that attendees joined and left meetings, and much more.

Note

To see all attendance report data, view the report on Teams for desktop or web.

Turn attendance reports on or off

To turn attendance reports on or off before your meeting:

  1. Tap CalendarScreenshot: Teams Calendar tab icon in Teams.
  2. Tap a meeting.
  3. In Details, tap See more > Meeting options.
  4. In ParticipationScreenshot: Icon for Participation in Microsoft Teams , turn the Allow attendance report toggle on or off.
  5. Tap Save.

Participants can decide if they want to show or hide their information in attendance reports.

To change your attendance report privacy settings:

  1. Tap your profile picture in Teams.
  2. Tap SettingsScreenshot: Settings button > PrivacyScreenshot: Privacy settings button .
  3. Tap Attendance report data.
  4. Turn the Identify me in attendance reports toggle on or off.

For more help managing your meeting attendance report settings, contact your IT admin.

Open an attendance report

To open an attendance report:

  1. Tap ChatScreenshot: Teams Chat Tab icon in Teams.
  2. Open the past meeting chat history.
  3. In the Meeting ended message, tap AttendanceScreenshot: Attendance icon in Microsoft Teams .

Share an attendance report

To open an attendance report:

  1. Open an attendance report.

    • If you’re using an iOS device, tap ShareScreenshot: Teams iOS share icon .
    • If you’re using an Android device, tap ShareScreenshot: Android share button .

  2. Choose how you want to share the report.

  3. Send the report.

Manage town hall emails in Microsoft Teams

When you publish a town hall in Microsoft Teams, attendees will automatically receive email invites and recording updates from Teams.

Customize emails or turn them off completely from the event details in your Teams calendar.

Edit town hall emails

In Teams, town hall emails are generated using a template that automatically fills in details from the event scheduling form.

Keep the emails as they are or customize them from the event details in your Teams calendar.

Email invites

Teams email invites will contain important details, including the event name, date and time, and description. They’ll also reflect your event’s customized theming.

To add or change details, edit the invites before publishing your town hall.

To edit town hall email invites:

  1. Go to your Teams calendar.

  2. Open an existing town hall or schedule a new one.

  3. Select Emails.

  4. In the Event invitation row, select Edit.

    Screenshot: Screenshot highlighting UI to preview town hall email invitations

  5. Make changes in the email template.

    Screenshot: Screenshot showing how to edit town hall email invitations

  6. Select Preview email to see how the email will appear to invitees.

    Note

    The email preview might look different to some recipients depending on their email service and device.

  7. Select Edit email to keep editing, Cancel to discard edits, or Save to apply your changes.

After you publish the town hall, attendees will receive an email invite.

Event recording emails

After your event ends, you can publish the event recording for attendees. Attendees will automatically receive an email notifying them that the event recording is available.

Add follow-up details, links, and more by editing the event recording email.

To edit the event recording email:

  1. Go to your Teams calendar.

  2. Open the town hall details.

  3. Select Emails.

  4. In the Event recording available row, select Edit.

  5. Make changes in the email template.

  6. Select Preview email to see how the email will appear to invitees.

    Note

    The email preview might look different to some recipients depending on their email service and device.

  7. Select Edit email to keep editing, Cancel to discard edits, or Save to apply your changes.

Turn off town hall emails

Town hall emails are turned on automatically when you create a town hall. You can turn them off at any time before you publish the event site.

To turn off town hall emails while scheduling a town hall:

  1. In the scheduling form, go to Details > Invite attendees.
  2. Turn the Enable attendees emails toggle off.
  3. Select SaveScreenshot: Save icon .

To turn off town hall emails for a scheduled town hall:

  1. Go to your Teams calendar.
  2. Right-click a town hall and select Manage eventScreenshot: Edit icon .
  3. Go to Details > Invite attendees.
  4. Turn the Enable attendees emails toggle off.
  5. Select SaveScreenshot: Save icon .

Important

  • Changing this setting will turn off all town hall emails, including email invites.
  • You can only change this setting before the event site is published.

Record a town hall

Go to Details > Meeting optionsScreenshot: Settings icon > Recording and transcriptionScreenshot: teams-record-and-transcribe-button-icon . Meeting roles, your org’s license, and admin policies also determine who can record and transcribe.

Record a town hall manually

Download a town hall recording

To translate a town hall transcript:

  2. Select a past town hall.

The translated transcript will appear in the Transcript and captionsScreenshot: Start transcription button menu.

Publish a town hall recording

After recording a town hall, publish the recording to make it available to attendees.

To publish a town hall recording:

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: teams-calendar-tab-icon in Teams.

  2. Select a past town hall.

Only one recording can be published at a time. After you publish a recording, attendees will be notified by email. External presenters won’t receive an email notification.

Extend town hall recording access

Published town hall recordings expire, but you can extend how long they’re available. To extend a town hall recording:

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: teams-calendar-tab-icon in Teams.
  2. Select a past town hall.
  3. Select View eventScreenshot: teams-expand-icon > Manage eventScreenshot: edit-icon .
  4. Select Recordings.

If a recording expires after you extended it, republish it to make it available again for attendees.

View a town hall recording

To view a town hall recording:

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: teams-calendar-tab-icon in Teams.
  2. Select a past town hall.
  3. Select View eventScreenshot: teams-expand-icon > Manage eventScreenshot: edit-icon .
  4. In Recordings, select the recording you want to view.

Attendees can view a town hall recording after you publish it. When it’s published, they’ll receive an email with a link to the recording.

You can also find town hall recordings and transcripts by selecting the past town hall in your Teams calendar and selecting the Recap tab. From there, you can watch the recording, search the transcript, and more. To learn more, see Recap in Microsoft Teams.

Share a town hall recording

To share a town hall recording:

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: teams-calendar-tab-icon in Teams.
  2. Select a past town hall.
  3. Select View eventScreenshot: teams-expand-icon > Manage eventScreenshot: edit-icon .

Anyone with event access can view the shared recording. To learn more about event access, see Schedule a town hall in Microsoft Teams.

Remove a town hall recording

To remove a town hall recording:

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: teams-calendar-tab-icon in Teams.
  2. Select a past town hall.
  3. Select View eventScreenshot: teams-expand-icon > Manage eventScreenshot: edit-icon .
  4. In Recordings, choose the recording you want to remove.
  5. Select Remove.

Manage webinar emails in Microsoft Teams

Notify, remind, and update registered attendees about an upcoming webinar with webinar emails.

Types of webinar emails

There are different types of webinar emails that inform and remind people about their approval status, event details, and more.

  • Attendee registration
    • What it does: Notifies recipient that their spot is reserved for the event.
    • When it’s sent: Immediately
  • Attendee pending approval
    • What it does: Informs recipient that their registration request has been received.
    • When it’s sent: Immediately
  • Attendee waitlisting
    • What it does: Informs recipient that the event is full, but they’ve been added to the waitlist & will be notified if a spot opens up.
    • When it’s sent: Immediately
  • Attendee rejection
    • What it does: Informs recipient that the event is at capacity and their registration request can’t be accepted.
    • When it’s sent: Immediately
  • Attendee cancellation
    • What it does: Confirms registration cancellation by an attendee.
    • When it’s sent: Immediately
  • Webinar cancellation
    • What it does: Notifies registered attendee that the event has been cancelled.
    • When it’s sent: Immediately
  • Webinar date time update
    • What it does: Updates registered attendee about changes to the event’s date or time.
    • When it’s sent: Immediately
  • Webinar reminder
    • What it does: Reminds registered attendee about the upcoming webinar.
    • When it’s sent: 1h before event starts*
  • Event recording available
    • What it does: Notifies attendee that the event recording is published and ready to review. Event recording emails won’t be sent to external presenters.
    • When it’s sent: As soon as recording is published

Modifying reminder email send times is unavailable for events scheduled less than an hour before their start times.

Edit webinar emails

Note

  • Editing webinar emails is an advanced feature, available in events with up to 3,000 attendees. For use of this feature in larger events, your org must have attendee capacity packs to enable instances up to 100,000.
  • If you had Teams Premium prior to April 1, 2026, you’ll continue to have access to this feature in events up to 100,000 attendees until the expiration of your license. To learn more about Teams licensing for events, please contact your IT admin.

By default, webinar emails are automatically drafted using templates in Teams. However, in events of up to 3,000 attendees, edit them before they’re sent.

To edit webinar emails:

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: teams-calendar-tab-icon in Teams.

  2. Select the webinar you want to edit emails for.

  3. Select View eventScreenshot: teams-expand-icon > Manage eventScreenshot: edit-pencil-icon-20x20-png .

  4. Select Emails.

    Screenshot: Screenshot of communications tab in webinar setup options, showing webinar emails

  5. Select Edit in the row of the email you want to edit. You can edit:

    • Sender name

    • Email subject

    • Banner and logo images

    • Body of the email

      Screenshot: Screenshot of webinar email template in Microsoft Teams.

  6. Make changes to the content of the email. Then:

    • Select Preview email to see how the email will look to recipients.
    • Select Keep editing to make more changes,
    • Select Cancel to discard your edits.

  7. Select Save.

Important

If an organizer doesn’t edit reminder email content, each attendee and organizer will see the email translated in their browser’s default language. If an organizer customizes the email, attendees will see it as it was written in the organizer’s language.

Change reminder email send time

By default, reminder emails will be sent to registrants an hour before the event starts. In events of up to 3,000 attendees, edit the send time to notify attendees sooner.

Note

  • Changing reminder email send times is an advanced feature, available in events with up to 3,000 attendees. For use of this feature in larger events, your org must have attendee capacity packs to enable instances up to 100,000.
  • If you had Teams Premium prior to April 1, 2026, you’ll continue to have access to this feature in events up to 100,000 attendees until the expiration of your license. To learn more about Teams licensing for events, please contact your IT admin.

To change the reminder email send time:

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: teams-calendar-tab-icon in Teams.

  2. Select the webinar you want to edit emails for.

  3. Select View eventScreenshot: teams-expand-icon > Manage eventScreenshot: edit-pencil-icon-20x20-png .

  4. Select Emails.

  5. In the Reminder email row, select 1h before event starts.

    Screenshot: Screenshot of how to edit webinar reminder emails send time

  6. Set how many hours or days before the event to send the reminder email. Select Save.

Screenshot: Screenshot of reminder email send time editor in Teams.

Webinar email reminders must be sent a minimum of one hour before the event starts.

Turn off webinar emails

Webinar emails are turned on automatically when you create a webinar. You can turn them off at any time before you publish the event site.

To turn off webinar emails while scheduling a webinar:

  1. In the scheduling form, go to Setup > Details.
  2. Under Event access, turn the Enable attendee emails toggle off.

To turn off webinar emails for a scheduled webinar:

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: teams-calendar-tab-icon in Teams.
  2. Select the webinar you want to edit emails for.
  3. Select View eventScreenshot: teams-expand-icon > Manage eventScreenshot: edit-pencil-icon-20x20-png .
  4. In Details > Event access, turn the Enable attendee emails toggle off.

Important

  • This setting will turn off all Teams webinar emails, including cancellation and event recording emails.
  • You can only change this setting before the event site is published.

Manage emails through integrations

Set up and manage webinar emails by integrating non-Microsoft marketing automation tools into Teams. Implement webinar integrations before publishing the event site.

To start using webinar integrations:

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: teams-calendar-tab-icon in Teams.
  2. Select the webinar you want to edit emails for.
  3. Select View eventScreenshot: teams-expand-icon > Manage eventScreenshot: edit-pencil-icon-20x20-png .
  4. In the scheduling form, select Connect apps.
  5. Select the marketing automation tool you want to use for your webinar. This will take you to the documentation, where you can find instructions to set up the necessary integrations.

Record a webinar

Stop recording a webinar

By default, a webinar will start recording automatically when the event begins. To prevent a webinar from automatically recording, you’ll need to turn off automatic recording in your webinar settings before the event starts. You can also stop recording during the webinar.

Before a webinar

Publish a webinar recording

Manage webinar registration in Microsoft Teams

Add structure to your webinar with additional registration settings and requirements. To modify attendee registration, open the webinar from your Teams calendar and go to Registration > Configuration.

Screenshot: 00f3e35f-c0f8-4fe5-93ad-33b0ebd0b7d8

From here, you can implement the following:

  • Event capacity - set a limit on how many people can register for the webinar.
  • Require manual approval of all event registrations* - decide who can attend the webinar by approving or denying registration requests.
  • Enable waitlist for this event* - after the event capacity is full, manage overflow registration requests by implementing a waitlist. The waitlist capacity will be equal to the event’s capacity.
  • Limit registration date* - set a time window during which potential attendees can register for your event.

*Advanced registration features.

Note

If you don’t have registration abilities in your event configuration, contact your IT admin.

Set registration start and end time

Note

  • Limiting registration start/end times is an advanced registration feature, available in events with up to 3,000 attendees. For use of this feature in larger events, your org must have attendee capacity packs to enable instances up to 100,000.
  • If you had Teams Premium prior to April 1, 2026, you’ll continue to have access to this feature in events up to 100,000 attendees until the expiration of your license. To learn more about Teams licensing for events, please contact your IT admin.

Limit when potential attendees can register for the webinar by setting registration start and end times.

To set registration start and end times:

  1. Go to Registration > Configuration.

  2. Select Limit registration date.

  3. Designate the registration window in the Start date and End date drop-down menus.

    Screenshot: 17ef9e01-38bd-4c2a-abc5-c4cd472a9b32

Manage registration

Add questions to a webinar registration form to learn more about your audience, including details about their background, how they heard about the event, and more. You can also include legal terms for potential attendees to view and accept.

Add registration fields

To add fields to the registration form:

  1. Go to Registration > Configuration.

  2. Under Form, select Add field.

    Screenshot: e2e093ee-b9e9-493f-b447-635791fd5b36

  3. Choose from preset fields or select Custom question to create your own.

  4. Once you’ve added a field or question, select Required to add it to the registration form.

Note

By default, registration is open until the event ends unless the organizer enables and sets a different registration end time.

View form answers

To view a potential attendee’s form answers:

  1. Go to Registration > Configuration.

  2. Select the dropdown arrow next to Pending approval.

  3. Select view in the attendee’s row to see their answers to the registration form.

    Screenshot: 5d31c2d4-988f-4462-8fb0-6e4568c1fb2b

Approve or deny requests

Note

  • Reviewing registration requests is an advanced registration feature, available in events with up to 3,000 attendees. For use of this feature in larger events, your org must have attendee capacity packs to enable instances up to 100,000.
  • If you had Teams Premium prior to April 1, 2026, you’ll continue to have access to this feature in events up to 100,000 attendees until the expiration of your license. To learn more about Teams licensing for events, please contact your IT admin.

To approve or deny registration requests:

  1. In Registration, make sure you’ve selected Require manual approval of all event registrations.

  2. Go to Registration > Attendee status.

  3. Select Pending approval.

    Screenshot: 2009c113-9f77-47f0-a522-75f2666bae0e

  4. Check the box next to each name you want to approve or deny. Select the box next to Name to select all.

  5. Select Approve or Reject to manage the request(s).

    Screenshot: 97dea86b-e0c9-433d-b1db-dc5f9085674c

Manage the registration waitlist

Note

  • Managing the registration waitlist is an advanced registration feature, available in events with up to 3,000 attendees. For use of this feature in larger events, your org must have attendee capacity packs to enable instances up to 100,000.
  • If you had Teams Premium prior to April 1, 2026, you’ll continue to have access to this feature in events up to 100,000 attendees until the expiration of your license. To learn more about Teams licensing for events, please contact your IT admin.

People who register for a webinar after the event has reached capacity will be added to the waitlist. When spots open up because the organizer increases capacity or other registrants cancel, waitlisted registrants will move to Pending approval if manual approval is enabled. Otherwise, their registration will go through automatically.

To enable the waitlist:
  1. Open the webinar in your Teams calendar.
  2. Go to Registration > Configuration.
  3. Select Enable waitlist for this event.
To access the waitlist:

  1. Open the webinar in your Teams calendar.

  2. Go to Registration > Attendee status.

    Note

    Organizers can’t remove or approve attendees from the waitlist; however, they can increase the event’s registration capacity to move waitlisted attendees to the registered or pending approval state.

Let registered attendees bypass the lobby

When people join your webinar, they’ll first enter a lobby until they’re let in by an organizer, co-organizer, or presenter. To manage the lobby more easily, let registered attendees bypass the lobby automatically by changing the lobby bypass settings.

To let registered attendees bypass the lobby:

  1. Go to your Teams calendar and select your webinar.

  2. Select View eventScreenshot: teams-expand-icon .

  3. Select Manage eventScreenshot: edit-pencil-icon-20x20-png .

  4. Select Meeting optionsScreenshot: Settings button.

  5. In Meeting accessScreenshot: teams-meeting-access-icon , turn the Attendees with a registration link can bypass the lobby toggle on.

    Note

    This will allow internal and external registered users and people designated in the Who can bypass the lobby? dropdown to bypass the lobby.

  6. Turn the Reject anyone who can’t bypass the lobby toggle on to reject anyone who isn’t registered for your event.

    Note

    This option is only available if the Attendees with the registration link can bypass the lobby toggle is turned on.

  7. Select SaveScreenshot: save-icon-001 .

This setting can be changed before and during the event. If you change it during the event, it’ll affect attendees who enter the lobby after the setting change. To learn more, see Using the lobby in Teams meetings.

Download registration reports

To download a registration report:

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: teams-calendar-tab-icon in Teams.
  2. Select the webinar you want to download a report for.
  3. Select Manage eventScreenshot: edit-pencil-icon-20x20-png .
  4. Select Reports.
  5. Select DownloadScreenshot: teams-desktop-download-icon > Registration report.

What’s next?

View webinar reports

Manage what attendees see in Microsoft Teams

Keep meetings and events running smoothly by managing what attendees see. Focus on certain people by showing them on and off screen, hiding others from view, and more.

Manage attendee view

Specify presenters and turn on Manage what attendees see to only show shared content and people you bring on-screen.

In a meeting

  1. Schedule a meeting in Teams.

  2. In the Invite attendeesScreenshot: Add people icon field, add people to your meeting.

  3. In the meeting description, press and hold Ctrl and select Meeting options.

    • If you’re in the new Teams calendar, select Meeting optionsScreenshot: Settings icon .

  4. In RolesScreenshot: People or Show Participants button :

    • Set Who can present to Specific people.
    • In Search for participants, search and select presenters.

  5. In Production toolsScreenshot: Production tools icon in Microsoft Teams , turn on the Manage what attendees see toggle.

  6. Select Save.

When you apply this setting, attendees won’t have camera and mic access.

Tip

These settings can be configured in the Teams mobile app.

In a webinar

  1. Schedule a webinar in Teams.

  2. In Co-organizers and Presenters from your org, add event co-organizers and presenters.

  3. Select Meeting optionsScreenshot: Settings button .

  4. In Engagement, turn on the Manage what attendees see toggle.

    By default, attendees won’t have access to their mics and cameras when you apply this setting. In Audio & video, their mic and camera permissions will be locked.

Tip

These settings can be configured in the Teams mobile app.

In a town hall

Town hall settings automatically default to managing what attendees see. To access these settings:

  1. Schedule a town hall in Teams.

  2. In Co-organizers and Presentersfrom your org, add event co-organizers and presenters.

  3. Select Meeting optionsScreenshot: Settings button .

  4. In Production toolsScreenshot: teams-production-tools-icon > Manage what attendees see, choose:

    1. Off to turn this setting off completely.
    2. On (default) to bring presenters on and off screen during the event. Attendees will see changes made in the Manage screen pane live.
    3. On with preview to queue up presenters to go on and off screen, before attendees see the changes live. Only people with control of production tools can manage what attendees see with preview. To learn more, see Manage attendee view with preview.

  5. Select Apply.

By default, attendees won’t have access to their mics and cameras. In Audio & video, their mic and camera permissions will be locked.

Tip

These settings can be configured in the Teams mobile app.

Manage attendee view with preview

In a Teams town hall, people who can control production tools will have the option to preview changes before applying them. This allows for smoother, more polished transitions in the attendee’s view, without showing every adjustment made while managing the screen.

Screenshot: Screenshot showing the preview queue for shared content in a town hall.

To manage what attendees see with preview:

  • Toggle presenter videos and shared content on and off under Manage screen to queue them up for the live feed.
  • Preview the queued presenters and content in the Preview feed before sending them live. Audio from unmuted presenters in Preview can be heard while they’re off screen.
  • When you’re ready to move the presenters and content from the Preview feed to the Live feed, select Send live.
  • The Live feed will show what the attendees are seeing in the event.

Note

People who control production tools won’t see what others are queueing in the Preview feed. Communicate about who’s arranging which scenes to keep the event running smoothly.

Bring a presenter on screen

Presenters, organizers, and co-organizers will appear in the left pane under Manage screen. When you bring someone on screen, their video feed will appear in the Manage screen pane and in the center of the meeting window simultaneously. This supports consistent viewing and helps event organizers see what’s being shown to attendees.

To bring someone on screen:

  1. In the Manage Screen pane, find the presenter you want to bring on-screen.

  2. Turn the Bring participant on screen toggle on that appears over their video feed or profile picture.

    Screenshot: Screenshot highlighting the toggle that brings people on and off the screen.

    Tip

    When the LIVE indicator appears on someone’s video feed or profile picture, they’re currently on the meeting screen and can be seen by attendees. The LIVE indicator is only visible in the Manage screen pane and can’t be seen by attendees.

You can also bring a presenter on screen by hovering over their video or profile picture and selecting More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > Bring on screenScreenshot: Spotlight video .

Note

  • Presenter view is currently only supported in Teams for desktop and web.
  • Firefox and Safari aren’t currently supported. Attendees joining from these browsers can only view the standard Teams meeting experience.

Take a presenter off screen

Easily take presenters off screen if they finish speaking or sharing content, or if they’re having technical difficulties.

To take a presenter off screen:

  1. In the Manage Screen pane, find the presenter you want to bring off screen.

  2. Turn the Bring participant on screen toggle off that appears over their video feed or profile picture.

    Screenshot: Screenshot showing the toggle that takes people off the meeting screen during a Teams event

You can also take a presenter off screen by hovering over their video or avatar and selecting More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > Take off screenScreenshot: Exit spotlight video .

When a presenter is brought off screen, the LIVE indicator on their video feed or profile picture will disappear.

Important

When you bring presenters off screen, their mics won’t be muted automatically. Attendees will still be able to hear them until they mute themselves manually.

Pin a presenter

Get ready to bring a specific presenter on-screen by pinning them in the Manage screen pane. In meetings or events that have many presenters, pinning someone makes them easy to find.

To pin a presenter:

  1. Find the presenter in the Manage Screen pane.

    Tip

    Select the arrows at the bottom of the Manage screen pane to see more people and find who you’re looking for.

    Screenshot: Screenshot showing arrows to see different pages of presenters

  2. Hover over the video or profile picture of the presenter you want to pin.

  3. Select More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > Pin for meScreenshot: Pin to taskbar icon .

Note

When you pin presenters, only you can see them pinned in the Manage Screen pane.

When you pin a presenter, they’ll appear under your personal video on the Manage Screen pane unless you unpin them.

To unpin a presenter:

  1. Find the presenter in the Manage Screen pane.
  2. Hover over the video or profile picture of the presenter you want to unpin.
  3. Select More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > Unpin for meScreenshot: Chat unpin icon .

Bring shared content on screen

When you start sharing your screen or other content while presenting, your shared content will first appear in the Manage Screen pane, where you can manually bring it on screen for everyone to see.

To bring shared content on screen:

  1. Select ShareScreenshot: skype-teams-icon-share in your meeting controls.

  2. Select the content you want to present.

  3. In Manage screen, a preview of the shared content will appear.

  4. Turn on the toggle in the shared content preview to bring it onto the live event feed. Turn the toggle off, or select Stop sharing in your meeting controls, to stop presenting content.

    Screenshot: Screenshot highlighting how to share visible content during a Microsoft Teams event.

Note

  • If someone shares their screen while another person is presenting live, the live presenter’s content will be taken off screen, and the newly shared content will replace the former presenter’s content in the Manage screen pane. Only participants with control of production tools can bring the shared window on screen afterwards
  • If you start a PowerPoint Live session, the PowerPoint will appear live to everyone immediately. To learn more, see Present from PowerPoint Live in Microsoft Teams.

Bring an attendee on screen

Typically, attendees will take on an audience role in this style of meeting or event and won’t have access to their mics or cameras. However, organizers can bring an attendee on-screen manually.

To bring an attendee on screen:

  1. Select PeopleScreenshot: People or Show Participants button from the meeting controls.
  2. Hover over the person you want to bring on screen.
  3. Select More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > Bring on screenScreenshot: Spotlight video .

Take an attendee off screen

When you take an attendee off screen, their mics and cameras will be turned off automatically.

To take an attendee off screen:

  1. Select PeopleScreenshot: People or Show Participants button from the meeting controls.
  2. Hover over the person you want to take off screen.
  3. Select More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > Take off screenScreenshot: Exit spotlight video .

Customize the event screen

Add visual appeal to your town hall during the event by customizing the event screen, available for people who have control over production tools.

Choose from several layouts to enhance the attendee experience, select a name tag color for attendees, and choose a background to make presentations stand out.

To customize your town hall screen, select Customize screenScreenshot: customize-screen-town-hall-icon in the event window. When you select a customization, the changes will be applied automatically.

Screenshot: Screenshot showing screen customizations in a Teams town hall.

Tip

For the best experience, use the Dynamic layout when bringing content on screen using RTMP-In.
