Manage your calendar in Microsoft Teams

Organize and plan your work schedule effectively by managing your Teams calendar. Stay on track by RSVPing to meetings and events and choosing a calendar view that suits you.

RSVP to a meeting

Let meeting organizers know whether or not you’ll be attending by RSVPing to their meetings ahead of time.

To RSVP to a meeting:

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: Teams Calendar tab icon in Teams.

  2. Select the meeting you want to RSVP to.

  3. Select RSVP.

  4. Select Accept or Decline, Follow, or Tentative.

    • If the meeting is part of a series, hover over your RSVP response and select This event to only RSVP to that occurrence or All events in the series to RSVP to all meetings in that series.
Add a note to your RSVP

When you RSVP, the organizer will be notified of your response via email.

To add a note to your RSVP response:

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: Teams Calendar tab icon in Teams.

  2. Select the meeting you want to RSVP to.

  3. Select View eventScreenshot: teams-expand-icon .

  4. Select RSVP with noteScreenshot: note-icon .

Change the calendar view

By default, your Teams calendar will display your work week.

View different dates

Meeting options in Microsoft Teams

Teams meeting options are settings that directly impact participant engagement, meeting efficiency, and security.

Default meeting options are determined by your IT admin, but they can be changed for a specific meeting.

Change meeting options

If you organize a meeting, you can access and change its settings depending on the meeting type:

Scheduled meetings

To get to meeting options:

  • In the Teams calendar, select an event and select View event > Options .
  • During a meeting, select Controls > View more options in your meeting controls.

Tip

Meeting options will open in a new window on your default browser. For the best experience, use Edge to open all meeting options.

About meeting options

Meeting access
  • Sensitivity
    • What it does: In Teams Premium , apply a sensitivity label to a meeting to protect and regulate access to sensitive content from your org. When you apply a sensitivity label, some other options will be set for you and locked.
    • When to use it: Apply sensitivity labels to apply more protection to meetings where confidential information and content will be shared.
  • Who can bypass the lobby?
    • What it does: Decide who gets into meetings directly and who should wait to be let in by using the lobby . If you use the lobby, you (and anyone else allowed to admit people) will see a list of people in the lobby. From there you can choose to admit or deny them.
    • When to use it: Use the lobby to add another layer of security to your meeting. Easily manage larger meetings by allowing people from trusted organizations and accounts to bypass the lobby.
  • People dialing in can bypass the lobby
    • What it does: Turn the People dialing in can bypass the lobby toggle on to allow anyone joining your meeting by phone to enter without waiting in the lobby. Depending on policies set by your IT admin, people dialing in might be placed in the lobby temporarily until someone from your org or a trusted org joins the meeting.
    • When to use it: Apply this setting in larger meetings to reduce the amount of people waiting and manage the lobby more easily.
  • Who can admit from the lobby
    • What it does: Choose who can let people into your event from the lobby. By default, organizers, co-organizers, and presenters can admit people from the lobby.
    • When to use it: Change this setting to prevent presenters from managing the lobby and increase meeting security.
  • Show meeting info on join screen
    • What it does: Show details about the meeting to people before they join, such as the meeting title, how many people have joined, and the status of the organizer.
    • When to use it: Change this setting to limit or provide meeting information for people before they join.
  • Reject anyone who can’t bypass the lobby
    • What it does: Automatically prevent people who don’t have lobby bypass permissions from joining the meeting.
    • When to use it: Turn on this setting to more efficiently manage admissions to high-volume events.
  • Announce when people dialing in join or leave.
    • What it does: Turn the Announce when people dialing in join or leave toggle on to receive alerts when people calling in by phone join or leave your meeting. Your admin might have enabled these alerts by default.
    • When to use it: Use this setting when you want to keep track of who is still in your meeting, and who has already left.
  • Require unverified participants to verify their info before joining
    • What it does: When you turn on the Require unverified participants to verify their info before joining toggle, unverified participants will receive an email with a one-time passcode they’ll need to enter to join the meeting.
    • When to use it: Use this when you want extra verification for participants attending the meeting. Your admin policy might also affect how people join. Available in Teams Premium .
  • Verify external presenters before joining an event
    • What it does: Select the level of verification you want to apply to presenters joining from outside your org.
    • When to use it: Customize this setting to add more security before external presenters join, or allow them to join directly without extra verification. If verification is required, anyone joining from a personal Teams account will be placed in the lobby first.
Advanced protection
  • Turn off copying and forwarding of meeting chat and transcripts
    • What it does: In Teams Premium , turn this toggle on to prevent attendees from copying and pasting content from meeting recaps, including messages, links, transcripts, and AI-generated insights. When this is turned on, right-click to copy, Ctrl + C , Forward message , Share to Outlook , and Copy link won’t be available for recap content in Teams. This setting doesn’t apply to scenarios outside of Teams (e.g., transcripts in Stream). This doesn’t prevent screen capture or third-party software from being used. To learn more, see Prevent screen captures in Microsoft Teams meetings .
    • When to use it: Turn this toggle on to protect sensitive information that was sent in a meeting chat, generated by AI, or transcribed.
  • End-to-end encryption
    • What it does: End-to-end encryption is available in Teams Premium to help protect sensitive meeting information. Turn the End-to-end encryption toggle on to encrypt meeting data at its origin and decrypt it at its destination.
    • When to use it: Use end-to-end encryption for an extra layer of security during highly confidential meetings.
  • Apply a watermark to shared content
    • What it does: When you turn on the Apply a watermark to shared content toggle, available in Teams Premium, each meeting participant will see a watermark with their name and email address cast across shared visual content.
    • When to use it: Apply a watermark to highly sensitive meetings to add an extra layer of security and deter attendees from sharing unauthorized screenshots.
  • Apply a watermark to everyone’s video feed
    • What it does: When you turn on the Apply a watermark to everyone’s video feed toggle, available in Teams Premium , everyone will see a watermark with their name and email address cast across all video feeds.
    • When to use it: Apply a watermark over people’s video feeds to protect information shared via camera ( physical whiteboards, documents, etc. )
  • Prevent screen captures
    • What it does: When you turn on the Prevent screen captures toggle, available in Teams Premium , the meeting window will turn black if anyone tries to take a screenshot. Anyone joining the meeting from unsupported platforms will be placed in audio-only mode to ensure content protection.
    • When to use it: Turn on screen capture prevention to protect confidential information shared during meetings.
  • Detect sensitive content during screen sharing
    • What it does: When you turn on the Detect sensitive content during screen sharing toggle, Teams will detect and notify someone if they’re sharing their screen and sensitive information (bank information, credit card numbers, etc.) is visible.
    • When to use it: Turn this setting on to help prevent attendees from accidentally sharing sensitive information while presenting.
Roles
  • Choose co-organizers
    • What it does: After you invite people to your meeting, add co-organizers to give them most organizer capabilities.
    • When to use it: Add co-organizers for more help managing the meeting, lobby, and breakout rooms.
  • Who can present
    • What it does: See Roles in a Teams meeting for details about selecting presenters and changing someone’s role before and during a meeting. Note: Meeting rooms are part of your org, so they’ll join meetings the same way any other participant in your org does.
    • When to use it: Designate presenters before and during your meeting to keep your meeting focused and on-track.
  • Enable language interpretation
    • What it does: Turn on the Enable language interpretation toggle to add a professional interpreter to your meeting who can instantly translate the speaker’s language into another in real-time.
    • When to use it: Break down the language barrier in multi-lingual meetings with language interpretation .
Production tools
  • Manage what attendees see
    • What it does: Specify presenters and turn on the Manage what attendees see toggle to show only shared content and people you bring on screen. This option will limit attendee mic and camera use.
    • When to use it: Use this setting to keep your meeting on-track, professional, and free of distractions.
  • RTMP - In
    • What it does: Turn on the RTMP – In toggle to produce a meeting directly from an external hardware- or software-based encoder. To learn more, see Use RTMP-In in Microsoft Teams .
    • When to use it: Use RTMP - In when you want to stream high-quality live or pre-recorded media during a Teams meeting or event.
  • Enable Green room
    • What it does: The Green room allows organizers and presenters to join an event while attendees wait in the lobby.
    • When to use it: Use the Green room to prepare for an event before attendees are present. Test your audio and video, shared content, and more.
Participation
  • Allow mic for attendees
    • What it does: Turn the Allow mic for attendees toggle on or off to change attendee mic permissions.
    • When to use it: Use this setting to manage attendee discussion during a meeting.
  • Allow camera for attendees
    • What it does: Turn the Allow camera for attendees toggle on or off to change attendee camera permissions.
    • When to use it: Turn this setting off to keep focus on shared content and presenters during a meeting and encourage attendee participation.
  • Meeting chat
    • What it does: Change this setting to let attendees chat anytime, during a meeting only, or not at all. By default, anyone invited to a meeting can participate in the meeting chat before, during, and after the meeting.
    • When to use it: Change this setting to limit or open attendee discussion during a meeting or event.
  • Q&A
    • What it does: Enable Q&A to allow attendees to ask questions, post replies, and post anonymously during a meeting. Q&A can be unmoderated or moderated by meeting co-organizers.
    • When to use it: Use Q&A to make large events more interactive and engaging for attendees. Receive and respond to people’s questions in real-time.
  • Allow reactions
    • What it does: By default, attendees can send live reactions during a meeting to express how they feel about what’s being shared.
    • When to use it: Turn off the Allow reactions toggle in larger meetings to limit distractions or keep the meeting recording free from reaction pop-ups.
  • Hide attendee names
    • What it does: Turn on the Hide attendee names toggle to keep attendees anonymous to each other. Only organizers, presenters, and apps will have access to attendee names. To use this setting, first make people presenters before the meeting. Then, turn on the Hide attendee names toggle before the meeting starts.
    • When to use it: Use this setting to ensure attendee privacy during a meeting or event.
  • Allow attendance report
    • What it does: Attendance reports contain meeting attendance details, including how long attendees stayed, and how long your meeting lasted, and more. Turn on the Allow attendance report toggle to generate, view, and download attendance reports.
    • When to use it: Use attendance reports to gain more insights about your meeting and participant behaviors.
Recording & transcription
  • Record and transcribe automatically
    • What it does: Turn on the Record and transcribe automatically toggle to record and transcribe your meeting as soon as it starts.
    • When to use it: Apply this setting to make sure all your meeting is recorded and transcribed from the moment it starts until it ends or you stop recording and transcribing.
  • Who can record and transcribe
    • What it does: In Teams Premium , choose whether to allow presenters to record and transcribe a meeting in addition to organizers and co-organizers.
    • When to use it: Use this setting to manage who can start and own the recording. Whoever starts a meeting recording owns the recording and can delete it later.
  • Enable multilingual speech recognition
    • What it does: Turn on the Enable multilingual speech recognition toggle to allow everyone to be understood in their spoken languages. For transcription and caption accuracy, make sure each person sets their correct spoken language.
    • When to use it: Use this setting during meetings and events where people are speaking multiple languages to ensure everyone understands each other.
Copilot and other AI
  • Allow Copilot and Facilitator
    • What it does: Choose when to allow Copilot during a meeting or event by selecting an option from the Allow Copilot dropdown menu. If you choose Only during the meeting , Copilot can work without turning on transcription. If you turn on transcription, Copilot can always be used after the meeting.
    • When to use it: Modify this setting to limit or expand when Copilot is used for a meeting.
  • Facilitator
    • What it does: Facilitator is an agent that takes notes, joins the meeting chat, and more using the meeting’s spoken language. Facilitator is available when Copilot is enabled.
    • When to use it: Enable Facilitator in meetings for easy review of important discussion points, follow-up tasks, and more.
Accessibility
  • Provide CART Captions
    • What it does: Turn on the Provide CART Captions toggle to use Communication access real-time translation (CART) captions during a meeting. CART captions are generated by a trained CART captioner who listens and translates speech into text instantly.
    • When to use it: Use CART captions to provide accurately translated captions and make your meeting more accessible and inclusive.

Default meeting options

Default meeting options are set by your IT admin and may affect meeting security or which features you can use.

Network outages

In case of a Teams network outage, your meeting options might revert back to the defaults set by your IT admin. If this happens, check your meeting options before your meeting starts to make sure they’re set the way you want them.

Your settings will return to normal once the outage is resolved. For more help, contact your IT admin.

Moderate a Q&A in a live event in Microsoft Teams

Important

The Teams live event experience is retiring on June 30, 2026. Please switch to Teams town halls for the newest event features and experience. For more information, please read this blog post.

When a live event is created with the Q&A option, attendees can interact with producers and presenters in a moderated Q&A.

Watch this video for an overview of moderating a Q&A in a Teams live event.

Before the event

Attendees can start asking questions in the Q&A as soon as they join the event, even if the event hasn’t started yet. These questions are only visible to moderators until a moderator publishes them to the event.

During the event

By default, the Q&A will be open for questions when the event begins. Moderators can then control when attendees can ask questions by using the Q&A toggle.

Open or close the Q&A

  1. Open the Q&A pane by selecting Show Q&AScreenshot: The Q&A icon in the meeting controls.

    Screenshot: The icon is the third from the left

    The toggle in the pane will show that the Q&A is open for questions.

    Screenshot: Toggle says Open

  2. To prevent attendees from entering questions, select the toggle. The toggle will then say Closed.

Respond to questions

All questions initially appear on the New tab.

Respond publicly

  1. Select Publish above a question to immediately make it visible to everyone.

    Screenshot: The New tab is the first tab

    Then the question moves to the Published tab.

  2. On the Published tab, enter your reply in the compose box and select SendScreenshot: Send icon . Everyone can now see your answer.

    Screenshot: The Published tab is the second tab

Note

It’s also possible to send a response and then make the question and answer public.

To “like” the question, select the thumbs-up icon Screenshot: Like button .

Respond privately
  • On the New tab, enter your answer in the Private reply box and select SendScreenshot: Send icon . The answer is instantly available to the person who asked the question.
Make an announcement

To send a message to everyone, enter it in the Make an announcement box at the bottom of the pane and select SendScreenshot: Send icon .

Reject a question
  • To remove a question from the Q&A, select Dismiss.

The question moves to the Dismissed tab.

You can also delete a published question by selecting the Delete icon Screenshot: Delete button .

After the event

When the event is over, you can download reports, including a Q&A report.

  1. Go to your Teams calendar and double-click the event invite.

The report is downloaded as a .CSV file to your computer’s Downloads folder.

Monitor call and meeting quality in Microsoft Teams

Identify and troubleshoot issues during a Teams meeting or call in with call health metrics. View real-time data about your network, audio, screen sharing, and outgoing video quality. Call health metrics update every 15 seconds.

To view call health metrics:

  1. Select More actionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon in your meeting controls.
  2. Select SettingsScreenshot: Settings icon > Call healthScreenshot: Call health icon in Microsoft Teams .

How to read your call health stats

Network
  • Roundtrip time
    • In group calls, it’s the response time between your system and the Teams Service. In one-on-one calls, it’s the response time between your system and the other participant’s. Lower is better.
    • Typical value: < 200 ms
  • Received packet loss
    • The result of a poor network connection. Lower is better.
    • Typical value: < 2%
  • Teams send limit*
    • The max limit of data Teams can send based on the current network conditions and how it’s used. This isn’t your ISP speed limit.
    • Typical value: Audio: 70 kbps Video: 1.5 Mbps
  • Teams receive limit*
    • The max limit of data Teams can receive based on the current network conditions and how it’s used. This isn’t your ISP speed limit. For more information, see the admin instructions Bandwidth requirements .
    • Typical value: Audio: 70 kbps Video: 1.5 Mbps
Audio
  • Sent bitrate
    • The amount of audio data sent. High is better.
    • Typical value: > 24 kbps minimum; 36-128 kbps is typical
  • Sent packets
    • Data gets sent over the network in packets. This value is the number of data packets sent during a call.
    • Typical value: Informational only
  • Roundtrip time
    • Response time between your system and the Teams server. Lower is better.
    • Typical value: < 200 ms
  • Sent codec
    • The codec used for encoding audio sent by your system.
    • Typical value: Informational only
  • Received jitter
    • The distortion in audio caused by inconsistent audio packet arrival times, Lower is better.
    • Typical value: < 30 ms
  • Received packets
    • The number of audio data packets received
    • Typical value: Informational only
  • Received packet loss
    • The result of a poor network connection, this is the percentage of audio data packets not received by your system. Lower is better.
    • Typical value: < 2%
  • Received codec
    • The codec used for encoding audio data received by your system.
    • Typical value: Informational only
Video
  • Sent frame rate
    • The number of video frames sent per second. Higher is better
    • Typical value: Between 1-30 fps (Variable based on what content is being shared.)
  • Sent width/height
    • Video resolution sent. Higher is better.
    • Typical value: Between 160x90 to 1920x1080 pixels (Variable based on what content is being shared and your device’s capabilities.)
  • Sent bitrate
    • The amount of data your device sends. The higher the number, the better the quality.
    • Typical value: Informational only
  • Roundtrip time
    • Response time between your system and Teams server. Lower is better
    • Typical value: < 200 ms
  • Sent packets
    • The number of packets of data sent over the network.
    • Typical value: Informational only
  • Sent codec
    • The codec used to encode your video data.
    • Typical value: Informational only
  • Video processing
    • Resource used to encode video.
    • Typical value: Hardware processing preferred
Screen sharing
  • Sent frame rate
    • The number of video frames sent per second. Higher is better.
    • Typical value: Between 1-30 fps (Variable based on what content is being shared.)
  • Sent width/height
    • Video resolution sent. Higher is better.
    • Typical value: Between 160x90 to 1920x1080 pixels (Variable based on what content is being shared and your device’s capabilities.)
  • Sent codec
    • The codec used to encode screen sharing data.
    • Typical value: Informational only
  • Screen share and processing
    • Indicates whether CPU (Central Processing Unit) or GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) is used for encoding video data.
    • Typical value: Hardware or hardware plus software processing preferred
  • Received frame rate
    • The number of video frames received per second by your system. Higher is better.
    • Typical value: 1-30 fps
  • Received width/height
    • Resolution of the video your system receives. Higher is better.
    • Typical value: Between 160x90 to 1920x1080 pixels (Variable based on what content is being shared and device capabilities.)
  • Received codec
    • The codec used for processing and encoding incoming screen sharing data.
    • Typical value: Informational only
  • Screen share received processing
    • Indicates whether CPU (Central Processing Unit) or GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) is used for encoding video data.
    • Typical value: Hardware processing preferred

*Exceptionally low values in some scenarios indicate Teams is limiting its peak bandwidth usage to maintain transmission while competing with network traffic or hitting network and service issues between endpoints. In these cases where Teams restricts quality, network conditions should be evaluated to see if something can be improved.

Teams might also limit its peak bandwidth usage if the complexity of screen sharing, video, or audio content is low or if a participant in the call or meeting chose lower-quality settings. Teams will adapt to the current use as well, not just because of network conditions.

Note

Low frame rates don’t necessarily imply a poor call experience. If you are experiencing poor video quality and low frame rates, it could be due to the performance of the computer system or insufficient hardware resources.

Multilingual speech recognition in Microsoft Teams

Communicate clearly and effectively in multilingual Microsoft Teams meetings. In multilingual meetings, individual participants can speak, listen and read in their preferred languages through:

  • The Interpreter agent
  • Multilingual speech recognition
  • Live translated captions and transcripts
  • Translated recap after multilingual meetings

Supported languages

English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Chinese, Japanese, and Korean.

Interpreter agent

Note

Interpreter agent is available as part of the Microsoft 365 Copilot license. A Microsoft 365 license is required to listen to others’ speech through the Interpreter agent. To get access to Microsoft 365 Copilot, contact your IT admin. 

The interpreter agent helps participants speak and listen in their preferred languages through real-time speech-to-speech interpretation.

To learn more about the Interpreter agent, see Interpreter in Microsoft Teams meetings.

Multilingual speech recognition

Note

  • Multilingual speech recognition is available as part of the Microsoft 365 Copilot license, an add-on license that provides additional features to make Teams meetings more personalized, intelligent, and secure. To get access to Microsoft 365 Copilot, contact your IT admin.
  • Multilingual speech recognition is also available as part of Teams Premium.
  • Multilingual speech recognition isn’t currently supported in Teams town halls.

Multilingual speech recognition provides live translated captions and transcripts in real time without the Interpreter agent turned on, ensuring everyone can participate fully regardless of the language they speak.

When you organize or attend meetings with multilingual speech recognition turned on, each participant can select their own preferred spoken language and see accurate live captions and transcripts in that language.

To turn on multilingual speech recognition:

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: Teams Calendar tab icon in Teams.

  2. Select an event.

  3. Select View eventScreenshot: teams-expand-icon .

    • To make changes to a meeting series, select Edit series.

  4. Select OptionsScreenshot: Settings icon .

  5. In Recording and transcriptionScreenshot: teams-record-and-transcribe-button-icon , turn on the Enable multilingual speech recognition toggle.

  6. Select Apply.

Live translated captions and transcripts

Note

  • Live translated captions in meetings are available as part of Teams Premium and Microsoft 365 Copilot, an add-on license that provides additional features to make Teams meetings more personalized, intelligent, and secure. To get access to an eligible license, contact your IT admin.
  • If the meeting organizer has a Teams Premium or Microsoft 365 Copilot license, all meeting participants can use translated captions and transcription without a specific license required.
  • If individual participants have a Teams Premium or Microsoft 365 Copilot license, only those licensed participants will see the Translate to option and can use translated captions and transcription.

Live captions and live transcriptions will be translated automatically in meetings with multilingual speech recognition or the Interpreter agent enabled. With live translated captions and transcripts, participants can see multilingual conversations translated into the languages they can understand. Translation language can be set up in the language settings.

Translated captions and transcripts are only available during the meeting and won’t be accessible after the meeting ends. Post-meeting translated transcripts can be generated via Clipchamp.

Note

If your IT admin enabled transcript translations for your org, transcription owners can generate translations in 100+ languages. Translations will then be accessible on the Recap page. To learn more about the requirements for this feature, see Pay-as-you-go transcript translations for videos in Microsoft 365.

To learn more about live translated captions and transcription, see View live transcription in Microsoft Teams meetings or Use live captions in Microsoft Teams meetings.

Set your languages during meetings

To set your spoken and translation languages during meetings:

  • Select More actionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon in your meeting controls. Then, select Language and speechScreenshot: Language and speech menu item icon > Show live captionsScreenshot: teams-live-captions-icon > Open caption settingsScreenshot: skype-teams-mobile-icon-settings > Language settingsScreenshot: teams-language-settings-icon .
  • Select More actionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon in your meeting controls. Then, select Record and transcribeScreenshot: teams-record-and-transcribe-button-icon > Start transcriptionScreenshot: teams-start-transcription-icon > Confirm > Language settingsScreenshot: teams-language-settings-icon .

In Language settings > Your spoken language, choose your preferred spoken language.

In Language settings > Translate to, select the language you want your live captions, transcripts, and recap translated into.

If you’re viewing live captions in a language that isn’t supported by Interpreter agent, and Interpreter agent is turned on in your meeting, the caption language will automatically switch to English. You can then choose one of the languages supported by Interpreter agent or multilingual meetings.

If you’ve previously used Interpreter or participated in multilingual meetings, your language settings for those features will persist in future meetings.

Note

  • If the meeting organizer has a Teams Premium or Microsoft 365 Copilot license, all meeting participants can use translated captions and transcription without a specific license required.
  • If individual participants have a Teams Premium or Microsoft 365 Copilot license, only those licensed participants will see the Translate to option and can use translated captions and transcription.
  • The Translate to option is available independent of multilingual speech recognition as long as licensing conditions are met.

Translated recap

If you used translated captions or translated transcription during a multilingual meeting, your meeting recap may appear in the preferred language you set for captions and transcription.

There are two ways translated recaps are generated:

  • If multilingual speech recognition was turned on during the meeting, your recap will appear in the language you selected under Translate to for captions and transcription.
  • If the Interpreter agent was turned on during the meeting, multilingual speech recognition was automatically turned on. Your recap will appear in the language you selected under Translate to for captions and transcription. To learn more, see Interpreter in Microsoft Teams meetings.

To learn more about recap, see Recap in Microsoft Teams.

Mute and unmute your mic in Microsoft Teams

When you join a Teams meeting, you can choose to mute your mic to prevent any unwanted noise or unmute your mic to participate in the meeting.

There are a few different ways you can mute or unmute your mic in Teams.

Mute or unmute before a meeting

Before joining a meeting, you can turn your mic on or off by selecting the MicrophoneScreenshot: Mute button toggle.

Screenshot: manage audio before a meeting

Teams will remember the mic preference you set here when you join future meetings.

Mute or unmute during a meeting

To mute your mic during a meeting, select MicScreenshot: Mute button in your meeting controls. To turn your mic back on, select MicScreenshot: teams unmute icon .

Screenshot: manage audio during a meeting

You can also turn your mic on and off by pressing the shortcut keys Ctrl + Shift + M. To learn more, see Keyboard shortcuts for Microsoft Teams.

Note

Some mic capabilities might be unavailable depending on meeting settings or policies set by your IT admin.

To automatically mute your mic if your screen locks:

  1. In Teams, select More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > SettingsScreenshot: Settings button .
  2. Select PrivacyScreenshot: Privacy settings button .
  3. Turn on the Turn off my camera and mic when my screen locks toggle.
  4. Restart Teams to activate this setting.
Mute or unmute from your taskbar (Windows)

If you join a Teams meeting on a Windows device, you can mute or unmute your mic from your Windows taskbar.

To mute and unmute your mic from your Windows taskbar:

  • Select the mic icon Screenshot: Microphone on Teams meeting toolbar icon in your taskbar.
  • Press the WindowsScreenshot: The Windows key icon. + alt + K keys.

Use Ctrl + Spacebar to unmute

On the Teams desktop app, you can also choose to stay muted to avoid unwanted interruption or noise during a meeting and rapidly respond when called upon. To quickly unmute, hold down the keys Ctrl + Spacebar (Windows) and Option + Spacebar (Mac). Release keys to go back to muted state again.

How to enable:

  1. In Teams, select More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > SettingsScreenshot: Settings button .

  2. Select PrivacyScreenshot: Privacy settings button .

  3. Turn on the Keyboard shortcut to unmute toggle.

  4. Join a call or a meeting. Mute yourself.

    1. On Windows, press and hold Ctrl + Spacebar. On Mac, press and hold Option + Spacebar. You’ll see an alert regarding temporary unmute. Check to make sure you’re unmuted.
    2. When you release the key combination, your mic will be muted again.

Note

Shortcuts in general—including Ctrl + Spacebar and Option + Spacebar to unmute—don’t work within the chat box or when apps like PowerPoint Live or Whiteboard are shared in the meeting stage.

Want to learn more? See Meetings in Teams.

Avoid unwanted distractions during meetings by muting notifications. You’ll still get alerts about activity related to the meeting you’re in, like when someone sends a message to the meeting chat. But all other activity is muted while you’re in the meeting.

To turn off notifications during meetings:

To turn them back on, select Settings and moreScreenshot: Settings and more > Settings > Notifications and activityScreenshot: Activity button and select Show notifications during calls and meetings.

My calls or meetings keep dropping in Microsoft Teams

If you’re experiencing multiple dropped calls or you’re getting disconnected from a Teams meeting, it’s likely due to network issues. You might encounter error messages like:

  • “Oh dear! Your call has dropped. Please try again.”
  • “Please hold on while we try to reconnect you,” or “I was placed on hold during the meeting.”
  • “Hold on. It looks like something went wrong. We’re trying to get you back in the meeting.”
  • “Try joining again, or dial in. To join the meeting, you might need to call in on your phone due to a network issue.”

In the above cases, first check your internet connection. Make sure both the caller and callee have a stable connection with adequate throughput.

For further troubleshooting, follow the steps in this article: Troubleshoot User Call Quality Problems.

Additionally, you can check for ongoing service incidents here: Microsoft 365 Service Status.

It’s important to note that call drops can also occur if you’re using non-certified devices which aren’t supported. For example, a call can drop when clicking on a call notification, or when resuming a call from hold. For the best experience please ensure your headsets and/or other audio devices are officially certified: Teams Certified Devices.

Finally, consider restarting the Teams application to resolve temporary issues and make sure you’re using the latest Teams version.

My camera isn’t working in Microsoft Teams

If you’re having trouble with the camera in Microsoft Teams, we have some suggestions to help you get back on track.

Tip

Windows 10 users can also go here for more information about troubleshooting common camera issues.

Check if your camera is in use

To make sure you can use your camera in Teams:

  • Close all other apps that might be using your camera (like Skype or FaceTime).
  • If you’re using an external camera, try unplugging it and plugging it back in.
  • Try restarting your device.
  • Contact support from your device’s manufacturer in case it’s a hardware issue.

Check for updates

Make sure you have the latest Windows update or Mac OS update and Teams app version installed.

Check for updates in Teams to make sure you’re running the latest version.

Note

To troubleshoot Teams in Virtual Desktop Infrastructures (VDI), contact your IT admin or go here for more information.

Make a test call

To double-check whether your camera is working, make a test call in Teams.

To make a test call:

  1. Select Settings and moreScreenshot: Teams settings and more icon. at the top-right of Teams.
  2. Select SettingsScreenshot: Settings button > DevicesScreenshot: Teams settings device icon .
  3. Under Audio Settings, select Make a test callScreenshot: Test call button icon .

In a test call, you’ll see how your mic, speaker, and camera are working. Follow the instructions from Test Call Bot and record a short message. The message will play back for you. After that, you’ll get a summary of the test call, and you can go to your device settings to make changes.

Note

  • The test call feature is only available in English for now. Additional languages coming soon.
  • We’ll delete your test recording immediately after the call. It won’t be retained or used by Microsoft.
  • The test call feature is currently unavailable for Teams on the web.

Troubleshooting for Windows

If you are still having trouble with your camera, here are some more solutions to try.

For more help, see Camera doesn’t work in Windows.

Check your Teams mobile app permissions

You might need to change permissions on your mobile device.

To change permissions on your Windows device:

  1. Open the Settings app on your device.

  2. Select Privacy & security > Camera.

    Screenshot: Windows settings with camera UI highlighted.

  3. Turn the Let apps access your camera toggle on.

    Screenshot: Camera sharing toggle turned on in Windows device settings.

  4. Under Let apps access your camera, turn the Microsoft Teams (work or school) toggle on

    • If the toggle is already turned on, turn it off and back on again.

  5. Close all apps and restart your device.

Check your drivers

When your camera isn’t working in Windows 10 (or if you’re using an external webcam), it might be a problem with your drivers. Go here for step-by-step instructions for checking your Windows drivers.

Troubleshooting for Mac OS

If you are still having trouble with your camera, here is another solution to try.

Check your app permissions

You might need to change your device permissions.

To change permissions on your Mac OS device:

  1. Open System Settings on your device.
  2. Select Security & Privacy.
  3. Under Privacy, select Camera.
  4. Make sure the Microsoft Teams (work or school) is selected.
  5. Close all apps and restart your device.

Note

These settings apply to Mac OS 10.14 and higher.

Troubleshooting for Teams on the web

If you’re using Teams on the web, here is something you can do to make sure your camera is set up properly.

  • Check your browser settings: You may need to “allow” your camera and/or microphone to work in Teams.
  • Contact your IT admin: Some settings may be managed by your IT admin; contact them for more details.

Note

Microsoft Teams on the web is currently supported in Chrome, Safari, Edge, Firefox, and Internet Explorer 11.

Microsoft Edge

  1. Select Settings and moreScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > SettingsScreenshot: Settings button .

  2. Select Cookies and site permissions.

  3. Select Camera.

    1. Turn on the Ask before accessing (recommended) toggle.

      Note

      If this is turned off, access to your camera will be blocked on Edge.

Google Chrome

  1. Open Settings.

  2. Select Privacy and security > Site settings > Permissions.

  3. Select Camera.

    1. At the top of this screen, make sure your correct device is selected from the dropdown menu.
    2. Under Default behavior, select Sites can ask to use your camera.
Safari
  1. In Safari, open Preferences.
  2. Select Websites.
  3. In General, select Camera.
  4. Next to When visiting other websites:, select Ask or Allow.

Contact Microsoft support

Still need help? Contact Microsoft support.

My microphone isn’t working in Microsoft Teams

If people are having trouble hearing you in Teams meetings, here are some tips to help you get back on track.

To learn more about changing mic settings in Microsoft Teams for personal use, see Manage your device settings in Microsoft Teams Free.

Check for updates

For the best performance, make sure you have the latest version of Teams and the most recent Windows update or Mac OS update installed.

Make sure you’re not muted

In your meeting controls, make sure MicScreenshot: Microphone on Teams meeting toolbar icon is in an unmuted state.

If the mic icon has a line through it, you’re currently on mute. Select Unmute micScreenshot: Muted microphone button to unmute.

Check your physical mic

Some mics have physical mute options on the devices themselves.

Check that your headphone boom is not in the mute position (usually upright or away from your mouth), or that your external mic’s physical mute button is not turned on.

Check settings on your device or browser

To use your mic in Teams, you might need to change privacy settings on your device or on the web to give let Teams access to it.

Change device settings

If you’re using the Teams desktop app, double-check your device settings to make sure Teams has access to your mic.

Windows

  1. Open your device settings and select Privacy & security.

  2. Under App permissions, select Microphone.

  3. Turn on the Microphone access toggle.

  4. Turn on the Let apps access your microphone toggle.

  5. Turn on the Microsoft Teams (work or school) toggle.

  6. Turn on the Let desktop apps access your microphone toggle.

    Note

    If these toggles were already turned on, try turning them off and on again to make sure the settings apply.

  7. Close all apps and restart your device.

When your mic isn’t working in Windows 10, it might be a problem with your drivers. Go here for step-by-step instructions to check your Windows drivers.

macOS
  1. Open System Preferences on your device.
  2. Select Security & Privacy.
  3. Select Microphone.
  4. Under Privacy, make sure Microsoft Teams is selected.
  5. Close all apps and restart your device.
iOS
  1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap Privacy > Microphone.
  3. Make sure the Microsoft Teams toggle is turned on.
  4. Close all apps and restart your device.
Change browser settings

If you’re using Teams for web, make sure your default browser settings allow Teams access to use your mic.

Note

Microsoft Teams on the web is currently supported in Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Internet Explorer 11.

Microsoft Edge

  1. In Edge, select Settings and moreScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > SettingsScreenshot: Settings button .

  2. Select Cookies and site permissions.

  3. Select Microphone.

    1. Turn on the Ask before accessing (recommended) toggle.

      Note

      If this is turned off, access to your camera will be blocked on Edge.

Google Chrome

  1. In Google Chrome, select Settings.

  2. Select Privacy and security > Site settings > Permissions.

  3. Select Microphone.

    1. At the top of this screen, make sure your correct device is selected from the dropdown menu.
    2. Under Default behavior, select Sites can ask to use your microphone.
Safari
  1. In Safari, open Preferences.
  2. Select Websites.
  3. In General, select Microphone.
  4. Next to When visiting other websites: select Ask or Allow.
  5. Close all apps and restart your device.

Reconnect your mic

Try reconnecting your mic through your Teams settings.

Before a meeting

  1. In Teams, select Settings and moreScreenshot: Select to see more options > SettingsScreenshot: Settings button .

  2. Select DevicesScreenshot: Teams settings device icon .

  3. Under Audio settings, make sure your mic is selected from the Microphone dropdown menu.

  4. Select Make a test callScreenshot: Test call button icon to test your settings. Follow the instructions from Test Call Bot and record a short message. The message will play back for you. After that, you’ll get a summary of the test call, and you can make changes in your device settings.

    Note

    • The test call feature is currently available in English only.
    • Your test recording will be deleted immediately after the call. It won’t be retained or used by Microsoft.
    • The test call feature is currently unavailable on Teams for web.
During a meeting
  1. In your Teams meeting window, select the dropdown arrow next to MicScreenshot: mic-icon .
  2. Select More audio settings.
  3. Make sure your correct microphone is selected

If your mic isn’t in the Microphone dropdown menu, unplug and plug it back in. If you’re having trouble using a Bluetooth mic, make sure it’s charged and not connected to another device. Then try reconnecting.

Check sound settings (Windows)

Go to your Windows settings to make sure your microphone is enabled and unmuted.

  1. From Windows Start, open your device Settings.

  2. Select System > Sound.

  3. Under Input:

    1. Select your mic in Choose a device for speaking or recording. If you don’t see your mic here, select Add device to pair it;

    2. Next to Volume, make sure your mic is unmuted.

      Screenshot: UI 3

If you’re still having trouble, try re-enabling your speaker by going to Advanced > More sound settings. In the Recording tab, right-click your mic. Then select Enable.

Check remote desktop settings (Windows)

If you’re using Remote Desktop, double-check the audio settings on your local Windows device.

  1. From Windows Start, search and select Remote Desktop Connection.

  2. Open the Local Resources tab.

  3. Under Remote audio, select Settings….

    1. Under Remote audio playback, select Play on this computer.
    2. Under Remote audio recording, select Record from this computer.

  4. Select OK to save changes.

Use your phone’s audio

If your mic doesn’t work after trying the solutions above and you see one of the messages below, select Call me back to use your phone’s mic.

Enter your phone number and select Call me to receive a call from Teams that will connect you to your meeting. Your audio will come from your phone, but other content sharing will still take place on your desktop.

My speaker isn’t working in Microsoft Teams

If you’re having trouble hearing others in your Teams calls and meetings, the problem is either with your speaker not working, or with their microphone. If you’re the only one who can’t hear them, there might be an issue with your speaker.

Here are some solutions to help you get back on track.

Important

For the best performance, make sure you have the latest version of Teams and the most recent Windows update or Mac OS update installed.

Check your speaker settings in Teams

Before a meeting

If your speaker is muted before the call starts, Teams will show you the notification below. Select Unmute to hear others in your meeting.

You can also make sure your speaker is working before your meeting or call starts by checking your device settings.

To check your speaker device settings:

  1. Select Settings and moreScreenshot: Select to see more options > SettingsScreenshot: Settings button in Teams.

  2. Select DevicesScreenshot: Teams settings device icon .

  3. In Audio > Audio settingsScreenshot: teams-audio-settings-with-gear , make sure your speaker is selected from the Speaker dropdown menu.

    Note

    If your audio device doesn’t appear, make sure it’s charged (Bluetooth), or unplug and plug it back in (wired). Then, try reconnecting it.

  4. To test your audio settings, select Make a test callScreenshot: Test call button icon . Follow the instructions from Test Call Bot and record a short message. The message will play back for you. After that, you’ll get a summary of the test call, and you can make changes in your device settings.

    Note

    • The test call feature is currently available in English only. Additional languages are coming soon.
    • Your test recording will be deleted immediately after the call. It won’t be retained or used by Microsoft.
    • The test call feature is currently unavailable on Teams for web.
During a meeting

If you can’t hear others during a call or meeting, check whether your speaker is muted or disconnected in your device settings.

  1. In your Teams meeting window, select the dropdown arrow next to Mic.
  2. Select More actionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > Audio settingsScreenshot: Teams audio settings .
  3. Under Speaker, make sure your device is selected and unmuted

If you don’t see your device in the Mic dropdown menu, unplug and plug it back in. If you’re having trouble using a Bluetooth speaker, make sure it’s charged and not connected to another device. Then try reconnecting.

Check sound settings (Windows)

Go to your Windows settings to make sure your speaker is enabled and unmuted.

  1. From Windows Start, search and select Sound settings.

  2. Select System > SoundScreenshot: teams speaker icon .

  3. In Choose where to play sound, select your speaker. If you don’t see your speaker here, select Add device to pair it.

  4. Next to Volume, make sure your speaker is unmuted.

If you’re still having trouble, try re-enabling your speaker by going to Advanced > More sound settings. In the Recording tab, right-click your mic. Then select Enable.

Check remote desktop settings (Windows)

If you’re using Remote Desktop, double-check the audio settings on your local Windows device.

  1. From Windows Start, search and select Remote Desktop Connection.

  2. Open the Local Resources tab.

  3. Under Remote audio, select Settings….

    1. Under Remote audio playback, select Play on this computer.
    2. Under Remote audio recording, select Record from this computer.

  4. Select OK to save changes.

Overview of Microsoft Teams Premium

What is Microsoft Teams Premium?

Microsoft Teams Premium is an offering that builds on the current Teams experience with additional features that help make Teams meetings even more personalized, intelligent, and protected. It also enables premium capabilities for additional meeting scenarios, including Virtual Appointments and webinars.

Screenshot: An image of Intelligent Meeting Recap

With Teams Premium, you can:

  • Focus on what matters with AI-powered meetings and intelligent meeting recaps that automatically generate meeting notes, recommended tasks, and personalized highlights to help you get the information most important to you, even if you miss the meeting. Learn more about intelligent productivity with Teams Premium.
  • Customize meetings with personalized touches for best-in-class experiences during client calls or company presentations with branded meetings, organizational backgrounds, and more. Learn more about engaging meeting experiences in Teams Premium.
  • Keep meetings confidential with advanced meeting protections like watermarks, sensitivity labels, end-to-end encryption, and limiting who can record. Learn more about adding protection to sensitive meetings.
  • Delight customers with advanced personalized features in virtual appointments, streamlining appointment management and tracking performance with reports and analytics. Learn more about hosting high-quality virtual appointments.

Participate in a Q&A in a live event in Microsoft Teams

Important

The Teams live event experience is retiring on June 30, 2026. Please switch to Teams town halls for the newest event features and experience. For more information, please read this blog post.

In a Teams live event, attendees can interact with producers and presenters through a Q&A, if the organizer set it up when they organized the event.

Ask a question

As an attendee, you can ask questions in the Q&A as soon as you join the event, even if the event hasn’t started yet. If the event includes a Q&A, the Q&A panel will be open when you join.

  1. Select Ask a question at the bottom of the pane
  2. Type your question in the compose box
  3. Select SendScreenshot: Send icon Screenshot: private q and a ask a question
  4. If this is a public event and you want to ask your question anonymously, your name will be optional and you can leave it blank. Then select Post as anonymous before you send your question. Screenshot: Enter question in compose box

If the moderator publishes your question, it appears on everyone’s Featured tab, along with the answer. If it isn’t published, it appears on your My questions tab where only you will see it.

“Like” someone else’s question

Select the thumbs-up Screenshot: Like button icon next to it.

Screenshot: Select the thumbs-up icon

Hide or show the Q&A pane

Select the Q&A icon Screenshot: Q&A button at the top of the pane when the pane is open to close it.

Screenshot: Icon at top of the pane

Or at the top of the screen when the pane is hidden to show it.

Personal meeting templates in Microsoft Teams

Note

  • Personal templates are available as part of Teams Premium, an add-on license that provides additional features to make Teams events more personalized, intelligent, and secure. To get access to Teams Premium, contact your IT admin.
  • Personal templates aren’t currently available on Teams for mobile.

Personal meeting templates help simplify your scheduling experience by pre-saving meeting options as templates you can use to quickly organize meetings.

Create a personal template

Create personal templates from scratch or while scheduling a new meeting.

Create a template from scratch
  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: teams-calendar-tab-icon in Teams.
  2. Select the dropdown arrow next to NewScreenshot: teams-new-event-button-icon .
  3. Select Create templateScreenshot: plus-icon-teams .
  4. In Meeting options, adjust the settings the way you want to save them in your template.
  5. Select Save as template.
  6. Name your template.
  7. Add an optional description about your template (what it’s used for, template details, etc.)
  8. Select Save.
Create a personal template while scheduling a meeting

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: teams-calendar-tab-icon in Teams.

    1. Select NewScreenshot: teams-new-event-button-icon .
    2. Select the dropdown arrow next to NewScreenshot: teams-new-event-button-icon and select an event type.

  2. Designate the meeting as a Teams meeting by either inviting attendees or turning on the Teams meeting toggle.

  3. Select Meeting optionsScreenshot: skype-teams-mobile-icon-settings .

  4. Adjust settings and select Save as template.

  5. Name your template and add an optional description about your template.

  6. Select Save.

Note

Sensitivity labels can’t be saved as part of a personal template.

Schedule using a personal template

To schedule a meeting using a personal template:

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: teams-calendar-tab-icon in Teams.

  2. Select the dropdown arrow next to NewScreenshot: teams-new-event-button-icon .

  3. Select the template under Your templates.

    • If you can’t find a template, select View all templatesScreenshot: view-all-templates-icon . Select Schedule next to the template you want to use. If you still can’t find Your templates, make sure you have the latest version of Teams.

  4. Add meeting details and invite attendees. Select SaveScreenshot: save-icon-001 .

Update or delete personal templates

Save up to 40 personal templates in Teams and keep them relevant by updating them or removing the ones you no longer use.

To update or delete a personal template:

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: teams-calendar-tab-icon in Teams.

  2. Select the dropdown arrow next to NewScreenshot: teams-new-event-button-icon .

  3. Select View all templatesScreenshot: view-all-templates-icon and find the template you want to change or remove.

    1. Select EditScreenshot: edit-pencil-icon-20x20-png to make changes to the template. Select Apply to save changes.
    2. Select DeleteScreenshot: forms-delete-button-trashcan-icon to remove the template. Once a template is deleted it can’t be recovered.

Note

After you edit a personal template, all future meetings you schedule with it will have the updated settings. Meetings already scheduled from the template, including series meetings that have future occurrences, won’t have the updated settings.

Delegate personal templates

Delegates who manage your calendar can create personal templates and use them to schedule meetings for you.

For the best experience, delegates should create personal templates in their own calendar. They can use their saved personal templates to schedule meetings in your calendar by following the steps in Schedule using a personal template.

Meeting options in Microsoft Teams

Play, share, and download meeting recordings in Microsoft Teams

Play a meeting recording

After a meeting ends, you can find the meeting’s recording in the meeting chat or calendar.

From a chat
  1. Go to ChatScreenshot: Teams Chat Tab icon in Teams.
  2. Select the chat for the specific meeting.
  3. Select Shared.
  4. Select a recording.
  5. When the viewer opens, select PlayScreenshot: Play button . Screenshot: Recording screen play selected
From your calendar
  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: teams-calendar-tab-icon in Teams.
  2. Select the past meeting you want to see the recording from.
  3. Select RecapScreenshot: recap-icon .
  4. On the meeting recording, select PlayScreenshot: Play button .
From a channel
  1. Select TeamsScreenshot: Teams button in Teams.
  2. Select a channel.
  3. Select Shared.
  4. Find and select the recording. The recording is an .mp4 file and has the Screenshot: Recording button play iconRecording icon at the beginning of the line.
  5. Select PlayScreenshot: Play button if the recording doesn’t start immediately.

Closed or live captions

Live captions are available during a meeting but aren’t recorded.

To turn on captions during a meeting:

  1. In your meeting controls, select More actionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > Language and speechScreenshot: Language and speech menu item icon .
  2. Select Show live captionsScreenshot: Closed caption menu icon .

Your captions will appear under the meeting screen. These captions are only shown to you during the meeting.

You can also start live transcription, which can be viewed after the meeting.

To view closed captions later during playback:

  1. Go to ChatScreenshot: Teams Chat Tab icon in Teams.

  2. Select the past meeting chat.

  3. Find and select the recording thumbnail.

    Screenshot: Recording thumbnail

  4. Select PlayScreenshot: Play button to start playing the meeting recording.

  5. Hover over the video player and select Toggle captionsScreenshot: Closed caption menu icon , or press Alt+C.

  6. Select your language and view.

If you don’t see Toggle captionsScreenshot: Closed caption menu icon :

  1. Select Watch in browser at the top of the video.
  2. On the video player page, select Video SettingsScreenshot: Stream video settings button .
  3. Expand Transcript and captionsScreenshot: Transcript and captions button > Generate. Screenshot: Stream Generate caption button

Depending on the length of the video, generating closed captions can take several minutes.

Once generated, you can watch the video in the browser on its player page and have captions displayed at the bottom of the screen.

When the captions have been created, the Generate button turns to Translate. Select Translate to change the spoken or screen language to automatically translate the captions.

Customize captions
  1. In the video player, hover and select Playback optionsScreenshot: Settings gear button .
  2. Select Caption settings.
  3. Choose your caption size, color, or background transparency.

Note

Captions aren’t captured in recordings or downloads. However, you can turn them on while viewing a recording in Teams or in the browser on its Microsoft 365 video player page.

Meeting recording storage and permissions

Non-channel meeting recordings are automatically stored in the organizer’s OneDrive for Business. Channel meeting recordings are stored in the channel’s SharePoint site.

Meeting recordings expire after a period of time set by your IT admin. Organizers can change recording expiration dates. When a recording expires, it will move to the recycle bin where the recording was saved.

Recovering files is time sensitive. Once recordings are deleted from the recycle bin, they can’t be restored.

To learn how to recover expired or deleted meeting recordings, see Restore deleted files in OneDrive or Restore items in SharePoint.

Channel meetings

For channel meetings, the recording will be stored on the Files tab for the channel.

The Files tab stores all files for the channel. Everyone who is a part of the channel will have permission to edit and view the recording.

All other meetings

For non-channel meetings, the recording will be stored in the Recordings folder in the meeting organizer’s OneDrive folder. If you were invited to the meeting, you can access the recording through the Files or Shared tabs in the chat, channel, or meeting details.

Note

Only the meeting organizer and co-organizers can edit the recording. But everyone invited to the meeting is able to view the recording.

Share a link to a meeting recording with others

If you organized the meeting, you can share the recording with people who weren’t invited to the meeting by sharing it like you would share any other file.

To share a recording from a meeting chat:

  1. Select ChatScreenshot: Teams Chat Tab icon in Teams.

  2. Open the meeting chat you want to share a recording from.

  3. Select the Shared tab.

  4. Hover over the recording you want to share and select More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > Copy linkScreenshot: Copy link icon .

    • To manage link access or request the owner to give access to someone outside your org, select SettingsScreenshot: Settings gear button in the Link dialog.

  5. Paste the link into a message or post to share.

Note

  • Guests and external attendees can only view a recording if they’re sent a direct link to the recording.
  • To learn more about sharing meeting recordings in OneDrive, see Share OneDrive files and folder.

To learn more, see Customize access to meeting recordings or transcripts in Microsoft Teams.

Download a meeting recording

Only the meeting organizer can download the meeting recording.

To download a meeting recording:

  1. Select the Shared tab in a meeting chat or channel.
  2. Find and select the meeting recording.
  3. Select More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > DownloadScreenshot: Teams download arrow icon .

To learn more, see Edit or delete a meeting transcript in Microsoft Teams.
