Meetings in Teams

Use SRT-In in Microsoft Teams

Note

SRT_In in Teams is available as part of the public preview program and might undergo further changes before being released publicly. To get access to this and other upcoming features, switch to Teams Public Preview.

Enable SRT-In for your Teams event to produce your event directly from an external hardware- or software-based encoder. Teams SRT-In can support an additional SRT source that will automatically failover if the first SRT stream drops from the meeting or event.

Unlike RTMP, SRT has a security layer in the encoder by default, so there’s no option to turn on Secure connection SSL. Please ensure proper SRT-In configuration before using this feature.

Note

An additional SRT-In source will only failover when the primary SRT-In source completely drops from the meeting or event. It will not failover in the event of streaming quality issues.

To schedule an event with SRT-In:

  1. Select Calendar in Teams.
  2. Select New or select an event type in the dropdown menu.
  3. Enter your event details.
  4. Select OptionsScreenshot: Settings button .
  5. In Production tools , turn the SRT - In toggle on. To use an additional SRT stream, turn the Additional SRT source toggle on.
  6. Select Apply to get a link and finish setup.

Note

If you don’t see this in your meeting options, contact your IT admin.

SRT-In link

To see the SRT-In link:

  1. Select Calendar in Teams.
  2. Select an event.
  3. Select View event > Options .
  4. In Production tools , you’ll see the Server Ingest URL.

SRT captions

To use SRT captions for your meeting or event:

  1. Select Calendar in Teams.
  2. Select an event.
  3. Select View event > Options .
  4. In Accessibility , under Translate attendee captions, verify no languages are selected.

If a language selection is made here, SRT captions will be disabled and live translated captions will be available in the selected languages.

Send video feed from Teams encoder

After you join the meeting, start streaming from your encoder using the ingest URL to display the stream to attendees.

If the meeting has Manage what attendees see enabled in your meeting options, people can select their SRT-In feed to Bring on stage.

There are a lot of ways to customize your video experience—and the video you share with others—when you join a Teams meeting or call.

Turn your video on or off

Before a meeting

To turn on your video before a meeting, turn the CameraScreenshot: Camera off icon toggle on before you join.

Screenshot: Select camera icon to turn camera on

During a meeting

To turn your video on and off during a meeting, select CameraScreenshot: Video call button in the meeting controls.

Note

To enable your camera to turn off when your screen locks during a meeting, go to Settings and moreScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > SettingsScreenshot: Settings gear icon > PrivacyScreenshot: Privacy settings button in Teams. Then, turn the Turn off my camera and mic when my screen locks toggle on. Restart Teams to activate this setting.

Apply video effects and filters

Change your background

Before a meeting, select Effects and avatarsScreenshot: Pre-meeting Effects and avatars icon to open background options.

During a meeting, select the dropdown arrow next to CameraScreenshot: Video call button to view backgrounds.

To learn more, see Change your background for a Teams meeting.

Use video filters

Customize your video feed with video filters like:

  • Soft focus to create a smoothing effect for your face over video.
  • Adjust brightness to enhance your video quality when lighting is poor.

To apply a video filter before your meeting:

  1. Select Open device settingsScreenshot: Settings button on the pre-join screen.
  2. In Video Settings, turn on the toggle next to your desired filter.

To learn more about video filters, see Apply video filters in Teams meetings.

Change your view

Gallery

Gallery is the default view during a Teams meeting. On Teams for desktop, customize how you see people in your meeting.

Note

  • Gallery view of up to 49 participant videos is only supported in the Teams desktop app.
  • When opened in a new window, Gallery view will show up to nine video participants on any device.
  • Supported devices: Windows devices with the Intel 11th generation processor (or newer) with four or more cores and Mac devices with Apple Silicon (M1 and M2 chipsets or newer).
  • To provide the best possible audio and video quality, we might decrease the number of videos you’re seeing at once if you’re running low on bandwidth or device memory.

Screenshot: Screenshot showing updated Gallery view during a meeting

For people who haven’t turned on their videos, Teams shows their profile pic instead (or their initials if they haven’t added one).

Change gallery size

In Teams for desktop, you can choose to view 4, 9, 16, or 49 people at a time, depending on how many people are in your meeting. In Teams for web, you can see 4 or 9 people at a time.

Devices might show fewer participant videos based on hardware capabilities.

To change gallery size:

  1. Select ViewScreenshot: Gallery view icon in the meeting window.
  2. Select Select max gallery size.
  3. Choose how many people you want to see.

Note

To change gallery size, make sure GalleryScreenshot: Gallery view icon is selected under ViewScreenshot: Gallery view icon .

Prioritize videos

GalleryScreenshot: Gallery view icon view will show participants equally in the meeting window, whether their cameras are turned on or off. Prioritize video to see more people who have their cameras on.

To prioritize video:

  1. Select ViewScreenshot: Gallery view icon in the meeting window.
  2. Select Prioritize video.

Note

To prioritize videos, make sure GalleryScreenshot: Gallery view icon is selected under ViewScreenshot: Gallery view icon .

Reposition your video

See more video feeds during your meeting by repositioning your video feed in the meeting window. You can place your video outside the meeting window or hide it altogether.

To hide your video:

  1. Select ViewScreenshot: Gallery view icon in your meeting controls.
  2. Select More options > Hide meScreenshot: Teams Hide icon .

This option only hides your video from your view. Other people in your meeting will still be able to see your video unless you turn your camera off.

To unhide your video:

  1. Select ViewScreenshot: Gallery view icon in your meeting controls.
  2. Select More options > Unhide meScreenshot: Hide objects button .

Note

To reposition your video, make sure GalleryScreenshot: Gallery view icon is selected under ViewScreenshot: Gallery view icon .

Large gallery

In large meetings, Teams’ Large gallery view shows up to 49 participant videos in the meeting window at once.

Screenshot: Large gallery view showing 49 videos at once

Note

If no one is sharing video, Large gallery won’t be available.

When more than 49 participants join a Teams meetings, select the navigation controls < > at the bottom of the gallery to view or engage with more participants.

Screenshot: 806eab8b-5beb-4578-934b-0f69a4824a1f

Focus on content

Pay close attention and eliminate distractions while someone is presenting content.

To focus on content:

  1. Join your meeting.
  2. In the meeting controls, select ViewScreenshot: Gallery view icon > Focus on content.

Pin a video

Pin your own video

To pin your own video:

  1. Hover over your video feed.
  2. Select More optionsScreenshot: More options button next to your name.
  3. Select Pin for meScreenshot: Teams Pin Chat icon . This will pin your video for your own view, others won’t see you pinned.
  4. To unpin yourself, hover over your video feed and select More optionsScreenshot: More options button > Unpin for meScreenshot: Chat unpin icon .
Pin someone’s video

Pin someone’s video to see it regardless of who’s talking.

To pin someone’s video:

  1. Hover over their video feed.
  2. Select More optionsScreenshot: More options button next to their name.
  3. Select Pin for meScreenshot: Teams Pin Chat icon .
  4. To unpin someone, hover over their video feed and select More optionsScreenshot: More options button > Unpin for meScreenshot: Chat unpin icon .

Spotlight a video

Spotlight someone’s video feed to highlight it for everyone in the meeting. Organizers and presenters can spotlight anyone’s video feed, including their own.

To spotlight a video feed:

  1. Hover over the video feed and select More optionsScreenshot: More options button .
  2. Select Spotlight for everyoneScreenshot: Spotlight video .
  3. To remove a video feed from the spotlight, hover over it and select More optionsScreenshot: More options button > Stop spotlightingScreenshot: Exit spotlight video .

People can also exit the spotlight themselves by selecting Exit spotlightScreenshot: Exit spotlight video in their meeting controls.

For more details, see Spotlight someone’s video in a Teams meeting.

Reframe a video

Teams crops some videos to make them fit your screen better. If you want a different view of a particular video—for example, if someone’s cropped out of the video or it only shows part of their face—select More optionsScreenshot: More options button in their video feed then Fit to frame to see the entire video.

Select Fill frame to see a closer, cropped view.

When you join a Teams meeting or call on the mobile app, you can customize your video experience—and the video you share with others—in a bunch of different ways.

Turn your video on or off

Before a meeting

To turn on your video before a meeting, tap Video is offScreenshot: Teams video off icon before you join.

During a meeting

To turn your camera on or off during a meeting, tap the camera icon in your meeting controls.

Screenshot: Camera button in meeting controls

Blur your background

Blur your background before or during a meeting to subtly conceal what’s behind you. You’ll appear nice and clear in the foreground.

To blur your background before a meeting:

  1. Tap Background effectsScreenshot: Background settings in the corner of your screen.
  2. Tap the blurred background effect to preview it.
  3. Tap Done to apply the effect.
  4. Tap Join to enter the meeting with your camera on and background blurred.

To blur your background during a meeting:

  1. Tap More actionsScreenshot: More options button in your meeting controls.
  2. Tap Background effectsScreenshot: Background settings .
  3. Tap the blurred background effect to preview it.
  4. Tap Done to apply the effect.

For more details about changing your background, see Change your background for a Teams meeting.

Change your view

Customize how you see other people’s video during a Teams meeting with Views . For example, in a large meeting, you may want to see as many video feeds as you can at one time.

The following examples show the default Gallery view on different devices.

Phone view exampleScreenshot: Eight different video streams on one screenTablet view exampleScreenshot: Nine different video streams on a tablet screen

  1. Select More actionsScreenshot: More options button > Views .
  2. Tap the view you want. Screenshot: Video layout options
  3. Pinch in or out to zoom and adjust your view.
Gallery

The default view when you join a meeting. When there are more than seven others in attendance (eight if you’re using a tablet), Teams features the people who have their video turned on and those who speak the most. Your video feed always appears in the corner of the screen.

  • If you’re using a phone, you can see up to eight featured participant videos and 15 additional people to scroll through at the bottom of the screen.
  • If you’re using a tablet, you can see up to nine featured participant videos and 20 additional people to scroll through at the bottom of the screen.
Large gallery

This option is available when at least nine people have their cameras turned on. You can view up to 100 participant videos (though not all at once).

The number of people you can see on your screen at once depends on your device and its software.

  • Phone
    • iOS 13 or later: 10 people at once
    • iOS 12 or earlier: 49 people at once (lower resolution)
    • Android 9 or later (or greater than 4 GB RAM): 10 people at once
    • Android 8 or earlier (or less than 4 GB RAM): 49 people at once (lower resolution)
  • Tablet
    • iOS 13 or later: 9 people at once
    • iOS 12 or earlier: 49 people at once (lower resolution)
    • Android 9 or later (or greater than 4 GB RAM): 9 people at once
    • Android 8 or earlier (or less than 4 GB RAM): 49 people at once (lower resolution)
  • Swipe left or right to view or engage with more participants.

Pin someone’s video

To pin someone’s video to your view:

  1. Press and hold their video.
  2. Tap Pin for meScreenshot: Teams Pin Chat icon .

To unpin someone’s video from your view:

  1. Press and hold their video.
  2. Tap UnpinScreenshot: Chat unpin icon .

Spotlight a video

When a video is spotlighted, it’s pinned for everyone in the meeting. Spotlighting someone’s video isn’t currently supported on Teams for mobile, but you can see who other people have spotlighted.

For more info, see Spotlight someone’s video in a Teams meeting.

Hardware acceleration

Experience better video quality, power efficiency, and device performance during Teams meetings with hardware acceleration in compatible iOS and Android mobile devices. Devices with hardware acceleration compatibility offload video processing from the CPU to specialized hardware in the device.

On devices with hardware acceleration, you’ll automatically experience:

  • Higher maximum video resolution during meetings (360p to 720p)
  • Lower battery consumption
  • Reduced device heating

To view a list of currently supported devices, see Hardware acceleration devices.

Using the green room in Microsoft Teams

Prepare in the green room with other organizers and presenters before a Teams meeting or event to test content sharing, video and audio settings, and more. Return to the green room when the event ends to debrief and discuss the event.

Set up the green room

To set up a meeting or event with a green room:

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: Teams Calendar tab icon in Teams.
  2. Select an event and select View eventScreenshot: teams-expand-icon .
  3. Select OptionsScreenshot: Settings icon .
  4. In RolesScreenshot: People or Show Participants button , change Who can present to Specific people or Only organizers and co-organizers.
  5. In the Search for participants field, enter presenter names. Presenters must already be invited as attendees to appear in the drop-down list.
  6. In Production toolsScreenshot: Production tools icon in Microsoft Teams , turn on the Enable Green room toggle.
  7. Select Apply.

Organizers can turn the green room on or off while a meeting is active by selecting ControlsScreenshot: controls-icon > View more options in the meeting controls, but the change won’t be reflected unless the meeting ends and restarts.

Note

Green room is currently supported in Teams for desktop and web (Edge and Chrome browsers only) and mobile Teams meetings on iOS and Android devices. The meeting organizer may call into the meeting but others who dial in, dial out, or use the Call me functionality may not be greeted with the proper voice prompt.

Join the green room

You’ll automatically join the green room before starting the meeting for attendees. Bring presenters on screen, set up shared content, and more.

To join the green room:

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: Teams Calendar tab icon in Teams.
  2. Select the town hall you want to start.
  3. Select Join > Join now.
Join by phone

Join or invite others to join by phone during a Teams meeting or event.

Find town hall dial-in codes by selecting Share event in the event details. The codes must be shared with presenters directly. If an organizer or presenter joins a webinar or town hall by phone, they’ll join as an attendee until they’re promoted to presenter by an organizer.

If an organizer or presenter requests someone to join a webinar, town hall, or structured meeting by phone, that person will enter the waiting room as an attendee until their role is changed to Presenter.

To learn more, see Roles in Microsoft Teams meetings.

Note

To allow people to join the green room directly, turn the People dialing in can bypass the lobby toggle on in meeting options. Otherwise, you can admit them into the green room from the lobby.

Green room experience

Before the meeting

From the green room, organizers can change meeting options and admit participants from the lobby into the meeting.

Screenshot: fcad6e1f-f073-4ce0-a733-97e800af8acd

Both organizers and presenters can:

  • Chat. The chat available to the organizers and presenters in the green room is the global chat available to all in the meeting.
  • Manage what attendees see.
  • Turn on captions.
  • Add apps to the meeting, such as Q&A. When an organizer adds an app to the meeting, attendees will be able to access the app while they wait.
  • Access meeting notes.
  • See and remove participants.
  • See other presenter’s and organizer’s audio, video, and shared content.
  • React and see reactions.
  • Start the meeting. Only presenters and organizers who join using Teams for desktop or web (Edge and Chrome browsers) can start the meeting.

Organizers and presenters can’t change the meeting layout or turn on transcripts, recording, or Speaker Coach from the green room. They’ll be able to do so when the meeting starts.

There are some limitations when organizers and presenters join the green room:

  • CVI participants will join as attendees and can’t interact with people in the green room until they’re promoted to presenters. While the CVI participants are attendees, they’ll see a blank screen before the event starts and after the event ends.

  • If someone in the green room is made an attendee, they won’t be able to turn on their mic or camera.

  • When an attendee waiting for a meeting to start is made a presenter, other attendees waiting for the meeting to start will be able to hear them. We recommend demoting them to avoid any live microphones.

  • Compliance recording will not be available to those who join the green room or attendees who are waiting for the meeting to start; however, compliance recording will start for all specified participants once the meeting has also started.

Note

Green room capacity is limited to 100 presenters at a time.

During the meeting

Meeting recording and transcription will resume if they were paused due to the green room. If captions were turned on in the green room, they’ll continue to work as expected in the meeting.

Note

If automatic recording is turned on, captions won’t work until the meeting starts. To make sure captions are available in the green room, don’t turn on Record and transcribe automatically in the meeting options.

After the meeting

Return to the green room after the meeting by selecting End meeting in your meeting controls.

Screenshot: Screenshot of a Microsoft Teams meeting or event with the End event button highlighted.

When you select End meeting, the event will stop recording and transcribing automatically. You’ll also see a notification that the event has ended and recording has stopped.

Screenshot: Screenshot of a meeting notification that says the meeting has ended for attendees and recording has stopped.

Attendees will return to the waiting room while organizers and presenters stay in the green room to debrief and discuss the event.

  • If Manage mode is turned on, organizers and presenters will be removed from the meeting stage when the event ends. They’ll see a message on the stage and can turn off Manage Mode if they want to.
  • Ending an event won’t interrupt an organizer or presenter’s screen sharing.

At the end of the event, organizers and presenters will still have access to the backroom chat.

Note

Presenters and organizers joining from mobile devices will return to the green room but won’t have the End event button.

Add and remove people

Add and remove people from the green room by changing their roles during the meeting or event. To bring someone into the green room, change their role to Presenter.

To make someone a presenter:

  1. Select PeopleScreenshot: People or Show Participants button in your meeting controls.
  2. In the Participants pane, find the person you want to bring into the green room from the Attendees list.
  3. Hover over the person’s name and select More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > Make a presenterScreenshot: Make a presenter icon in Microsoft Teams .
  4. Select Change.

The person will enter the green room automatically when you change their role.

To remove someone from the green room, change their role back to Attendee.

To make someone an attendee:

  1. Select PeopleScreenshot: People or Show Participants button in your meeting controls.
  2. In the Participants pane, find the person you want to bring into the green room from the Presenters list.
  3. Hover over the person’s name and select More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > Make an attendeeScreenshot: Make an attendee icon in Microsoft Teams .
  4. Select Change.

To learn more, see Roles in Microsoft Teams meetings.

Attendee experience

While the green room is active, attendees will be in the waiting room where they’ll be greeted by a waiting screen and can interact via chat or use enabled apps, like Q&A.

Screenshot: 94716b8a-ac81-482e-9b13-779d5c4f3133

Attendees can’t turn on their mics or cameras or see and hear what’s happening in the green room. They also can’t access the participant panel but can view people in or invited to the meeting.

When you end an event, attendees will automatically return to the waiting room and see this message until they leave.

Screenshot: Screenshot showing the attendee view when a Microsoft Teams event ends.

At the end of the event, attendees will still have access to view and send messages in the global chat.

Note

Meeting organizers may receive a Start Meeting notification if a participant joins a meeting. This doesn’t mean the meeting has officially started. When the green room is enabled for a meeting, only presenters or organizers can start the meeting.

Using the lobby in Microsoft Teams meetings

Use the meeting lobby in Teams meetings to keep people from directly entering a meeting when they join. Organizers, co-organizers, and presenters will be notified when people enter the lobby and can let them into the meeting.

Lobby settings

Each meeting defaults to the lobby settings set by your IT admin but you can change them before or during the meeting. You might not be able to change some settings if your meeting uses a template or sensitivity label.

Choose who can bypass the lobby

As the meeting organizer, you get to decide who gets into your meetings directly, and who should wait for someone to let them in.

If you choose to have people wait, you (and anyone else allowed to admit people) will see a list of people in the lobby. From there you can choose whether to admit or deny them.

  • Only organizers and co-organizers
    • What happens: As the meeting organizer, you and any co-organizers can get into the meeting directly. Everyone else will wait in the lobby.
    • Recommended when…: You want everyone else to wait in the lobby until you’re ready to admit them.
  • People who were invited*
    • What happens: Anyone who receives the invitation, including those to whom it is forwarded, will join the meeting directly. People without a Teams account won’t bypass the lobby. Additionally, distribution lists up to 10,000 users are supported. If you don’t want people to forward the invite to others, turn off Allow Forwarding in the invitation.
    • Recommended when…: You want a specific, limited group of people who were invited via their Teams accounts to join the meeting directly, and everyone else to wait in the lobby.
  • People in my org
    • What happens: Only people within your org can get into your meeting directly. Everyone else will wait in the lobby.
    • Recommended when…: You want all guests and external people to wait in the lobby so you can approve them one by one.
  • People in my org and guests
    • What happens: People in your org and people with guest access can get into your meeting directly.
    • Recommended when…: You want all external people (anyone outside your org, except guests) to wait in the lobby so you can approve them one by one.
  • People in my org, trusted orgs, and guests
    • What happens: Anyone from your organization and organizations with which your IT admin has set up a connection, or anyone joining as a guest, will be able to bypass the lobby.
    • Recommended when…: You want some external people (e.g., people joining without a Teams account and people from organizations with which your IT admin did not set up a connection) to wait in the lobby so you can approve them one by one.
  • Everyone
    • What happens: Anyone who has access to the meeting link gets into the meeting directly, including people who call in. Depending on the meeting policy set up by your IT admin, people joining without a Teams account, people from untrusted organizations, and people dialing in may be placed in the lobby until someone from your organization or a trusted organization joins the meeting, even if the Everyone option is selected.
    • Recommended when…: You don’t want anyone to wait in the lobby. You want everyone to be able to join your meetings without specific approval.

* For channel meetings, only those channel members who are directly invited can bypass the lobby.

Change lobby settings

You can change lobby settings before, during, or after a meeting (in the case of a meeting series). The changes will only apply to the meeting you change them in unless the meeting is part of a series. Then, changes will be applied to all future meetings in that series. To change default lobby settings, contact your IT admin.

Before a meeting

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: Teams Calendar tab icon in Teams.

  2. Select an event.

  3. Select View eventScreenshot: teams-expand-icon .

    • To edit a meeting series, select Edit series.

  4. Select OptionsScreenshot: Settings button .

  5. In Meeting accessScreenshot: Meeting access icon in Microsoft Teams :

    • Choose an option from the Who can bypass the lobby? dropdown menu.
    • Turn the People dialing in can bypass the lobby toggle on or off.
    • Choose who can let people into the meeting from the Who can admit from the lobby dropdown menu.

  6. Select Apply.

During a meeting

If you change lobby settings during a meeting, people waiting in the lobby will still be there.

  1. Select ControlsScreenshot: controls-icon> View more options in your meeting controls.

  2. In Meeting accessScreenshot: teams-meeting-access-icon :

    • Choose an option from the Who can bypass the lobby? dropdown menu.
    • Turn the People dialing in can bypass the lobby toggle on or off, if available.
    • Choose who can let people into the meeting from the Who can admit from the lobby dropdown menu.

  3. Select Apply.

Manage the lobby

During a meeting, people you designated to manage the lobby can admit or deny entrance to the meeting.

Who can manage the lobby

The meeting organizer, co-organizer(s), and presenter(s) can manage the lobby. If you’re the organizer, choose which of those roles can manage the lobby during that specific meeting. You can also make someone a co-organizer or presenter by changing their meeting role.

To change who can manage the lobby:

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: Teams Calendar tab icon in Teams.

  2. Select an event.

  3. Select View eventScreenshot: teams-expand-icon .

    • To edit a meeting series, select Edit series.

  4. Select OptionsScreenshot: Settings button .

  5. In Meeting accessScreenshot: Meeting access icon in Microsoft Teams , choose who can let people into the meeting from the Who can admit from the lobby dropdown menu.

  6. Select Apply.

Admit or deny participants

During the meeting, people managing the lobby can see a list of participants waiting to get into the meeting and choose whether to admit or deny them.

To admit or deny participants:

  1. Select PeopleScreenshot: People or Show Participants button in your meeting window.

  2. Under Waiting in the lobby:

    • Select the check mark next to someone’s name to admit them.
    • Select the X next to someone’s name to deny them.
    • Select Admit all to let everyone in from the lobby.

Lobby chat

Screenshot: Screenshot showing the lobby chat pane open for a Teams meeting.

Send chat messages to attendees waiting in the lobby to communicate delays, waiting times, or any prerequisites or tasks to complete before joining.

Organizers can view and send messages in the lobby chat when at least one person is in the lobby. If the lobby is empty, lobby chat won’t be available.

To view and send messages in the lobby chat:

  • Select ChatScreenshot: teams-chat-tab-icon in Teams. Open the meeting chat and select Lobby.
  • Select ChatScreenshot: teams-chat-tab-icon in your meeting controls. In the chat pane, select Lobby.

Organizers can view all lobby chat messages before, during, and after the meeting.

Note

  • The Lobby option only appears while someone is waiting in the lobby.
  • Lobby chat doesn’t support the following: Message reactions, replies, @mentions, emoji, GIFs, stickers, Rewrite with Copilot, Loop components, Actions and appsScreenshot: plus-icon-teams functionalities (add an app, attach a file, record video clip, etc.).
Attendee view

When a new message is sent in the lobby chat, the lobby chat pane will open automatically for attendees on the pre-join screen, ensuring no one misses a message. They can also select Lobby chatScreenshot: teams-chat-tab-icon on the pre-join screen to view messages.

Screenshot: Screenshot showing the lobby chat pane open for a Teams meeting.

Attendees won’t be able to send replies or reactions and will only see messages sent while they were in the lobby. Any messages sent before they joined won’t be visible to them. Lobby chat messages don’t appear in the main meeting chat and aren’t accessible to attendees after they join the meeting.

Lobby notifications

People managing the lobby will receive notifications that people are waiting in the lobby. In the notifications, select View lobby to go right to the lobby or Mute these notificationsScreenshot: Icon to snooze or mute in Microsoft Teams to turn the notifications off.

Screenshot: Screenshot of a lobby notification highlighting the Mute these notifications icon.

Select Undo to turn the notifications back on.

Turn off the lobby for a meeting

If you want everyone to join your meeting directly, set Who can bypass the lobby? to Everyone. This change will apply to that meeting and future meetings if it’s part of a meeting series. Contact your IT admin if you want to change this setting for all the future meetings you organize.

Note

If anonymous participants join first, they’ll wait in the lobby. They’ll be let into the meeting automatically after someone from your org, a trusted org, or a guest user joins. Contact your IT admin to allow anonymous participants to start meetings.

You can also remove people or lock your meeting.

To remove people from the meeting:

  1. Select PeopleScreenshot: People or Show Participants button in your meeting window.
  2. Hover over the name of the person you want to remove.
  3. Select More options Screenshot: More options icon** > Remove from meeting**.

Video recap in Microsoft Teams

Note

Video recap in Teams is available as part of Microsoft 365 Copilot, an add-on license that provides additional features to make Teams meetings more personalized, intelligent, and secure. To get access to an eligible license, contact your IT admin.*

Catch up on key conversations and moments from meetings with Microsoft Teams video recaps. After a recorded and transcribed meeting ends, Teams generates a narrated highlight video that captures presented content, real video clips, and discussion from the meeting.

Note

Video recaps aren’t currently supported on Teams for mobile devices.*

Watch a video recap

To watch a video recap in Teams:

  • Select Recap in the meeting chat after the meeting ends. Select Video recap.

  • Select a past meeting in your Teams calendar and select View recap.

Note

Video recaps are generated by AI and should be checked for accuracy.*

Video recap requirements

For a video recap to generate after a meeting:

  • The meeting must be between 10 and 90 minutes long.

  • The meeting must be recorded and transcribed.

  • The meeting must have cloud recording enabled.

Storage & limits

  • Video recap data (highlight metadata, audio clips, and captions) is stored as alternate streams on the original Teams meeting recording file in SharePoint/OneDrive.

  • Video recaps consume minimal SharePoint/OneDrive storage.

  • Video recaps are stored alongside the original recording; no separate files are created.

FAQ

Are video recaps available for all meetings?

Video recaps require cloud recording and transcription to be enabled. They’re generated automatically for eligible meetings—check with your IT admin for availability in your organization.

Can I share a video recap?

A video recap is part of the meeting recap. Anyone with access to the recording can view the video recap. Share the meeting recap with people that you want to give video recap access to.

How long does it take to generate a video recap?

A video recap is generated available 10 to 15 minutes after the meeting recording and transcription are successfully uploaded. Timing may vary based on meeting length.

Voice isolation in Microsoft Teams calls and meetings

Filter out background noise during Teams calls and meetings with voice isolation. Voice isolation uses AI to block surrounding noise so others can hear you clearly.

How it works

When you add a voice profile, Teams will know which sounds to keep (your voice) and which ones to filter out. Voice isolation also filters out sound from other speakers to prevent echoes. Voice isolation is powered by AI within Teams.

Add your voice profile

Add a voice profile to start using voice isolation in your meetings and calls. A voice profile takes about 30 seconds to make and can be deleted anytime.

To add your voice profile:

  1. Select Settings and moreScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > Settings Screenshot: Settings button in Teams.

  2. Select RecognitionScreenshot: Start transcription button .

  3. Select Create voice profile.

    Note

    If you don’t see RecognitionScreenshot: Start transcription button in your settings, contact your IT admin.

  4. Choose your microphone from the dropdown menu.

  5. Select Start voice capture and read the provided text.

  6. When you finish reading, select Stop voice capture.

  7. Select Close.

Turn off voice isolation

Voice isolation will be active in your calls and meetings after you add your voice profile.

To turn off voice isolation in a Teams meeting:

  1. Select the dropdown arrow next to MicScreenshot: Mute button in your meeting controls.
  2. Turn off the Noise suppression toggle.

You can also access these settings by selecting the dropdown arrow next to MicScreenshot: Mute button and selecting More audio settings.

How it looks

After you add your voice profile, indicators will tell you when and how voice isolation is working in your meeting or call.

    • What it means: Voice isolation is turned on and active.
    • What it means: You entered the meeting with your mic muted.
    • What it means: Only your name is displayed. Unwanted audio isn’t detected and voice isolation is active.
    • What it means: Voice isolation is active and filtering out unwanted audio.
    • What it means: Someone nearby is detected (e.g., you and a colleague are sharing your device for the meeting). If you want them to be heard, select Turn off voice isolation .

Troubleshooting

If you’re having issues adding a voice profile:

  • Make sure you’re in a relatively quiet environment.
  • Connect your microphone again or use a different one to improve your audio.
  • Restart Teams.
  • Check Teams for updates.
  • Delete and recreate your voice profile.

You might receive one of these alerts in Teams. Learn what they mean and how to resolve them:

    • What this means: There’s an issue with turning on voice isolation in your meeting or call. Restart Teams to reload voice isolation.
    • What this means: Your device is running too many apps and can’t support voice isolation. Try closing other apps on your device. Then, turn voice isolation off, then back on.

Watermark for Teams meetings

Note

Watermark is available as part of Teams Premium, an add-on license that provides additional features to make Teams meetings more personalized, intelligent, and secure. To get access to Teams Premium, contact your IT admin.

Protect confidential content during your meetings by applying a watermark.

When you apply a watermark, participants will see their own email address overlaid across shared content in the meeting window. This deters people from taking unauthorized screenshots of shared content.

Screenshot: 363b8386-fa69-4029-a0cd-e73012e617cd

Apply watermarks to your meeting

To apply watermarks to a meeting, turn them on before the meeting starts. If you turn on watermarks after a meeting starts, the setting won’t take effect unless everyone leaves the meeting and rejoins.

To apply watermarks to shared content in a meeting:

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: Teams Calendar tab icon in Teams.

  2. Select an event.

  3. Select View eventScreenshot: teams-expand-icon .

    • To edit a meeting series, select Edit series.

  4. Select OptionsScreenshot: Settings icon .

  5. In Advanced protectionScreenshot: Privacy settings button :

    • Turn the Apply a watermark to shared content toggle on to apply a watermark when someone shares their screen.
    • Turn the Apply a watermark to everyone’s video feed toggle on to apply a watermark over people’s video feed. Use this when people use their cameras to share physical objects, like whiteboards and documents. To learn more, see Share whiteboards and documents using your camera in Microsoft Teams meetings.

  6. Select Apply.

Customize watermarks

Customize watermarks in your meeting by choosing the watermark pattern and adjusting its transparency level.

To customize watermarks:

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: Teams Calendar tab icon in Teams.

  2. Select an event.

  3. Select View eventScreenshot: teams-expand-icon .

    • To edit a meeting series, select Edit series.

  4. Select OptionsScreenshot: Settings icon .

  5. In Advanced protectionScreenshot: Privacy settings button :

    • Select a Pattern for the watermark(s) you want to apply.
    • Adjust the Transparency level slider for the watermark(s) you turned on to make the pattern appear more or less opaque.

  6. Select Apply.

Watermark limitations

Refer to the table for a list of watermark experience variations and corresponding meeting limitations.

  • If watermark is enabled for shared content…
    • Meeting limitations: Unavailable features: large gallery view, shared content from cameras
  • If watermark is enabled for everyone’s video feed…
    • Meeting limitations: Unavailable features: large gallery view
  • If watermark is enabled…
    • Meeting limitations: Audio only (no viewable shared content): VDI, participants who aren’t signed in (anonymous participants), Direct Guest Join , meeting overflow (greater than 1,000 participants), older Teams versions, Microsoft Teams (preview)

Troubleshooting

Can I apply a watermark to a meeting series? Yes, if you enable watermark in the meeting options, it will take effect for all meetings in the series.

If I already have a meeting scheduled, do I need to schedule a new one to use watermark in meeting? No, you can open the meeting from Outlook or your Teams calendar, go to Meeting options and turn the Apply a watermark toggle on. Make sure to select either the single occurrence or the meeting series as necessary.

Can I turn on a watermark during the meeting or turn it off while I’m in the meeting? No, these changes to enable or disable watermark do not take effect once the meeting has begun. You must enable a watermark before the meeting starts. Organizers can turn on the watermark from Meeting options during the meeting, but the watermark won’t take effect unless everyone leaves and rejoins the meeting. However, whether participants leave and rejoin or not, it will be enabled on all future meetings in the series.

Why can’t I see the watermark features in Meeting options? Watermark is only available if you have a Teams Premium license. To make sure this policy is enabled, contact your IT admin.

Meetings and events

Attend an event in Microsoft Teams

Depending on the event size and settings, attendees can engage with presenters and each other in various ways. Attendees may be able to use their mics and cameras, participate in the event Q&A and chat, and use live reactions.

Note

Availability of engagement features during events, such as raised hands and reactions, may vary depending on event size. To learn more, see Microsoft Teams event features at scale.

Join an event

Join an event in the Teams Events app up to 15 minutes before the event starts. If you’re an organizer, co-organizer, presenter, or invited attendee, your invite will also contain dial-in codes to join by phone. External presenters won’t have dial-in codes.

To join an event directly in Teams:

  • Select CalendarScreenshot: calendar icon in Teams. Select the event you want to join and select JoinScreenshot: teams camera icon .

  • Select EventsScreenshot: events app icon on the left side of Teams. Select the event you want to join and select JoinScreenshot: teams camera icon .

    • Can’t find your event? Select the Registered filter in Upcoming events in your org to see events you’ve registered for.

  • If you registered for an event, join from the registration link provided via email.

Use live translated captions

Depending on your event type, you’ll have different options to understand your event presenters better with live translated captions. Some events will allow you to choose from up to six or 10 preset languages based on the organizer’s Office, M365, or Teams Premium offerings.

To use live translated captions during an event:

  1. Select CaptionScreenshot: closed captions icon in your Teams window.

  2. Hover over Caption language or trackScreenshot: settings-icon-1 .

  3. Select the language most familiar to you.

You’ll now be able to view live captions in the selected language.

Note

In some events, depending on your Office, M365, or Teams Premium offerings, you may have more languages to select from. Selecting these translated languages will be the same as your current meeting experiences.

Raise your hand

To raise your hand during an event, select RaiseScreenshot: raise hand icon in your meeting controls. If others’ hands are also raised, numbers will appear next to the raised hands indicating the order in which they were raised.

When you finish speaking, your hand will automatically be lowered unless you choose to keep it raised.

To learn more, see Raise your hand in Microsoft Teams.

Use live reactions

Express your reaction towards what’s being shared during an event by selecting a live reaction. When you select one, it’ll pop up momentarily in the meeting window. Live reactions are visible to everyone in an event.

To use a live reaction during an event:

  • On Teams for desktop, select ReactScreenshot: react-icon in your meeting controls and choose a reaction.

  • On Teams for mobile, tap MoreScreenshot: teams-ellipses-icon and choose a reaction.

To learn more about live reactions in Teams, see Express yourself in Microsoft Teams meetings with live reactions.

Speak during an event

Ask questions or share comments during an event by raising your hand to request to speak. When you speak, everyone in the audience will be able to hear you.

To request to speak during an event:

  1. Select RaiseScreenshot: raise hand icon in your meeting controls.

  2. Select Raise hand. The organizer will see your request to speak.

  3. You’ll see a notification when it’s almost your turn to speak.

  4. When it’s your turn to speak, select CameraScreenshot: teams camera icon or MicScreenshot: teams-mute-mic-icon to share your video or unmute yourself.

When you’re finished speaking, the organizer will take you off the main screen.

Participate in Q&A

Post, reply, and react to questions during an event by participating in Q&A. If the Q&A is moderated, you’ll receive a notification that an organizer received your question and will review it before posting it.

To open Q&A, select Q&AScreenshot: qa-icon-1 in your meeting controls.

To ask a question, type in the Ask a question text box at the top of the Q&A panel.

To learn more, see Q&A in Microsoft Teams meetings.

Rewind during an event

In certain events, you may be able to previous moments during an event or watch from the beginning if you join after it starts. Move your cursor over the event window to surface the progress bar. Then, select a past point on the progress bar to rewind and watch from that moment on.

To return to the live presentation, select Watch LiveScreenshot: production-tools-icon-1 beneath the progress bar.

Note

Reactions and raised hands are only available when you’re watching the event live. The event chat and Q&A will always reflect live activity.

Leave an event

Leave an event anytime by selecting LeaveScreenshot: teams leave meeting icon in the top corner of your Teams window.

    The app will search for and then list nearby Teams Rooms. If you don’t see the Teams Rooms device you want, move closer to it.

Create an event in the Microsoft Teams Events app

Use the Events app in Microsoft Teams to create, customize, and manage events such as webinars, town halls, or large meetings from a single experience. Events organized in both the Events app and Teams calendar will appear in the Events app, where they can be managed.

Important

If you created your event in the Teams calendar, these experiences may look different. For help customizing events scheduled from your Teams calendar, see Schedule a town hall in Microsoft Teams and Schedule a webinar in Microsoft Teams.

Create an event

Schedule an event from scratch in the Events app to tailor the experience to your exact needs. From the event capacity to attendee features, every element of your event can be customized.

For more structure while scheduling, choose a template that most represents the type of event you want to host. You can always modify template settings while scheduling.

To create a new event in the Events app:

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: events app icon on the left side of Teams.

    • If Events isn’t pinned on your app bar, select View more appsScreenshot: teams-ellipses-icon on the left side of Teams. Then, search and select Events.

  2. Select Create eventScreenshot: add-event-glyph-1 .

  3. Select Create an event from scratchScreenshot: add-glyph or choose an event template.

Fill out event details

Whether you’re creating an event from scratch or using a pre-existing template, customize details and settings to tailor the event to your needs.

To customize event details and settings:

  1. In Add event details:

    • Enter a Name for your event.

    • Add a Description to tell attendees about your event.

    • Specify start and end dates and times.

  2. In Where’s this event happening?, add a location if applicable.

    • If you’re adding a Teams Room, select Teams rooms options to specify who the room is for.

    • In the Set up room for dropdown menu:

      • Select Presenting if the room is for people who will be speaking or presenting during the event. When that room joins, it will have the option to join as a presenter or attendee.

      • Select Attendee viewing if the room is for event attendees. When that room joins, it won’t have the option to join as a presenter.

    • To learn more, see Host or attend an event from a Microsoft Teams Room.

  3. In Who’s planning this event:

    • In the Send invites from this mailbox dropdown menu, designate the mailbox that invites will be sent from. Send emails from yourself, a delegate, an event mailbox, or a shared mailbox. Anyone with access to the specified mailbox will be able to edit the event.

    • Add optional co-organizers and presenters. They’ll receive invites when you save the event.

  4. In Who can attend:

    • Specify who will have access to the event.

    • Invite people and groups.

    • Turn on registration if needed.

  5. In Set up experience and options:

    • Set your event capacity. Turn on the Optimize for large audience toggle to apply settings that best accommodate larger events. Once your event is saved, this setting can’t be changed.

    • Select attendee participation features to turn them on or off and preview how they’ll appear during the event.

    • Turn Manage what attendees see on or off for more control over how content and people appear during the event.

    • Turn the Enable Green room toggle on to give yourself and other organizers and presenters a place to check audio, video, and screen setup before the event starts.

    • Select All options for more meeting options.

    Note

    Some features may be unavailable depending on your event size and licensing. To learn more about scaling event features, see Microsoft Teams event features at scale.

  6. Select Save and ContinueScreenshot: save icon .

Your changes will be saved. Presenters and organizers will receive invites when you save the event and have access to make changes. Attendees won’t receive invites nor be able to view the event until you publish it.

Important

After your event is saved as a draft, the mailbox selection and choice to optimize for a large audience can’t be changed.

Designate mailbox for event emails

When creating an event, you can choose which mailbox sends invitations and event emails. Once your event is saved as a draft, the mailbox selection can’t be changed.

There are several mailbox options:

  • Event mailbox: A dedicated mailbox is created for the event. Emails are sent from this event-specific identity and co-organizers will have full scheduling and editing capabilities.

  • Your mailbox: Emails are sent from your personal mailbox, and co-organizers have limited capabilities.

  • Delegate mailbox: Emails are sent by a delegate on behalf of another person. Other delegates for that person can also edit the event.

  • Shared mailbox: Emails are sent from a shared organizational mailbox created and managed by your org’s admin. Anyone with access to that mailbox can edit the event.

Co-organizers only have full parity when using an event mailbox. With other options, co-organizers may not be able to edit scheduling details or manage other event elements. To learn more, see Manage Microsoft Teams events in shared mailbox and delegate scenarios.

If a shared mailbox was set up using classic Outlook, it won’t appear as an option in the Send invites from this mailbox dropdown menu. To resolve this:

  1. Turn on shared calendar improvements in Outlook.
  2. Restart Outlook.
  3. In Outlook, re-add the missing calendar.
  4. Close and reopen the Teams Events app.

Existing meetings won’t be affected and no data will be lost. If you still don’t see the shared mailbox, contact your IT admin.

Add external presenters

Easily add up to 20 external presenters to your event. External presenters are presenters who are anonymous, outside your org, or don’t use Teams.

When you add an external presenter, they’ll receive a unique join link that will allow them to enter the event without waiting in the lobby. Anonymous presenters won’t need to sign in with a Microsoft account; they can join using the link and type in their name before entering.

To add an external presenter:

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: events app icon on the left side of Teams.

  2. Select Manage.

  3. Select an event.

  4. Select Edit details. Screenshot: edit event details icon

  5. Select Who’s planning the event?.

  6. In Presenters, enter the email addresses of the external presenters you want to add.

  7. Select Save and send invitesScreenshot: save icon .

To edit presenter details, like their name, bio, and how they appear on the event page, open the event details and select Manage presentersScreenshot: manage presenters icon .

You can also add external presenters when creating the event.

Note

External presenters shouldn’t forward their links. They’re able to join using the same link on up to three devices. If a guest hasn’t successfully authenticated when joining the event, they’ll be placed in the lobby. From there, an event organizer or presenter can approve or deny their request to join the event.

Regenerate or copy the external join link

To regenerate or copy the link that external presenters join with:

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: events app icon on the left side of Teams.

  2. Select Manage.

  3. Select an event.

  4. Select People & emails > Presenters.

  5. Next to the presenter you want to create a new link for, select View join link.

  6. Select CopyScreenshot: copy icon to copy the link to your clipboard or ReloadScreenshot: reload icon to regenerate a new one.

Manage event drafts

Until an event is published, it will remain a draft that organizers and co-organizers can access and make multiple edits to without sending invites to attendees.

To access an event draft:

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: events app icon on the left side of Teams.

  2. Select Manage.

  3. Under Drafts, choose the draft you’d like to open.

  4. Select Edit detailsScreenshot: edit event details icon to make changes to event details. Then, select Save changesScreenshot: save icon .

Note

If the event was created in the Teams calendar, editing details will open the calendar event scheduling form. Only events created in the Events app can be edited directly in the app.

Publish an event

After you’ve finalized event details and are ready to invite attendees, publish your event. When you publish an event, invites will be sent to attendees automatically. They’ll be able to view the event details, register, and join the event.

You can still invite attendees after an event is published and modify some event settings. You can’t change the access level or turn registration on or off after the event is published.

To publish an event:

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: events app icon on the left side of Teams.

  2. Select Manage.

  3. Under Drafts, find the event you want to publish.

  4. Select Edit detailsScreenshot: edit event details icon to finalize the event details.

  5. Select Save changesScreenshot: save icon if needed, or BackScreenshot: back icon to return to the main draft.

  6. Turn on the Preview toggle to preview how the event site will look to attendees.

  7. Select Publish eventScreenshot: publish event icon .

After your event is published, you’ll be able to publicize your event.

Duplicate an event

Recreate an event with the same customizations by duplicating it. When you duplicate an event, the event details, added people and groups, and settings will be copied over to a new one. You can then update the name, date, time, and other details as needed.

To duplicate an event:

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: events app icon on the left side of Teams.

  2. Select Manage.

  3. Find the event you’d like to duplicate and select More optionsScreenshot: teams-ellipses-icon > DuplicateScreenshot: copy icon .

Save as a template

Save an event as a template to reuse for similar events in the future without having to build it from scratch each time. Templates carry over all your event settings except for the date and time for you to use again.

To save an event as a template:

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: events app icon on the left side of Teams.

  2. Select Manage.

  3. Select the event you want to reuse.

  4. Select More optionsScreenshot: teams-ellipses-icon > Save as templateScreenshot: save icon .

  5. Add a template name and description so you can identify it later.

  6. Select Save template.

The template will be available when you create a new event, under Your saved templates. Edit, schedule, or delete templates from here.

Cancel an event

To cancel an event created in the Events app:

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: events app icon on the left side of Teams.

  2. Select Manage.

  3. Select the event you want to cancel.

  4. Select More actionsScreenshot: teams-ellipses-icon > CancelScreenshot: cancel event icon .

    Screenshot: Screenshot of cancelling a Teams event .

  5. Select Cancel event.

To cancel events created outside of the Events app, see Cancel a webinar or Cancel a town hall.

Customize event emails in the Microsoft Teams Events app

Customize communications with attendees leading up to your event to keep them informed about important event updates, including cancellations, changes to the date and time, and more.

Event organizers and presenters can edit event emails to change:

  • Sender’s name

  • Email subject

  • Email body

  • When the email is sent*

*Available only for event reminder emails

Important

If you created your event in the Teams calendar, these experiences may look different. For help customizing emails for events scheduled from your Teams calendar, see Manage webinar emails in Microsoft Teams and Manage town hall emails in Microsoft Teams.

Edit event emails

To edit event emails:

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: events app icon on the left side of Teams.

  2. Select Manage.

  3. Select an event.

  4. Select People & emails.

  5. Select Email notifications.

  6. Next to the email you want to change, select Edit.

  7. Make desired changes.

  8. Select Preview to see how the email will appear to attendees.

  9. Select Save.

Some event emails are only available when event registration is turned on.

Turn event emails on or off

Before your event, you can choose to turn event email communications on or off. If you turn off event emails, attendees won’t receive any event emails. Teams doesn’t currently support turning specific event emails on or off.

To turn event emails on or off:

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: events app icon on the left side of Teams.

  2. Select Manage.

  3. Select an event.

  4. Select People & emails.

  5. Select Email notifications.

  6. Turn the Send attendee emails toggle on or off.

Discover events in the Microsoft Teams Events app

Find, track and join events across your org in the Events app in Microsoft Teams. Instead of relying only on calendar invites or email links, the Events app brings everything together in one experience so you can easily explore upcoming events, register, and revisit past sessions.

Using the Discover tab, browse events you’re invited to, find new ones that are open for registration, and stay connected to events you care about, all from within Teams.

Open the Events app

To discover events, first open the Events app in Teams.

To open the Events app:

  1. Select Apps on the left side of Teams.

  2. Search for “Events”.

    Screenshot: A screenshot the search result for Events in Teams apps

  3. Select the Events app to open it.

Tip

If you use the Events app often, consider pinning it to your app bar for quicker access.

Discover events

In the Discover tab, explore new or promoted events. Find and register for events you’re eligible to attend.

To browse and find events relevant to you:

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: events app icon on the left side of Teams.

  2. Select Discover.

  3. Browse available events.

  4. Select an event to view details such as description, timing, and registration options.

  5. Choose Register or Join, if available.

View your events

In addition to discovering new events, track events you’ve registered for or been invited to. You can also rejoin events or view past event recordings, if available. This creates a single place to manage your event activity across Teams.

Tips for finding the right events

  • Check regularly: New events may appear in Discover as they’re published.

  • Look for promoted or featured events: Organizers might highlight important events to make them easier to find.

  • Combine with search: Use the Teams search bar to find specific events by name or keyword.

Excel Live in Microsoft Teams meetings

Excel Live is a collaborative feature in Microsoft Teams where team members can edit and explore Excel documents directly in the Teams meeting window.

Presenting with Excel Live

Use Excel Live to share workbooks with your team. Edit and explore content with others within the meeting window. While you share, you set the pace. Participants can navigate through content on their own and sync with you later.

Screenshot: Screenshot of presenter (sharer) screen during Excel Live session in Teams.

Note

  • You can share Excel workbooks using Teams for web. Mobile presenting isn’t available.
  • You’ll need to have full sharing permissions for a file to present it.
Presenter
  • Present and work together over the same file, with real-time changes visible to everyone in the meeting.
  • Presenter updates to the file, including sorting and filtering, are visible to everyone.
  • Presenter controls aren’t visible to everyone.
Attendee
  • Meeting participants can follow the presenter to automatically view the region of the file being shown. No other action is required.
  • Use zoom controls to optimize readability. Zooming into a file as a participant doesn’t affect others.

Collaborating in Excel Live

Anyone in an Excel Live session can collaborate in shared content. If you’re not presenting, navigate through the shared workbook on your own and join the presenter when you’re ready.

Screenshot: Screenshot of participant (viewer) screen during Excel Live session in Teams.

Note

People who join the meeting from a mobile device can follow along with the presentation and explore content but can’t make edits directly in Teams. If you want to edit an Excel workbook from a mobile device, tap Edit in the meeting window to open it in the Excel app.

Starting an Excel Live session

To start an Excel Live session:

  1. Open Microsoft Teams for desktop or web.

  2. Join an existing meeting or start a new one with your team members.

    Note

    Excel Live is supported for meetings with 25 or fewer invitees.

  3. Select ShareScreenshot: teams-new-share-screen-icon in your meeting controls.

  4. Under Excel Live, choose the Excel workbook you want to share. If you can’t find the Excel workbook you’re looking for, select Browse OneDrive or Browse my computer to see more files.

    Screenshot: Screenshot of share options highlighting Excel files in Teams meeting.

  5. Select Share to give others in your meeting permission to access and edit the workbook.

    Screenshot: Screenshot of permission pop-up when selecting a file to share in Excel Live during Teams meeting.

  • All participants in the meeting are provided with file permissions to edit. Meeting participants retain file permissions to edit even after the meeting ends.

    Note

    External participants who aren’t from your organization won’t have access to the file in the meeting itself. They can access the file by opening it in a browser window. Guest participants who aren’t signed in to a Teams account won’t have access to the file either. However, guests with pre-existing access to the file can open it in a browser window.

Presenting with Excel Live in a meeting or conference room

Meeting/conference room display devices can’t show content shared using Excel Live in a meeting. All participants in the meeting can collaborate in Excel Live from their respective devices.

Recording Excel Live sessions

Excel Live meeting recordings don’t include the interactive workbook shared in the meeting. The audio and video are recorded just as they are in other meetings.

FAQs

I’m not seeing the file that I want to share using Excel Live in a meeting. What do I do? Your file might not be in a modern format, like .xlsx, or your file might not be a Cloud file. Try uploading the file to solve the issue.

After the meeting, will participants have access to files shared through Excel Live during the meeting? Yes. Files shared through Excel Live in a meeting are accessible to the participants even after the meeting ends. To revoke access to a file shared during Excel Live in a meeting, go to the Share and manage access option for the file and remove the participants you don’t want to give continued file access to. You can also stop sharing OneDrive or SharePoint files or folders, or change permissions (microsoft.com).

Can I share a password-protected file using Excel Live in a meeting? No. We don’t support coauthoring in password-protected files.

Why does the meeting show 25 participants when there are fewer than 25 participants in the meeting? The restriction for using Excel Live in a meeting is based on the number of invitees to the meeting, not the number of participants who joined the meeting.

Frequently asked questions about meeting audio recap

What is meeting audio recap?

Teams meeting audio recap is a feature that uses AI to capture and summarize key topics discussed during your Teams meetings with an engaging audio output. It converts the selected meeting transcripts into audio summaries, allowing users to quickly review highlights for multiple meetings, helping them find important information efficiently.

What can meeting audio recap do?

Meeting audio recap enhances productivity and efficiency by providing audio summaries of selected meeting transcriptions, mitigating the need for users to go through entire recaps.

What is meeting audio recap’s intended use?

Meeting users want to quickly recall or recap what happened in meetings without going through each individual meeting recap. Meeting audio recaps help users stay updated on what matters the most and boost productivity.

How was meeting audio recap evaluated? What metrics are used to measure performance?

Meeting audio recap was evaluated through extensive manual and automatic testing on top of Microsoft internal usage. The evaluated metrics were internally defined, grounded (including accuracy, comprehensiveness, inclusion, clarity) and ungrounded (including thought provoking, storytelling, engagement) metrics.

More evaluation was performed over custom datasets for offensive and malicious input and output. In addition, meeting audio recap is continuously evaluated with user online feedback.

What are the limitations of meeting audio recap?

  • Currently, Chinese, variations across English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese, and Spanish are supported as audio output in audio recap scenarios. More languages and locales will be added in the future.
  • Currently, only a maximum of 8 meetings can be summarized in one audio recap.
  • AI-generated content might be missing key information and contain inaccurate content. Users can listen to the meetings’ original recordings or read the transcripts to check for accuracy.

How do I provide feedback on meeting audio recap?

Users can provide feedback directly through the user interface of the Audio recap page by selecting the thumb up/ thumb down button and entering in your feedback.

What content is used to provide audio recap and where is it stored?

To use meeting audio recap, users must enable meeting transcription, which admins can manage with Recording & transcription meeting policies in the Teams admin center. The generated audio recap is exclusively accessible to you and will expire after 60 days.  You can manage your audio recaps in OneDrive, where you have the option to delete any audio recap that is no longer needed. Once an audio recap is deleted from OneDrive, it will no longer be available on your Teams Audio recap listing page.

How does Microsoft use data to provide meeting audio recap?

Customer data isn‘t logged or used for any AI model training or testing.

Audio recap generation uses a GPT model from Open AI through Azure OpenAI Service. Customer data isn’t shared with non-Microsoft parties, including Open AI. Microsoft runs the GPT-based models internally using a dedicated GPT service (Azure OpenAI). This dedicated service runs within the compliance boundaries that are used only for Microsoft 365 and Office 365 services.

Audio recap automatically inherits Microsoft security, compliance, and privacy policies for Microsoft 365 Copilot.

Get started with the Microsoft Teams Events app

Create, discover, and manage events from one place with the Events app in Microsoft Teams, a unified hub that simplifies event creation and maintains a consistent, flexible experience across all event types.

Teams events are designed for structured, large-scale experiences with controlled attendee participation and advanced production capabilities. These work well for:

  • Company-wide updates or executive announcements

  • Internal or external training sessions

  • Customer-facing product launches or demos

  • Webinars or town hall-style presentations

  • Live events requiring moderated Q&A and limited attendee interaction

Flexible event creation and management

Use a unified creation flow to configure event settings based on your goals instead of choosing between fixed event types. Customize audience interaction, registration, scale, and more.

In the Manage tab, organizers can select a published or drafted event to open its central page and manage settings, customization, and communications, as well as provide attendees with event information and resources.

Encourage engagement

Enhanced discoverability and built-in engagement capabilities help increase event attendance and interaction. Share and embed events in SharePoint sites to make them more visible and accessible to attendees.
