Hide your identity in meeting captions and transcripts in Microsoft Teams

When meetings include live captions or transcription, Teams automatically identifies the speaker along with what they say. You can choose to hide your name in live captions, live transcription, and the saved transcription that’s available after the meeting.

Do this before the meeting where you want to speak anonymously.

  1. Select More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft teams More options icon. > SettingsScreenshot: skype-teams-mobile-icon-settings in Teams.
  2. In Accessibility > Captions and transcripts, turn off the Automatically identify me in live captions and live transcripts toggle.

Host an event in Microsoft Teams

When you host an event in Microsoft Teams, you can manage the entire experience, from preparation to live delivery and wrap-up. Organizers and presenters can control what attendees see, share content, engage audiences, and ensure a smooth production flow.

Prepare in the green room

Get ready with other co-organizers and presenters in the green room before starting an event. Practice sharing content, check your audio and video settings, and more. While you prepare in the green room, attendees will wait in the lobby until you start the event.

To use this feature, make someone a presenter and turn it on before the event starts.

To enable the green room for an event you scheduled in the Events app:

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: events app icon on the left side of Teams.

  2. Select Manage.

  3. Select an upcoming event.

  4. Select Edit detailsScreenshot: edit event details icon .

  5. In Set up experience and optionsScreenshot: teams-meeting-options-icon , turn the Enable green room toggle on.

You’ll automatically join the green room when you join the event.

Important

If you created your event in the Teams calendar, this experience may look different. To learn more, see Using the green room in Microsoft Teams.

Join an event

When you join an event before it starts, you’ll first enter the green room. In the green room, you can prepare with other co-organizers and presenters, as well as start the event when you’re ready.

To join a town hall directly in Teams:

  • Select EventsScreenshot: events app icon on the left side of Teams. Select the event you want to join and select JoinScreenshot: teams camera icon .

  • Select Calendar in Teams. Select the event you want to join and select JoinScreenshot: teams camera icon .

Start an event

To start an event:

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: calendar icon in Teams.

  2. Select the event you want to start.

  3. Select Join > Join now.

  4. Prepare with others in the green room.

  5. Select Start meeting and confirm.

When you start the event, recording and transcription will begin automatically.

Add presenters and attendees

After an event starts, add missing presenters or attendees so they can participate and share content.

To add a presenter or attendee who isn’t currently in the event:

  1. Select PeopleScreenshot: teams people icon in your meeting controls.

  2. In the Participants pane, search for the person you want to invite.

  3. Next to the person’s name, select Request as presenter and select Presenter or Attendee from the dropdown menu.

  4. The presenter or attendee will receive a call on their Teams device and will join directly if they accept the request to join.

When you add a presenter or attendee, they’ll join as the role previously assigned to them. If they don’t have a predefined role, they’ll join as attendees.

To make someone a presenter:

  1. Select PeopleScreenshot: teams people icon in the meeting controls.

  2. Hover over an attendee’s name and select More optionsScreenshot: teams-ellipses-icon > Make a presenter.

Manage what attendees see

Ensure smooth event production and elevate attendee experiences by managing what attendees see. Focus on specific people by bringing them on and off the screen, pinning their video feeds, or hiding others from view.

Note

Note: Managing what attendees see isn’t currently available for events optimized for scale. To learn more, see Microsoft event features at scale.

To turn on Manage what attendees see in your event:

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: events app icon on the left side of Teams.

  2. Select Manage.

  3. Select an upcoming event.

  4. Select Edit detailsScreenshot: edit event details icon .

  5. Select Set up experience and optionsScreenshot: teams-meeting-options-icon > All options.

  6. In Production toolsScreenshot: production-tools-icon-1 , turn the Manage what attendees see toggle on.

  7. Select Apply.

Important

If you created your event in the Teams calendar, this experience may look different. To learn more, see Manage what attendees see in Microsoft Teams.

Give control of production tools

Give control of production tools to give people in the meeting control over what is shown on screen for attendees. People with control of production tools can preview changes and queue up presenters before they appear live. They can also start and end the event.

To determine who has control of production tools:

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: events app icon on the left side of Teams.

  2. Select Manage.

  3. Select an upcoming event.

  4. Select Edit detailsScreenshot: edit event details icon .

  5. Select Set up experience and optionsScreenshot: teams-meeting-options-icon > All options.

  6. In Production toolsScreenshot: production-tools-icon-1 > Who has control of production tools, choose who will have control from the dropdown menu.

  7. Select Apply.

Important

If you created your event in the Teams calendar, this experience may look different. To learn more, see Control production tools in Microsoft Teams.

Bring presenters on and off screen

Before and during an event, choose which presenters to bring on and off screen. When a presenter is on screen, attendees will be able to hear them speak and see their videos and shared content.

To learn more about bringing presenters on and off screen, see Manage what attendees see in Microsoft Teams.

Bring attendees on and off screen

Engage with your audience in events by bringing attendees on screen when they raise their hands. When you bring an attendee on screen, they’ll have access to turn on their mic and camera. If they do, they’ll be seen and heard by everyone at the event.

To learn more about bringing attendees on and off screen, see Manage what attendees see in Microsoft Teams.

Present content

When you organize an event, designate presenters to bring on screen to share content during the event. To make someone a presenter, change their role when you schedule an event.

Present with CVI

Join and present in Teams events using your own Video Teleconferencing (VTC) devices, even if they’re not Teams Rooms devices. Organizers can share CVI join codes directly from the town hall’s share event dialog with presenters.

To learn more, see Manage and set up Cloud Video Interop for Microsoft Teams.

Share content using RTMP-In

During an event, organizers and presenters can use an external encoder and enable RTMP-in to integrate different types of media into the event. Experience higher-quality screen sharing, video production, and more.

Learn more about using RTMP-in during your event here.

Start Q&A

For more engagement between attendees and presenters before and during an event, turn on Q&A. Attendees can post and reply to questions while they wait for the event to start and while they’re in it. To learn more, see Q&A in Microsoft Teams.

Create a poll

Get real-time feedback from your audience by creating a poll during an event. To create a poll in an event, you must add the Polls app before the event starts. After events that were optimized for large audiences, poll data will remain accessible for up to 36 hours after the event ends.

To learn more, see Create a poll in Microsoft Teams.

Note

Polls are available in events with up to 20k attendees. To learn more about hosting large events in Teams, contact your IT admin. Word Cloud Polls aren’t supported in events optimized for large audiences.

Preview an event as an attendee

Organizers, co-organizers, and presenters can preview an event as an attendee to monitor the experience from the audience’s point of view.

To preview as an attendee, join the event from a different entry point than you joined as organizer, co-organizer, or presenter. For example, if you originally joined on Teams for desktop, preview as an attendee from the web or your mobile device.

Note

At least one organizer, co-organizer, or presenter must join the event before previewing as an attendee is available. The attendance report won’t reflect organizers, co-organizers, or presenters previewing as attendees. Some event experiences, such as Q&A, aren’t currently supported when previewing as an attendee.

Leave, restart, or end an event

Leave an event

To leave an event, select Leave in the corner of your Teams window. This won’t end the event for everyone.

Restart an event

Restarting an event might be a way to resolve technical issues, including the inability for attendees to join, widespread audio or video issues, broken content, or if the event is unresponsive. Organizers, producers, and presenters who were assigned production capabilities can restart a town hall.

To restart an event:

  1. Select the dropdown arrow next to Leave in the corner of your Teams window.

  2. Select Restart event.

After an event restarts, attendees will see a message indicating the event is restarting and return to the join screen, where they can rejoin. Presenters and producers will join the green room, where they can start the event again. There will also be separate event recordings and attendance reports for each event segment. Q&A and event chat will continue seamlessly; all communications will be preserved before and after the restart.

End an event

To end an event, select End event in the event controls. This will end the event for everyone and stop the recording.

Join a Teams meeting by phone

Connect to a Microsoft Teams meeting by dialing in or out to a phone number. Dial in as a participant, presenter, or organizer. Dial out to your phone number or another person’s phone number. Once in the meeting, use dual-tone multiple-frequency (DTMF) commands to manage the audio conferencing experience.

Note

In Teams, conference call leaders are called presenters. The meeting organizer is automatically joined as the leader.

Dial in to a Teams meeting by phone

Join a Teams meeting by dialing one of the meeting’s dial-in numbers. Dial-in numbers are available in the invite for the meeting.

Screenshot: Screenshot showing where you can call into a Teams meeting.

The Find a local number link will list all the phone numbers across multiple countries and regions that you can use to join the meeting.

As soon as you connect to the call, use DTMF commands to mute your line or hear a list of people on the call. Here are the typical DTMF commands available during a conference call:

  • *1
    • Privately play a description of the available DTMF commands.
  • *3
    • Privately play the name of each participant in the audio conference.
  • *4
    • Mute audience or return mute control to participants. Important: Turning off audience muting doesn’t unmute individual participants. When you turn off audience muting, participants hear a message explaining how to unmute themselves.
  • *5
    • Raise or lower your hand.
  • *6
    • Mute or unmute your microphone.
  • *7
    • Lock or unlock the audio conference.
  • *8
    • Admit all participants currently in the lobby to the audio conference. After you use this command, anyone in the lobby will be let into the meeting.
  • *9
    • Turn announcements on or off for participants joining and leaving the call. Announcements are heard by everyone in the meeting.
  • *21
    • Admit all attendees waiting in the lobby.
  • *22
    • Mute everyone except the organizer.
  • *23
    • Turn enter/exit announcements on or off.

Call in to a Teams meeting

In Microsoft Teams, calling into a meeting gives participants a way to join the audio portion of a meeting by phone. This is useful when someone can’t use a computer for audio.

People who call in can hear and speak during the meeting through their mobile or landline phones. They can join on a second device to view shared content.

To call into a meeting with your phone number:

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: Teams Calendar tab icon in Teams.
  2. Select a meeting.
  3. Select Join.
  4. Select more join options on the pre-join screen.
  5. Select Call me.
  6. Enter the phone number you’d like the meeting to call and select Call me.
  7. Say “Ok” or press 1 to join the meeting.
  8. Hang up or select Disconnect in the meeting window to end the call.

To call another person to join by phone during a meeting:

  1. Select PeopleScreenshot: People or Show Participants button in your meeting controls.
  2. Add the phone number in Invite someone or dial a number.
  3. Select Add phone.
  4. The person will need to say “Ok” or press 1 to join.
  5. Hang up or select Disconnect in the meeting window to end the call.

Manage event registration in the Microsoft Teams Events app

Manage event registration in Microsoft Teams to determine how attendees sign up and participate in your event. Turn registration on or off, customize the registration form, review and manage registration requests, and manage your event waitlist to help ensure a smooth registration experience for attendees.

Important

If you created your event in the Teams calendar, these experiences may look different. For help managing registration for events scheduled from your Teams calendar, see Manage webinar registration.

Turn registration on or off

While scheduling your event, you can choose to turn registration on or off.

To turn registration on or off:

  1. Create an event in the Events app.

  2. In Who can attend, turn on the Turn on registration? toggle.

After you save your event, you won’t be able to change this setting.

Customize registration

Customize the registration experience for your event by editing the registration form, turning on manual registration approval and the event waitlist, and limiting registration start and end times.

Important

To modify registration, registration must have been turned on before you first saved the event while scheduling it.

Edit the registration form

Learn more about your attendees by adding custom fields to the registration form. The form will automatically ask attendees for their first and last names and emails, as well as include Microsoft consent fields.

To customize an event registration form:

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: Events app icon in the Teams left navigation sidebar on the left side of Teams.

  2. Select Manage.

  3. Find the event you want to customize the registration form for and select EditScreenshot: edit event details icon .

  4. Select Who can attend.

  5. In the registration settings, select Customize.

    Screenshot: Screenshot of customization option in Teams event registration

  6. Select Add field.

  7. Choose a field or select Custom question to create one.

  8. Choose whether the field is required.

  9. Use the arrows to move the field above or below others on the form.

  10. Select Save.

  11. Select Save changesScreenshot: save icon .

To customize a registration form for an event created in the Teams calendar, see Manage webinar registration in Microsoft Teams.

Turn on manual approval

Keep your event secure by requiring manual approval for each attendee’s registration.

To turn on manual approval:

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: Events app icon in the Teams left navigation sidebar on the left side of Teams.

  2. Select Manage.

  3. Find the event you want to customize the registration form for and select EditScreenshot: edit event details icon .

  4. Select Who can attend.

  5. Under Set up registration, check the Require manual approval of registrations box.

  6. Select Save changesScreenshot: save icon .

Manage registration requests

To manage event registration requests:

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: Events app icon in the Teams left navigation sidebar on the left side of Teams.

  2. Select Manage.

  3. Under Published, select an event.

  4. Select People & emails.

  5. Select Attendees.

  6. Next to Status, select Pending approval.

  7. Select View form next to someone’s name to view their registration form.

  8. To manage someone’s request individually, select Decline or Approve next to their name.

  9. To manage requests in bulk, check the boxes next to multiple names or check the box next to Name. Then, select Decline (#) or Approve (#) at the top of the list.

To turn on manual approval or manage registration requests for an event created in the Teams calendar, see Manage webinar registration in Microsoft Teams.

Limit registration start and end times

To set a specific timeframe for attendee registration:

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: Events app icon in the Teams left navigation sidebar on the left side of Teams.

  2. Select Manage.

  3. Find the event you want to customize the registration form for and select EditScreenshot: edit event details icon .

  4. Select Who can attend.

  5. Under Set up registration, check the Limit registration start and end time box.

  6. Set the registration start and end times.

  7. Select Save changesScreenshot: save icon .

To manage registration for an event created in the Teams calendar, see Manage webinar registration in Microsoft Teams.

Turn on event waitlist

Choose to start a waitlist after your event’s capacity is filled. If registered attendees cancel their registrations, waitlisted attendees will have the chance to register. The waitlist capacity will match the registration capacity.

To turn on the event waitlist:

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: Events app icon in the Teams left navigation sidebar on the left side of Teams.

  2. Select Manage.

  3. Find the event you want to turn on the waitlist in and select EditScreenshot: edit event details icon .

  4. Select Who can attend.

  5. Under Set up registration, check the Turn on waitlist box.

  6. Select Save changesScreenshot: save icon .

Manage event waitlist

If your event is full, remove a registered attendee or increase the event capacity to admit someone from the waitlist. People will be moved from the waitlist on a first-come, first-serve basis.

To manage an event’s waitlist:

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: Events app icon in the Teams left navigation sidebar on the left side of Teams.

  2. Select Manage.

  3. Select an event.

  4. Select People & emails.

  5. Select Attendees.

  6. Next to Status, select Waitlisted.

To manage the waitlist for an event created in the Teams calendar, see Manage webinar registration in Microsoft Teams.

View registration details

Look at how many people registered for your event, viewed the registration page, canceled their registrations, and more.

To view event registration details:

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: Events app icon in the Teams left navigation sidebar on the left side of Teams.

  2. Select Manage.

  3. Select an event.

  4. Select Insights.

To download this information for review later, select DownloadScreenshot: Teams download arrow icon .

Manage Microsoft Teams events in shared mailbox and delegate scenarios

When events are created using a shared mailbox or on behalf of another person through delegation, available event management actions depend on your role.

Shared mailbox scenarios

In shared mailbox scenarios, permissions depend on whether you’re the organizer, a co-organizer, or a mailbox member.

To manage and run an event, access reports, or publish recordings, you must be the organizer or an explicitly assigned co-organizer. Shared mailbox members who aren’t added as co-organizers have limited access and can only edit scheduling details.

Delegate scenarios

Manage upcoming events in the Microsoft Teams Events app

Manage upcoming and past events in one place with the Microsoft Teams Events app. Customize and edit upcoming event details, engage in the event Q&A, review RSVP statuses, and view past event insights and recordings.

Important

If you created your event in the Teams calendar, these experiences may look different. For help managing events scheduled from your Teams calendar, see Get started with Microsoft Teams webinars and Get started with town hall in Microsoft Teams.

Edit event details

Make changes to upcoming event details and branding to tailor the event to your audience. If the event is already published, you won’t be able to change who has access to the event or turn registration on or off.

To edit event details:

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: events app icon on the left side of Teams.

  2. Select Manage.

  3. Find the event you want to edit and select EditScreenshot: edit event details icon .

  4. Make changes to event details.

  5. Select Save changesScreenshot: save icon .

Customize event branding

Add a banner, logo, or theme color to align the event with your org’s branding.

To customize event branding:

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: events app icon on the left side of Teams.

  2. Select Manage.

  3. Select an event.

  4. On the existing cover image, select EditScreenshot: edit-image-icon-1 .

    • Under Cover image, select Edit imageScreenshot: edit-image-icon-1 to upload a new cover image. Zoom in or out of the image using the slide bar and drag the image into position. Select Save.

    • Under Logo, select UploadScreenshot: upload-icon-1 to upload an image of your org’s logo.

    • Under Theme color, choose a color that best represents your brand. Event elements, such as the Join button, icon colors, and more will be presented in that color.

  5. Select Save.

Chat with an event group

Start a chat with event organizers and presenters only to plan and prepare for an upcoming event. This chat will remain available after the event ends. Event participants won’t have access to this chat.

To chat with an event group:

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: events app icon on the left side of Teams.

  2. Select Manage.

  3. On the event you want to chat in, select More optionsScreenshot: teams-ellipses-icon > Chat with event group.

Chat with participants

Start a conversation with event participants leading up to an event to communicate updates, requirements, and more. Chatting before an event isn’t available for events optimized for a large audience or for events that require registration.

To chat with event participants:

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: events app icon on the left side of Teams.

  2. Select Manage.

  3. On the event you want to chat in, select More optionsScreenshot: teams-ellipses-icon > Chat with participants.

Manage Q&A

Encourage participation and engagement leading up to an event with Q&A. Share updates, start discussions, and post questions for attendees. Give attendees permission to post their own questions and comments, as well as engage with others using upvotes and reactions.

Create a post

To post in an event’s Q&A:

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: events app icon on the left side of Teams.

  2. Select Manage.

  3. Under Published, select an event.

  4. In Overview > Q&A, select Share updates or start a discussionScreenshot: chat-icon or Ask a questionScreenshot: qa-icon-1 .

  5. Create your post.

  6. Select Post.

Change Q&A settings

Modify Q&A settings to adjust attendee access to Q&A. Choose whether they can create posts, comment, upvote and react, or post and comment anonymously. You can also change organizer permissions to moderate posts.

To change Q&A settings:

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: events app icon on the left side of Teams.

  2. Select Manage.

  3. Under Published, select an event.

  4. In Overview > Q&A, select Q&A settingsScreenshot: settings-icon-1 .

  5. Adjust the setting toggles.

  6. Select Save.

View event RSVPs

To view RSVPs to your event:

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: events app icon on the left side of Teams.

  2. Select Manage.

  3. Under Published, select an event.

  4. Select People & emails.

  5. Select Attendees.

  6. Look at the Status column to view RSVP statuses.

Microsoft Teams event features at scale

When you schedule a Microsoft Teams event, available attendee features vary depending on the event capacity you choose and your org’s licensing. Smaller events support the most interactive experiences, while larger events prioritize stability and scalability for large audiences.

Event feature availability by attendee capacity

The following table shows which interactive features are available at different event capacity ranges:

  • Q&A
    • Up to 1,000 attendees (base license): ✅
    • 1,001 to 3,000 attendees (base license): ✅
    • 3,001 to 10,000 attendees (base license): ✅
    • 1,001-20,000 attendees (with attendee packs): ✅
    • 20,001-100,000 attendees (with attendee packs): ✅
  • Polls
    • Up to 1,000 attendees (base license): ✅
    • 1,001 to 3,000 attendees (base license): ✅
    • 3,001 to 10,000 attendees (base license): ❌
    • 1,001-20,000 attendees (with attendee packs): ✅
    • 20,001-100,000 attendees (with attendee packs): ❌
  • Chat
    • Up to 1,000 attendees (base license): ✅
    • 1,001 to 3,000 attendees (base license): ✅
    • 3,001 to 10,000 attendees (base license): ❌
    • 1,001-20,000 attendees (with attendee packs): ✅
    • 20,001-100,000 attendees (with attendee packs): ❌
  • Raised hands
    • Up to 1,000 attendees (base license): ✅
    • 1,001 to 3,000 attendees (base license): ✅
    • 3,001 to 10,000 attendees (base license): ❌
    • 1,001-20,000 attendees (with attendee packs): ✅
    • 20,001-100,000 attendees (with attendee packs): ❌
  • Live reactions
    • Up to 1,000 attendees (base license): ✅
    • 1,001 to 3,000 attendees (base license): ✅
    • 3,001 to 10,000 attendees (base license): ❌
    • 1,001-20,000 attendees (with attendee packs): ✅
    • 20,001-100,000 attendees (with attendee packs): ❌
  • Attendee mic
    • Up to 1,000 attendees (base license): ✅
    • 1,001 to 3,000 attendees (base license): ❌
    • 3,001 to 10,000 attendees (base license): ❌
    • 1,001-20,000 attendees (with attendee packs): ❌
    • 20,001-100,000 attendees (with attendee packs): ❌
  • Attendee camera
    • Up to 1,000 attendees (base license): ✅
    • 1,001 to 3,000 attendees (base license): ❌
    • 3,001 to 10,000 attendees (base license): ❌
    • 1,001-20,000 attendees (with attendee packs): ❌
    • 20,001-100,000 attendees (with attendee packs): ❌

Optimize for large audiences

When you optimize an event for large audiences, some features and settings will be configured or limited to support high-scale delivery. Attendee mics and cameras will be turned off. They’ll watch at a slight delay and can pause and rewind the live video.

Events with over 1k capacity will be optimized for scale automatically. Events with 1k capacity can be optimized for scale in your event details.

To optimize an event created in the Teams Events app for scale:

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: events app icon on the left side of Teams.

  2. Select Manage.

  3. Select the event you want to optimize for scale.

  4. Select Edit detailsScreenshot: edit event details icon .

  5. Select Set up experience and optionsScreenshot: teams-meeting-options-icon .

  6. Turn on the Optimize for large audience toggle.

Some Attendee participation features will be unavailable when this toggle is turned on.

Feature availability

Supported features in events optimized for scale:

  • Polls (up to 20k capacity*)

  • Streaming chat (up to 20k capacity*)

  • Raised hands (up to 20k capacity*)

  • Live reactions (up to 20k capacity*)

  • Q&A (up to 100k capacity*)

  • Ultra Low Latency (ULL)*

Unsupported features in events optimized for scale:

  • Attendee mics/cameras

  • Regular interactive chat (replies, reactions, etc.)

  • Breakout rooms

  • PowerPoint Live

*Contact your IT admin to learn more about feature availability with Teams attendee packs.

Chat at scale

Chat experiences vary depending on event capacity.

For events up to 1k attendees:

  • Attendees can reply, react, attach files, and use formatting options in chat.

  • Organizers can choose to open the event chat before the event starts, during the event only, or turn it off completely.

  • Access to chat history will continue after the event ends unless it’s deleted earlier due to admin retention policies.

For events between 1k-20k attendees, or events optimized for scale:

  • Chat is a streaming experience that is only available during the event unless the organizer turns chat off.

  • Attendees can send and view messages but won’t have engagement capabilities (replies, reactions, etc.).

  • Chat history won’t be accessible after the event ends.

Publicize an event in the Microsoft Team Events app

Build excitement and an audience for a Microsoft Teams event after you create it by publishing and sharing the event details and site. After you publish an event, invites will be sent to attendees automatically. You’ll also generate an active event link that can be shared via social media, websites, email, and chat.

Important

If you created your event in the Teams calendar, these experiences may look different. For help publicizing events scheduled from your Teams calendar, see Publicize a webinar in Microsoft Teams and Schedule a town hall in Microsoft Teams.

Publish an event

After you publish an event, attendees will be invited automatically and be able to view the event details, register, and join the event. You can still invite attendees after an event is published and modify some event settings. You can’t change the access level or turn registration on or off after the event is published.

After your event is published, you’ll see a screen with a view of your event card and options to publicize your event:

Screenshot: Screenshot of a confirmation message after publishing a Teams event

  • Turn on the Allow attendees to discover the event toggle to surface your event in the Events app Discover feed. This allows attendees to see the event in their Discover feeds and maximizes the reach of your event.

  • Select Copy join detailsScreenshot: copy-join-details-icon-1 to copy the meeting join link, meeting ID and passcode, and meeting options link to your clipboard.

  • Select Copy event page linkScreenshot: copy-event-link-icon to copy the URL of your meeting page to your clipboard.

  • Select Copy embed codeScreenshot: embed-icon-1 to copy the embed code to your clipboard.

Promote an event

Build an audience for events by surfacing them in the Events app Discover feed. This is beneficial for public events where there is no restriction on attendance, like social or volunteering events. Share links to various event assets or embed the event into SharePoint or other Microsoft 365 sites. Shareable event assets include the join details and event page link.

Make your event discoverable

Increase awareness around your event without directly sharing the event link or details by making it discoverable in the Events app Discover feed.

For public and in-org events, people can find your event there, view its details, and register or add it to their calendars if registration isn’t required.

To surface your event in the Events app Discover feed:

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: events app icon on the left side of Teams.

  2. Select Manage.

  3. Under Published, select the event you want to share event join details for.

  4. Select ShareScreenshot: share icon .

  5. Turn on the Allow attendees to discover the event toggle.

You can also turn on the Allow attendees to discover the event toggle when you publish the event.

Note

For events accessible to specific people or groups only, only invited people will see the event in their Discover feeds, regardless of whether the Allow attendees to discover the event toggle is turned on. Organizers, co-organizers, presenters, and invited attendees will always see the event details in their Discover feeds, regardless of whether the Allow attendees to discover the event toggle is turned on.

Share event join details

Event join details include the meeting join link, meeting ID and passcode, and meeting options link.

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: events app icon on the left side of Teams.

  2. Select Manage.

  3. Under Published, select the event you want to share event join details for.

  4. Select ShareScreenshot: share icon .

  5. Select Copy join detailsScreenshot: copy-event-link-icon .

Share an event page link

The event page link is a URL that can be shared anywhere and will allow anyone within your event access level to view the event page and details.

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: events app icon on the left side of Teams.

  2. Select Manage.

  3. Under Published, select the event you want to share an event page link to.

  4. Select ShareScreenshot: share icon .

  5. Select Copy event page linkScreenshot: copy-event-link-icon .

Embed an event

Embed an event to give attendees a single place to stream the event live, engage, and later watch the event recording. To embed an event, the event access settings must have been set to Your organization or Public before the event was published.

  1. Select EventsScreenshot: events app icon on the left side of Teams.

Use CART captions in a Microsoft Teams meeting (human generated captions)

Communication access real-time translation (CART) is a service in which a trained CART captioner listens to the speech and instantaneously translates all speech to text. The CART captioner uses a special phonetic keyboard or stenography methods to produce an accurate translation that is then broadcast to the recipients on a screen, laptop, or other device. CART is also sometimes called open captioning, real-time stenography, or real-time captioning.

As a meeting organizer, you can set up and offer CART captioning to your audience instead of the Microsoft Teams built-in live captions that are automatically generated.

As a CART captioner, you’ll need a CART caption link from the meeting organizer and a CART captioning solution or software to connect to and provide CART captions in a Microsoft Teams meeting.

Note

The CART software you use needs to connect through the Microsoft Teams CART Captions API. For information on the APIs, go to Meeting apps API references.

Tip

To learn how to use the Microsoft Teams built-in live captions, refer to Use live captions in a Teams meeting.

Set up CART captioning as meeting organizer

As the meeting organizer, you need to create and send a CART caption link to the CART captioner. They’ll then use the link to connect their CART system or software to the Microsoft Teams meeting.

While you can set up CART captioning during a meeting, we recommend doing this before the meeting so that the captioner has time to troubleshoot issues that might come up.

To set up CART captions for a meeting:

  • New calendar
  • Classic calendar

  1. Select CalendarScreenshot: teams-calendar-tab-icon in Teams.

  2. Double-click a meeting.

  3. Make sure to invite the CART captioner to the meeting in the Invite required attendees field.

  4. Select OptionsScreenshot: skype-teams-mobile-icon-settings .

  5. In AccessibilityScreenshot: teams-accessibility , turn on the Provide CART captions toggle.

  6. Select Apply.

  7. Reopen meeting options.

  8. Under AccessibilityScreenshot: teams-accessibility > Provide CART captions, select Copy linkScreenshot: teams-insert-link-button-icon .

    Screenshot: Copy cart captions link

  9. Paste the link to an email message and send it to the CART captioner to enter into their captioning software.

  10. Connect with the CART captioner before the meeting to make sure everything is set up correctly.

  11. Select CalendarScreenshot: teams-calendar-tab-icon in Teams.

  12. Double-click a meeting.

  13. Make sure to invite the CART captioner to the meeting in the Invite required attendees field.

  14. In the meeting options, hold down the Ctrl key and select Meeting options.

  15. In AccessibilityScreenshot: teams-accessibility , turn on the Provide CART captions toggle.

  16. Select Save.

  17. Close and reopen meeting options.

  18. Under AccessibilityScreenshot: teams-accessibility > Provide CART captions, select Copy linkScreenshot: teams-insert-link-button-icon .

    Screenshot: Copy cart captions link

  19. Paste the link to an email message and send it to the CART captioner to enter into their captioning software.

  20. Connect with the CART captioner before the meeting to make sure everything is set up correctly.

Turn CART captions on and off

If CART is enabled, captions display by default when you turn on captioning, but you can also toggle to the auto-generated captions if you prefer.

  • To use CART, go to your meeting controls and select More actionsScreenshot: More > Turn on live captions. CART captions display by default.
  • To use auto-generated captions, go to the overflow menu in the caption area and select your language.

Get the most out of your captions

To make sure your live captions are as accurate as possible, try to follow these best practices:

  • Speak clearly, slowly, and directly into the mic. As your distance from the mic increases, captions can become less accurate.
  • Avoid locations with background noise.
  • Avoid having multiple people speak at the same time.
  • Use the highest-quality Teams-certified equipment available to you.

Note

Obscenities are obscured by asterisks.

Welcome to Copilot in Microsoft Teams

Copilot in Microsoft Teams enhances collaboration and helps you get the most out of your Teams chats and meetings. Quickly recap, identify follow-up tasks, create agendas, and ask questions for more effective and focused meetings. Summarize key takeaways, see what you’ve missed, and pinpoint key people of interest in chat threads you were added to. All without breaking the flow of discussion.

Copilot in Teams uses your Teams chat and meeting content to generate insights and actionable suggestions alongside your most important Teams touch points.

Important

Copilot in Teams is available on Windows, Mac, web, Android, and iOS. You must have a Microsoft 365 and a Microsoft 365 Copilot license in order to access Copilot in Teams.

Use Copilot in Teams meetings and calls

Copilot in Teams meetings and calls helps you capture action items, different perspectives by topic, or unresolved questions. You can even ask Copilot to give you a response as a table, generating a markdown table that’s ready for you to copy and share. By processing the meeting transcript, it will generate responses to prompts such as:

  • What questions are unresolved in this meeting?
  • What opinions did team members have about this campaign?
  • Create a table of pros and cons for this campaign.

Copilot is available in the following meetings and calls:

  • One-on-one and group calls
  • Single meetings or scheduled private meetings
  • Instances or occurrences of meetings in a series
  • Channel meetings
  • Meet Now
Requirements for Copilot in meetings
  • Turn on transcription or recording. To use Copilot without recording or transcription, see Use Copilot without recording. All participants see a notification that the meeting is being transcribed.
  • Have enough meeting time where participants have been speaking. If there isn’t enough transcribed speech in the meeting yet, Copilot will state that it needs more information before responding to prompts.
  • Ensure the meeting was created by someone within your organization. If a meeting was created by an external participant, Copilot won’t be available in that meeting. If external participants are invited but not the meeting organizer, Copilot will still be available in the meeting.
Requirements for Copilot in calls
  • Turn on transcription or recording, and transcription for one-on-one calls. For VOIP callers, all participants see a notification that the call is being transcribed. For PSTN callers, all participants will hear an announcement that the call is being recorded.
  • Any additional caller added to an existing one-on-one call will not be able to use Copilot.
Access Copilot during a meeting or call
  1. During a meeting or call, select Copilot from the meeting controls. If transcription isn’t already turned on, you’ll be asked to turn it on.
  2. Copilot will appear in a panel on the right side of the meeting window. Select More prompts or type in your own prompt into the compose box. Copilot will process content from the meeting transcript to generate a response.
  3. If you’re at least five minutes late to a meeting that has been recorded or transcribed, Copilot will ask if you would like a summary of the meeting so far.
  4. When a meeting is ten minutes away from ending, Copilot will ask if you would like notes and action items to help end the meeting.
Access Copilot after a call

Once the call has ended, go to Calls Screenshot: Calls button on the left side of Teams. From there, go to your Teams call history, select Ask about this call and open Copilot.

Access Copilot after a meeting

Once the meeting has ended, select the meeting in your Teams Calendar. From there, select the Recap tab in your meeting details.

For more scenarios on how to use Copilot in Teams meetings, see Get started with Copilot in Microsoft Teams meetings.

Use Copilot in Teams chats

Copilot empowers you to ask questions about your chat conversations in Teams. You can use Copilot to quickly review the main points, action items, and decisions from your chats, without having to scroll through long threads. You can also choose to view highlights from the past 1, 7, or 30 days of conversation.

Note

Copilot in Teams chat only uses data available in the chat thread you have open.

Copilot is available in the following chats and only references the meeting chat, not the meeting transcript:

  • One-on-one and group chats
  • Single meeting chats or scheduled private meeting chats
  • Meet Now chats

To access Copilot in Teams chats:

  1. Select a chat in Teams, then select Copilot in the upper-right corner.
  2. A pane will open to the right of the chat where you’ll find introductory information about using Copilot in chat, and a compose box to ask a question about the chat.
  3. Besides answering questions and summarizing the conversation, select More prompts below the compose box to guide you and quickly pull out the details you need.
  4. In responses from Copilot, you will see citations to the relevant information in the chat thread. Selecting a citation will take you to the referenced message in the chat thread to the left.
  5. Only you can see your conversations with Copilot, but if you’d like to share the response with someone else, select Copy at the top right of the individual response to copy the text. Then, paste it into another chat, channel conversation, or anywhere else.
  6. To close Copilot in chat, select Copilot again or the X button at the top right of the pane.
Suggested actions in chat

Suggested actions appear in Teams chat and, when selected, will open Copilot to the right of the chat. For example, when returning to a chat, if there are eight or more unread messages, you might see a clickable suggestion “Summarize what I’ve missed.” Select the suggestion to open Copilot and generate a chat summary.

For more scenarios on how to use Copilot for chat, see Get started with Copilot in Microsoft Teams chat.

Use Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams and Teams mobile

Microsoft 365 Copilot is a cross-app chat experience in Teams that helps you get things done in whole new ways using the power of AI. Interact with Copilot like a contact in Teams chat. Use natural language to give Copilot instructions—the more details you add, the better the outcome. And you can improve on results by refining your instructions and iterating. Ask for a summary of the things you need to catch up on, including your files, messages, and people. Copilot can also help you find and use info that’s buried in documents or lost in conversations. And together you can create content with all of it.

Here are some things you can try:

  • What were the key takeaways from [a meeting]?
  • Draft an outline for a presentation about…
  • When’s my next meeting with [a person]?

Note

Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams can’t reference information from the following file type(s): PDFs.

When you open Copilot at the top of Chat in Teams, you will be presented with some suggested prompts to get you started. Use Copilot to:

Summarize

  • List out key points from [a file]
  • Recap your last meeting
  • Summarize unread emails from [this person]

Create

  • Create an FAQ based on [a file]
  • Write an intro to [an email]
  • Suggest 5 compelling titles for [a file]

Ask

  • What’s my next meeting?
  • Who am I meeting with tomorrow?
  • Where was I mentioned by [a person]?

Some suggested prompts require you to refer to files or other data sources, which are indicated by blue text. Copilot will suggest a list of items you can choose from. To select something not on the list, type in the reference after the slash “/” in the compose box and select from the newly generated options.

Allow some time for Copilot to provide a response. After Copilot provides a response, ask clarifying questions, provide additional information, refine the output, or type another question that continues the conversation for up to 20 queries.

Select New chat at the upper-right of the chat window to restart the conversation context with a new query and suggested prompts. Your previous chat history with Copilot will still be visible.

For more scenarios in Teams, see Get started with Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat in Teams.

Answer a call with the keyboard in Microsoft Teams

Any time you receive a call in Microsoft Teams, you’ll hear a ringtone. If you’re busy working in a different app, press Alt+Tab to refocus on Teams (or Command+Tab if you’re working on a Mac). If you’re actively working in Teams, you’re just one keystroke away from answering or declining your call. Here’s what to do.

For Windows:

  • If you’re working in the desktop app, press Alt+R to answer a call or Alt+Shift+R to decline it.
  • For those of you working in the web app on Windows, press Ctrl+Alt+R to answer a call and Ctrl+Alt+Shift+R to decline.

For Mac:

  • To answer a call in the desktop app, press Ctrl+R. To decline a call from the desktop app, press Ctrl+Shift+R.
  • If you’re working in the web app, press Ctrl+Command+R to answer a call and Ctrl+Command+Shift+R to decline.

Catch up with and manage badge count activity in Microsoft Teams

When a red circle with a number appears on your Teams taskbar icon, it means you have unread or unseen activity in your chats and teams. This is called a badge count, and it can help you stay on top of your most important conversations and activities.

This article explains where the badge numbers on the taskbar and app icons come from, how they’re calculated, and how you can clear or manage them.

What does the badge count represent?

The badge count number displayed on the Teams taskbar icon is a sum of counts from the Chat , Teams , and Activity apps.

Breakdown by app

  • Chat and Teams :

    • Adds +1 for every unmuted one-on-one chat, group chat, or meeting chat.
    • Chats that are muted don’t contribute to the badge count.
    • The count clears when the chat is opened or marked as read.
    • Adds +1 for each channel with an unread personal @mention or an unread tag @mention in a chat or channel.
    • Adds +1 for each unread followed thread.
    • The count clears when the channel is opened or the @mention is read.

If you have Chat and Teams separated, Chat will count items from chats and Teams will count items from channels.

  • Quick views, at the top of the chat and channels list, will show a purple number indicating the items within contributing to the count.

  • Collapsed sections will show a purple number indicating the items within contributing to the count.

  • Activity :

    • Shows the number of new activity items since your last visit.
    • The number clears when you navigate to the activity app.

How to clear the badge count

You can clear the badge count in several ways:

  1. Read the messages.

    • Open unread chats or channels to clear their respective counts.

    • Mentions can be cleared by:

      • Opening the channel directly.

      • Navigating to the Mentions or Tag mentions view at the top of the chat list and reading all mentions.

        Tip

        Use the filters at the top of your list to easily find the items included in your badge count.

  2. Mark all as read.

    • At the top of the chat or channel list, select More options > Mark all as read.
    • This clears all unread indicators and resets the badge count.

Change settings in Microsoft Teams

Modify your Teams settings directly in the desktop or mobile app. Update your region, language, time and date, and decide if you want Teams to sync automatically with your operating system. Change your profile picture, set your status, or try out different light themes to make your account more personal. You can also switch up your call ringtone, set up an Out of Office schedule, and much more.

Change Teams settings

By default, Teams reflects the same date and time format as your device’s language, date, and time settings. For example, if your device’s display language is set to English (United States), the date and time in Teams will display the regional format used in the United States.

Change the default setting by following the steps below:

Change your language and regional settings in Teams

When you update your language and regional settings in your operating system, you have the option to have Teams reflect those changes.

To turn Follow OS settings on or off:

  1. In Teams, go to Settings and moreScreenshot: Teams settings and more icon. > SettingsScreenshot: Settings button > General.
  2. Under Language and regional formats, use the toggle next to Follow OS settings to turn this setting on or off. Turn it off to manually set your App language, Date format, and Time format.
Change your language settings in Windows

  1. Open System settings on your Windows device.

  2. Select Time & language.

  3. Under Language & region > Windows display language, choose the language you want to use from the dropdown menu.

    Note

    To install a new language to use, select Add a language, choose the language you want to install, and select Next > Install.

  4. For more language settings, select More optionsScreenshot: Ellipsis icon> Language options next to your language.

    Screenshot: language screenshot one version two.png

To set your region in Windows:

  1. Open Settings on your Windows device.

  2. Select Time & language.

  3. Under Region, select your region from the Country or region dropdown menu.

    Screenshot: Regional settings on a Windows device.

  4. Keep your Regional format set to Recommended to sync your regional date and time with other apps, or choose another setting from the dropdown menu.

To change your region on MacOS:

  1. Open System Settings on your MacOS device.

  2. Select General > Language & Region.

  3. Select the Region dropdown menu and choose your region.

    Screenshot: Settings to change your region on MacOS

  4. Confirm your regional change.

Change your time zone

When you change your time zone in your device’s settings, Teams will reflect those changes unless you’ve turned this setting off, see above. You can also enable location permissions to update your time zone automatically.

To change your time zone in Windows:
  1. Open Settings on your Windows device.
  2. Select Time & language > Date & time.
  3. Next to Time zone, choose your time zone from the dropdown menu.
To change your time zone in MacOS:

  1. Open System Settings on your MacOS device.

  2. Select General > Date & Time.

  3. If the Set time zone automatically toggle is on, your time zone will update to reflect the time zone where you’re currently located.

    • To manually change your time zone, turn off the Set time zone automatically toggle. Then, select your Closest city from the dropdown menu to change to that city’s time zone.

      Screenshot: Settings to change your time zone on MacOS

Remember to restart Teams to reflect your updates.

Changing your preferred language and region in Teams also updates your time and date format.

Customize how apps appear

Customize apps in Teams by choosing whether to display labels beneath app icons and if you want to automatically collapse the app bar when you are using Teams.

To show or hide app labels:

  1. Select Settings and moreScreenshot: Teams settings and more icon. > SettingsScreenshot: Settings button in Teams.
  2. Select AppearanceScreenshot: appearance icon .
  3. Turn the Show app names toggle on or off.

To collapse or show apps:

  1. Select Settings and moreScreenshot: Teams settings and more icon. > SettingsScreenshot: Settings button in Teams.
  2. Select AppearanceScreenshot: teams appearance icon .
  3. Turn the Auto collapse app bar toggle on or off to automatically collapse the app bar after you select an app.

Tip

To easily access Appearance settings, Select Expand app bar or press Ctrl+0, or right click on the app bar and select Customize app bar.

Set Teams to start automatically

Teams is set to automatically open and run in the background as soon as you start your device. If you close the app, it keeps running in the background. You can change these settings anytime.

  1. Select your profile picture at the top right of Teams
  2. Select Settings and moreScreenshot: Teams settings and more icon. > SettingsScreenshot: Settings button> General.
  3. From the System section, uncheck the box next to Auto-start Teams. You can also change your settings so the app won’t run in the background or keep running after you close your window.

Turn efficiency mode on or off

The efficiency mode setting in Microsoft Teams is designed to improve performance and reduce resource usage, especially on devices that are under hardware stress or have limited capabilities.

Note that turning this setting on may affect some functionality such as camera resolution.

  1. In Teams, go to Settings and moreScreenshot: Teams settings and more icon. > SettingsScreenshot: Settings button > General.

  2. Scroll down to Efficiency mode.

  3. Choose your preferred setting:

    • Use only when resources are low (Default): Reduce processor and memory usage when reduced resources are detected.
    • Never use efficiency mode: Prioritize a richer experience, using more system resources.
    • Always use efficiency mode: Reduce processor and memory use at all times.

Change your status in Microsoft Teams

  • Desktop
  • Mobile
  • Web

Change your status

If you want to make sure people know when you’re busy or away from your desk, set your status in Teams. The little dot on your profile indicates if you’re available or not.

To change your status, select your profile picture at the top right of Teams. Select your current status to choose another status from the list.

Teams will automatically set the status in some cases, like when you’re on a call.

Screenshot: Status menu

You can also update your status from the search box by typing the following commands:

  • /busy
    • Available: Busy
  • /dnd
    • Available: Do not disturb
  • /brb
    • Available: Be right back
  • /away
    • Available: Away
  • /offline
    • Available: Offline

Tip

Learn more about using commands here: Use commands in Microsoft Teams.

Here are more details about each status:

  • Available is when you’re active in Teams and don’t have anything on your calendar (no meetings or calls, for example). Note that Teams will automatically set your status from Available to Away when you lock your computer or when it enters idle or sleep mode. On mobile, this will happen when the Teams app is in the background.

  • Busy is when you want to focus on something, and you still want to receive notifications. If you’re in a meeting or call, Teams will automatically change your status to In a meeting or In a call (Busy) when not set to Do not disturb.

  • Do not disturb is when you want to focus or present your screen and don’t want to receive notifications.

  • Be right back is when you want to say you’re temporarily away. It’s never set automatically.

  • Appear away is when you need to work without responding right away.

  • Appear offline is when you want to indicate that you’re not signed in to Teams, so won’t be responding until you’re back online. You’ll still receive notifications if anyone messages you.

    Note

    If you’re a MyAnalytics customer, use the MyAnalytics Outlook add-in to book focus time in your calendar. When you’re in your focus time, your Teams status will change to Focusing and all notifications will be silenced until your focus time ends.

Set a duration for your status

When you want to change your status for a specific period of time—for example, to set Do not disturb for an hour of concentrated work—you can set a duration so that Teams will automatically reset your status at the end of the allotted time.

You can set durations for any status except Available. However, a more available status (like Busy) will not override a less available status (like Away) even if its duration is set. To learn more about status priority, see Presence in Teams.

  1. Select your profile picture > current status > DurationScreenshot: Status duration icon .

    Screenshot: Duration on status menu

  2. Under Status, select the status you want to show going forward.

  3. Under Reset status after, select the amount of time you want that status to last.

    Screenshot: Set status and duration

    Or, if none of the suggested time frames work for you, select Custom under Reset status after and enter the date and time.

    Screenshot: Select Custom

  4. Select Done.

At the end of the period you entered, Teams will automatically reset your status based on your activity, your calendar, and the state of your computer.

Undo a status duration

Simply select a new status. Alternatively, you can select your profile picture, select your current status, and then select Reset status.

Turn off Do not disturb while presenting

You can choose whether to go into Do not disturb status automatically while presenting.

Go to Settings and moreScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > SettingsScreenshot: Settings button > PrivacyScreenshot: Privacy settings button > Set my status to Do not disturb when I’m sharing my screen.

Do not disturb is turned on by default, which means that you won’t be interrupted while presenting. Unchecking the box will allow you to keep receiving notifications while screensharing.

See who’s online

If someone is currently available on Teams, you’ll see a green circle with a check mark next to their profile picture.

To see who on a team is online right now, go to the team name and select More optionsScreenshot: More options button > Manage team > Members. Everyone who’s online right now has the green circle with a check mark next to their name.

Change your status

To change your status, tap MenuScreenshot: More button . Then, tap your status to view your options.

Here’s more detail about each kind of status that you change:

  • Available is when you’re active in Teams and don’t have anything in your calendar (no meetings or calls, for example). Teams will automatically set your status from Available to Away when the Teams app is in the background. On desktop and web, this will happen when you lock your computer or when it enters idle or sleep mode.

    Note

    Change your device’s sleep or idle settings to require more time before your status switches from Available to Away.

  • Busy is when you want to focus on something, and you do want notifications to pop up. If you’re in a meeting or call, Teams will automatically change your status to In a meeting or In a call (Busy) when not set to Do not disturb.

  • Do not disturb is when you want to focus or present your screen and don’t want notifications to pop up.

  • Be right back is when you want to say you’re temporarily away. It’s never set automatically.

  • Appear away is when you need to work without responding right away.

  • Appear offline is when you want to indicate that you’re not signed in to Teams, so will not be responding until you’re back online. You’ll still receive notifications if anyone messages you.

Set a duration for your status

When you want to change your status for a specific period of time—for example, to set “Do not disturb” for an hour of concentrated work—you can set a duration so that Teams will automatically reset your status at the end of the allotted time.

  1. Select your profile picture, select your current status, and then select Duration.

    Screenshot: Duration on status menu

  2. Under Status, select the status you want to show going forward. Under Reset status after, select the amount of time you want that status to last.

    Screenshot: Set status and duration

    Or, if none of the suggested time frames work for you, select Custom under Reset status after and enter the date and time manually.

    Screenshot: Select Custom

  3. Select Done.

At the end of the time period you entered, Teams will automatically reset your status based on your activity, your calendar, and the state of your computer.

Undo a status duration

Simply select a new status. Alternatively, you can select your profile picture, select your current status, and then select Reset status.

See who’s online

You’ll see a green circle with a check mark next to the profile picture of people who are online.

To see who on a team is online right now, tap More optionsScreenshot: More options button next to the team name and select View members. Everyone who’s online right now has the green circle with a check mark next to their profile picture.

Change your status

When you use Teams in a web browser, you can control how your status appears to others. To change your status, select your profile picture. Then select your current status to choose another status from the list.

For more information about status options, refer to the desktop tab of this article.

Keep your current status when active outside Teams

Turn this setting on to help prevent your status from switching to “Away” when you’re working in other browser tabs or apps. Your coworkers will see the right status, even if you’re not working in Teams.

  1. In Teams for Web, select SettingsScreenshot: Settings button .
  2. Go to Notifications and Activity > Presence.
  3. Turn on the toggle next to Keep my current status when I’m active outside of Teams on the web.

When you enable this setting, your browser will show a permission prompt asking if Teams can detect your activity in other tabs or apps.

  • Select Allow to grant permission. This lets Teams know when you’re active outside the app so your status stays accurate.
  • If you select Block, Teams won’t detect activity outside the app, and your status may change to “Away” even if you’re working elsewhere.

Get notified when someone’s status changes in Microsoft Teams

If you want to know when someone in Teams is available or offline, add them to your status notifications list. You can do this through a chat or in settings.

Create a status change notification through a chat

  1. Choose ChatScreenshot: Chat on the left side of Teams.

  2. In your chat list, choose a one-on-one chat with the person you want to add to your status notifications list.

  3. Select More optionsScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon and then choose Notify when availableScreenshot: Notify when available icon .

    Screenshot: Screenshot showing how to be notified when someones status changes from a chat.

  4. To stop seeing a person’s status, follow the steps above, and then choose Turn off notificationsScreenshot: Turn off notifications .

Create a status change notification in settings

The settings option allows you to search for someone in your organization and then add them directly to your notifications list.

  1. Select Settings and moreScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > SettingsScreenshot: Settings button > Notifications and activityScreenshot: Activity button to open notification settings.
  2. Under Presence, select Manage notifications.
  3. Type the name of the person you want to be notified about in the Add people search box. Select their name when it appears to add them to your notifications list.
  4. To remove someone from your status notifications list, follow the previous steps and then select the Turn off button next to their name.

Note

You can add up to 15 people to your status notifications list.

Manage accounts and organizations in Microsoft Teams

In Teams, you can add another account, switch between accounts and organizations, and choose which ones can send you notifications.

Add another account

In Teams on desktop, you can sign in to multiple work, school, and personal accounts, or sign in as a guest in other organizations.

  1. Select your profile picture.

  2. Select Add another account and do one of the following:

    1. Choose an account you’ve used before.
    2. Select Create or use another accountScreenshot: Teams add member to chat .

To switch to a different account, select your profile picture and choose a different account at any time.

Screenshot: MTMA new Teams

Manage notifications across accounts and orgs

By default, notifications are turned on for any organization you’ve previously joined as a guest. You can manage which notifications you see from your Teams settings.

All activated accounts and orgs will be visible on your profile.

To manage notifications across multiple accounts and organizations:

  1. Go to Settings and moreScreenshot: more > SettingsScreenshot: settings > Accounts and orgs.
  2. Turn on the toggle next to the org you want to receive notifications from.

Screenshot: a screenshot of multiple accounts logged in

In the ActivityScreenshot: Activity button tab, you can only see missed activity from one active account at a time. To view activity from other accounts, select Activity in your other accounts and orgsScreenshot: person alert icon in the bottom left corner of Teams.

View activity from other accounts and orgs

  1. Select Activity in your other accounts and orgsScreenshot: person alert icon in the bottom left corner of Teams.
  2. Select a notification to open that activity in a new window. You won’t switch accounts in the main Teams window.

Screenshot: Screenshot showing Teams activity across multiple accounts and orgs.

Pin accounts to the sidebar

To pin a particular account or org to the Teams sidebar, select the PinScreenshot: Pin to taskbar icon icon next to the account’s name. Selecting a pinned account shows activity notifications for that account only.

To switch to that account, select the Switch button.

To remove a pinned account, select Unpin next to the account’s name.

Note

Manage location sharing in Microsoft Teams

  • Windows
  • Mac
  • Mobile

In this article

Consent to location sharing on your operating system

Consent to location sharing on the Teams app

Turn on location services on your operating system 

Allow the Teams app to access your location

Add, edit, or reset your emergency location in the Calls app

Consent to location sharing at the operating system level

Several features within Microsoft Teams rely on location sharing to work properly. You have the choice of when and how Teams can use your location data.  

When you first log in to Teams, you’ll be prompted by your operating system to consent to let Teams access your precise location and location history.  

Screenshot: Teams location consent dialog box

If location access is managed by your IT Admin, you can still manually add your physical address for emergency calls via the Teams Calls app.  

Consent to location sharing on the Teams app

When you open Teams, you’ll be prompted to choose how you want the app to use your location.  

Screenshot: Consent location Teams method

  • Choose Allow all to grant Teams full location access for emergency calls and IT Admin insights.
  • Choose Keep emergency only to restrict location usage to emergency calling.

Note

  • It’s strongly recommended to Allow all so that IT admins can continue to troubleshoot and address issues with the network.
  • You will only see this prompt once, even if you turn location on or off.

Depending on the policies set by your admin, you might see a different version of this prompt.

Screenshot: Teams location detection on

On devices managed by the organization, these settings are on by default and only the IT Admin can turn them off. 

You can change your location detection preferences at any time. 

  • Go to Settings and moreScreenshot: Microsoft Teams more options icon > SettingsScreenshot: Settings icon > Privacy > Location.

 Learn more about how your location data is used by visiting Windows location service and privacy.

Turn on or off location services on your operating system

To enable or disable location services, you’ll first need to provide location permissions to Teams within your OS settings.  

  1. Set your Windows location service and privacy settings.

Screenshot: Image showing the Privacy & Security Location screen.

Allow the Teams app to access your location

On Windows 11 Version 24H2 or higher:   

  1. Turn on Location services.
  2. Turn on Let apps access your location.
  3. Turn on Microsoft Teams.

Screenshot: Screencap of the Locations settings window in Windows 11

 

Add, edit, or reset your emergency location in the Calls app

You can check your emergency location below the dial pad in Calls or at the bottom of the calls section in your Teams Settings.  

Note

You can only edit your Emergency Location in Calls. 

On the Teams dial pad, add, confirm, edit, or reset your emergency location. 

  1. Go to Calls on the left side of Teams.
  2. Select Emergency location.
  3. Select Edit.
  4. Update your address.
